al2VWDI7lR.one_liner: Causal decomposition of MLLM task failures via interventions on prerequisite dependencies, instantiated as the CADET diagnostic benchmark.
al2VWDI7lR.problem: End-to-end accuracy on compositional tasks cannot distinguish an intrinsic capability deficit from a cascading error caused by an upstream prerequisite.
al2VWDI7lR.method: Scores each task under unassisted, correct, or incorrect prerequisites (capability metrics NC, IC, RC) and quantifies each prerequisite's necessity and sufficiency with N-Score and S-Score adapted from probabilities of causation. CADET has 10 composite tasks decomposed into 46 unit tasks with over 33,000 human-annotated questions.
al2VWDI7lR.key_idea: Intervene on each task's prerequisite graph (supply correct or incorrect prerequisites) and score necessity and sufficiency with probabilities of causation to separate intrinsic from cascading failure.
al2VWDI7lR.evidence: Diagnosis of frontier MLLMs on CADET across perception, spatial, temporal, and cognitive categories.
al2VWDI7lR.claimed_gains: Supplying correct prerequisites eliminates 54% of errors on cognitive tasks, and supplying the single most important prerequisite captures 84% of the gain from supplying all prerequisites.
al2VWDI7lR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree controlled interventions on prerequisites give a clearer diagnosis than observational error analysis, with well-defined metrics, a carefully built benchmark, and informative findings such as a few critical prerequisites dominating.
al2VWDI7lR.main_concern: Prompt-level interventions do not measure internal capability, prerequisite structures are designer-specified, and the N/S-Score machinery is not shown to add insight beyond simple conditional accuracy.

45k9l8zWbL.one_liner: Compiles LLM or expert natural-language beliefs once into a belief function that multiplies any nonnegative acquisition in Bayesian optimization.
45k9l8zWbL.problem: Expert knowledge for Bayesian optimization often exists only in natural language, while prior-guided BO needs an explicit prior distribution and robustness to misleading information.
45k9l8zWbL.method: HapBO elicits beliefs once from an expert, an LLM, or both, deterministically compiles a structured specification into a reusable belief function pi from X to [0,1], and applies it through a bounded positive multiplier on the acquisition (building on alpha-pi BO), with no LLM calls during optimization.
45k9l8zWbL.key_idea: Deterministically compile a structured natural-language specification into a belief function and apply it as a bounded positive multiplier on the acquisition function.
45k9l8zWbL.evidence: 40 HPOBench tasks, a synthetic suite in 6-15 dimensions, and two real-world applications (cortical neurostimulation and constrained solar design), plus a proof that HapBO preserves the standard simple-regret rate for EI up to a bounded factor even under adversarial beliefs.
45k9l8zWbL.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the results sentence.
45k9l8zWbL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using an LLM to construct BO priors is an interesting and practically relevant idea, with extensive benchmarking, a structured language-to-prior design, and checks on bad priors, LLM choice, and data leakage.
45k9l8zWbL.main_concern: The prior construction is the main contribution but its quality is not studied directly (a Gaussian-only prior language performs strongly), and the EI regret guarantee requires removing acquisition normalization without full justification.

naoqVY2VBP.one_liner: ConsistentSample: a consistent dynamic algorithm for non-monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint with active-set-independent query complexity.
naoqVY2VBP.problem: Existing consistent algorithms for fully dynamic submodular maximization handle only monotone objectives and have expected amortized query complexity with an undesirable linear dependence on the maximum number n of active elements.
naoqVY2VBP.method: ConsistentSample maintains a stable solution under insertions and deletions for a cardinality constraint k, using sampling both to handle non-monotonicity in the style of Feldman and to make deletions cheap (per reviewers).
naoqVY2VBP.key_idea: Use random sampling both to handle non-monotone objectives and to make deletions cheap while keeping the maintained solution nearly unchanged after each update.
naoqVY2VBP.evidence: Theoretical approximation, consistency, and query-complexity bounds, plus MaxCut experiments comparing against less consistent algorithms such as DynamicNM (per reviewers).
naoqVY2VBP.claimed_gains: Achieves a (1/(3+2*sqrt(2)) - epsilon)-approximation with O(log k/epsilon^2) consistency and O(k^2 log^4(k/epsilon) + (k/epsilon^2) log^2(k/epsilon)) expected amortized query complexity.
naoqVY2VBP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical results are significant, giving the first constant-factor approximation with bounded consistency and active-set-independent query complexity for non-monotone dynamic submodular maximization.
naoqVY2VBP.main_concern: Practicality and motivation are weakly supported: experiments are limited to MaxCut with no setting that needs consistency, the algorithm trades solution quality against queries with high powers of k, and the value of consistency is not fully motivated.

hAZxes7EMV.one_liner: Shows hyperparameter tuning, not model size, drives small-scale scaling-law reliability, and builds a methodology for small-scale experiments
hAZxes7EMV.problem: Scaling laws are reported as unreliable at small scales, starting at 4M parameters, leading researchers to conclude that sizable models cannot be avoided.
hAZxes7EMV.method: The paper ablates the basic scaling-law recipe, shows that well-tuned hyperparameters matter most and that small models are highly sensitive to them, analyzes how the hyperparameter loss surface becomes lower dimensional with scale, and proposes a holistic methodology demonstrated on where to place normalization layers.
hAZxes7EMV.key_idea: Scaling laws only emerge on the fully tuned frontier, and hyperparameter sensitivity fades with scale because the hyperparameter loss surface becomes lower dimensional.
hAZxes7EMV.evidence: Extensive hyperparameter studies across model and data scales with held-out larger models (extrapolation tested up to 268M per a reviewer), plus a case study recovering the large-scale pre-normalization result from small-scale experiments.
hAZxes7EMV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives convincing evidence that hyperparameter tuning quality is critical to revealing small-scale scaling regularities, with carefully designed experiments and practical takeaways.
hAZxes7EMV.main_concern: The evidence rests on one Llama-style model family, one dataset and one optimizer setup, and long-range extrapolation remains unreliable, so the claim that small-scale experiments reliably guide large-scale decisions is not fully supported.

onXkWy1rsX.one_liner: Reweights the TD-MPC2 actor loss with an entropy-regularized allocation that caps each sample's normalized weight share.
onXkWy1rsX.problem: In planner-guided MBRL, actor updates evaluate actions poorly covered by replay data, and critic weighting that concentrates on a few samples amplifies value-estimate errors.
onXkWy1rsX.method: CAPI formulates weighting within a finite actor batch as an entropy-regularized allocation problem with an explicit capacity constraint, then uses the resulting allocation to reweight the TD-MPC2 actor objective.
onXkWy1rsX.key_idea: Allocate actor-batch weights by solving an entropy-regularized problem with a per-sample cap on normalized weight share, prioritizing high-scoring actions without letting a few dominate.
onXkWy1rsX.evidence: DeepMind Control Suite and HumanoidBench high-dimensional continuous control, 18 tasks with five seeds per task per a review, with allocation-rule and capacity ablations.
onXkWy1rsX.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review cites average improvements over TD-M(PC)^2 of about 18.6% on DMControl (remainder cut off).
onXkWy1rsX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the allocation view of batch weighting clearly derived and the improvements meaningful across many tasks, supported by allocation-rule and capacity ablations and a carefully delimited ideal-operator theorem.
onXkWy1rsX.main_concern: Related actor-weighting methods (UWAC, ReW-PE-SAC, DCEM, CVaR) are not compared, gains are not cleanly attributed to capacity because weighting also rescales the actor loss, and no analysis shows policy-planner mismatch is reduced.

VvqTP1PmT6.one_liner: Two discrete flows first generate typed fragment-connection interfaces, then jointly pick compatible fragment templates and attachment mappings.
VvqTP1PmT6.problem: Compatible fragment assembly alone does not ensure generated molecules follow the reference distribution, because connection requirements are not modeled separately from fragment identities.
VvqTP1PmT6.method: FIRM's Interface Flow models typed connection requirements with a latent probabilistic circuit, and its Conditional Realization Flow then refines fragment templates and attachment mappings by discrete denoising within the interface-compatible space.
VvqTP1PmT6.key_idea: Factor generation into typed connection interfaces first and fragment realization second, with discrete flows restricting the second stage to interface-compatible fragments.
VvqTP1PmT6.evidence: MOSES and NPGen: conditional-entropy measurements of fragment templates and attachment mappings, generation-order comparisons, and reference feature-distribution matching against fragment-graph baselines.
VvqTP1PmT6.claimed_gains: Conditioning on interfaces cuts empirical conditional entropy of fragment templates by about 61% and attachment mappings by 49.5%, and interface-first generation improves success without structural correction by 3.25 and 2.67 percentage points over mixed-order generation.
VvqTP1PmT6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating interface generation from fragment realization original and supported by improved realization prediction and generation success, with informative figures.
VvqTP1PmT6.main_concern: Coarse-to-fine and fragment-first strategies are not new (JT-VAE, FragFM, MAGNet), and the experiments do not show wide applicability.

oH5aAnTAvR.one_liner: Proves uniform and Gaussian diffusion LLMs sample in steps scaling with dual total correlation, separating them from masked diffusion.
oH5aAnTAvR.problem: How masked, uniform and Gaussian diffusion language models compare in their capacity for parallel generation lacks principled understanding.
oH5aAnTAvR.method: Proves upper bounds on forward passes scaling with dual total correlation for uniform and Gaussian diffusion, and a lower-bound separation on a family of random empirical measures where uniform and Gaussian diffusion need Theta~(sqrt(d)) passes but masked diffusion with certain approximate score oracles needs Omega~(d).
oH5aAnTAvR.key_idea: Parallelism is governed by the width of critical windows rather than by masked diffusion's commitment to tokens, which yields a provable separation among diffusion paradigms.
oH5aAnTAvR.evidence: Purely theoretical results (upper bounds, lower bounds and a separation) with no empirical evaluation.
oH5aAnTAvR.claimed_gains: Uniform and Gaussian diffusion need Theta~(sqrt(d)) forward passes on a family of random empirical measures, while masked diffusion needs Omega~(d) for certain approximate score oracles.
oH5aAnTAvR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, extends query-complexity upper bounds from masked diffusion to uniform and Gaussian diffusion, and gives the first provable separation with a new critical-window explanation.
oH5aAnTAvR.main_concern: The separation is worst-case over adversarial approximate score oracles on an unstructured Boolean-hypercube instance, so practical relevance to real text and diffusion language models is asserted rather than shown.

7nbwrIMUtV.one_liner: Scalable sequential Bayesian quadrature using Hilbert-space Gaussian process approximations of Matern kernels, with nonasymptotic integration-error bounds.
7nbwrIMUtV.problem: Exact sequential Bayesian quadrature becomes increasingly expensive as function evaluations accumulate.
7nbwrIMUtV.method: Represents both the quadrature estimator and an integral-targeted variance-reduction acquisition in a finite Laplacian eigenbasis, adds a geometry-stabilization constraint for quasi-uniform designs, and proves mean-squared integration-error bounds for Sobolev integrands that show how many features preserve full-kernel rates.
7nbwrIMUtV.key_idea: Quadrature and acquisition are computed in a finite Laplacian eigenbasis whose size, lengthscale and regularization follow response-independent sequences, preserving full-kernel integration rates.
7nbwrIMUtV.evidence: Nonasymptotic mean-squared error bounds for noiseless and noisy observations when target smoothness differs from the Matern RKHS smoothness, plus numerical experiments against full-kernel BQ and SSBQ (the abstract is cut off).
7nbwrIMUtV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is strong and detailed, bounding integration error directly with explicit dependence on feature budget, lengthscale and noise, and that the method is practical for an important problem.
7nbwrIMUtV.main_concern: Reviewers question originality (standard weight-space BQ and one-step variance acquisition), fit for an AI venue without an ML application, tensor-product feature growth exponential in dimension, and untuned baselines without error bars.

VqgFgmH3fn.one_liner: Replaces multi-step action denoising in world action models with one calibrated first-step velocity, run in parallel with visual prefilling.
VqgFgmH3fn.problem: Deploying world action models is bottlenecked by iterative action denoising and the sequential execution of visual prefilling and action prediction.
VqgFgmH3fn.method: Observes that action-denoising trajectories are approximately straight, so a lightweight calibrator directly corrects the first-step velocity and bandwidth-constrained action decoding further reduces error. The one-step action then runs in parallel with visual prefilling.
VqgFgmH3fn.key_idea: Because conditioned WAM action trajectories are near-straight, correct the first-step velocity with a small calibrator and a frequency-limited decoder instead of iterating.
VqgFgmH3fn.evidence: RoboTwin and LIBERO on FastWAM, ImageWAM and Kairos backbones, plus real-world deployment on the FastWAM backbone.
VqgFgmH3fn.claimed_gains: About 13.4M trainable parameters with inference speedups of 7.44x, 5.98x and 24.84x on RoboTwin for FastWAM, ImageWAM and Kairos, and a consistent 7.44x speedup in real-world FastWAM deployment while maintaining close success rates.
VqgFgmH3fn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the straight-trajectory observation is insightful and supported, and that the lightweight calibrator is easy to add to existing WAMs with a small performance drop.
VqgFgmH3fn.main_concern: Weak ablation and generality evidence: the calibrator lacks a naive one-step baseline with the same filtering, the frequency cutoff is not analyzed, and the single low-variance-mode assumption may fail for multimodal actions or out-of-distribution inputs.

dCO9l3C571.one_liner: MemAP turns stored agent experience into executable programs that retrieve similar traces, compute return-grounded action values, and enforce admissibility.
dCO9l3C571.problem: Retrieved memories supplied as LLM context stay advisory, since they do not determine action admissibility or candidate values.
dCO9l3C571.method: MemAP exposes memory traces through a programmable symbolic interface so executable programs compare decision contexts, retrieve transferable experience, compute return-grounded action values, and enforce admissibility constraints, using novelty to guide exploration when return support is insufficient. Interaction feedback updates program state while program definitions stay fixed.
dCO9l3C571.key_idea: Execute memory as symbolic programs that gate and score actions from stored returns and admissibility labels, rather than placing retrieved memories in the LLM context.
dCO9l3C571.evidence: WebArena experiments against memory-based baselines with GPT-4o and GPT-5, plus ablations showing that executing the same experience outperforms contextual reuse.
dCO9l3C571.claimed_gains: MemAP achieves 61.9% success on WebArena with GPT-4o, outperforming the evaluated memory-based baselines, and reaches 68.7% with GPT-5.
dCO9l3C571.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between advisory memory and executable decision control is interesting, the framework is interpretable, and results show a clear advantage over context-based memory.
dCO9l3C571.main_concern: Robustness is not shown, since hard gating can suppress valid actions when model-generated returns or admissibility labels are wrong, and comparisons with other neuro-symbolic frameworks and backbones are thin.

ypBUtS8SON.one_liner: Proves two-point Gaussian zeroth-order optimization converges at rates set by a pointwise Hessian trace-norm bound rather than ambient dimension.
ypBUtS8SON.problem: Classical zeroth-order theory scales with ambient dimension, and recent spectral analyses assume a fixed Hessian or a curvature envelope over a neighborhood or the whole space.
ypBUtS8SON.method: They assume the sum of absolute Hessian eigenvalues is bounded by H at every point, prove O(H/T) convergence to first-order stationary points and linear convergence under the PL condition, and construct a Twisted Valley function whose curvature direction sweeps every coordinate.
ypBUtS8SON.key_idea: A pointwise (not envelope) Hessian trace-norm bound suffices for the standard two-point Gaussian estimator, so the rate depends on H instead of the ambient dimension.
ypBUtS8SON.evidence: Theorems for non-convex and PL objectives, the Twisted Valley example, and numerical tests on that function and on forward-only adaptation of a CNN and a Vision Transformer.
ypBUtS8SON.claimed_gains: Rate O(H/T) for general non-convex objectives and linear convergence with contraction factor 1 - Theta(mu/H) under the PL condition.
ypBUtS8SON.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a nontrivial extension of effective-dimension analysis beyond common Hessian envelopes, made concrete by the Twisted Valley construction.
ypBUtS8SON.main_concern: Experiments give limited evidence of practical relevance (a nonrotating control matches, step sizes exceed the theorem's range, head-only adaptation performs similarly), and the contribution is an extension of existing theory.

sgtpPybHlA.one_liner: Runs POD in the output space of an invertible nonlinear map, so all information loss occurs in the POD projection.
sgtpPybHlA.problem: POD needs many modes when data lie near a curved manifold, while nonlinear autoencoders lose information in the encoder and have unordered, non-nested latent coordinates.
sgtpPybHlA.method: OPINE learns an invertible nonlinear change of coordinates and performs POD in the transformed coordinates, training by alternating gradient updates of the map with a damped update of the POD basis, with conditions keeping the basis within a bounded angle of the exact POD subspace.
sgtpPybHlA.key_idea: Make POD the only bottleneck inside an exactly invertible coordinate map, giving ordered, nested modes with all information loss confined to the projection.
sgtpPybHlA.evidence: Synthetic manifolds, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamics, forced Burgers turbulence, 2D Kolmogorov flow and 3D minimal channel flow, compared with POD and nonlinear reduction methods.
sgtpPybHlA.claimed_gains: OPINE is more accurate than POD at every tested retained dimension above one, and on Burgers it is at least as accurate as every compared nonlinear reduction.
sgtpPybHlA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is clean and well written, giving ordered, nested modes and an a-priori error estimate that fluid-mechanics practitioners value.
sgtpPybHlA.main_concern: Baselines and parameter-count comparisons are inadequate (the POD basis is excluded from the count and autoencoders look under-tuned), and benefits for downstream inference on the reduced coordinates are unclear.

5PY8CijJHO.one_liner: UAV orthomosaic dataset with pixel-level labels for illegal Amazon gold mining and four benchmark tasks including zero-shot VLM recognition.
5PY8CijJHO.problem: Satellite imagery misses small mining structures and subtle land-cover transitions under cloud cover, so illegal gold mining is hard to monitor at fine spatial scale.
5PY8CijJHO.method: ELDOR provides manually annotated UAV orthomosaics covering over 2,500 hectares with pixel-level labels for mining activities and surrounding ecological structures, and benchmarks semantic segmentation, segmentation-derived recognition, direct multi-label classification and VLM class-presence recognition.
5PY8CijJHO.key_idea: Derive all four benchmark tasks from one pixel-level annotation source covering both mining activities and surrounding ecological structures.
5PY8CijJHO.evidence: Comparison of generic and remote-sensing segmentation models, vision foundation model-based methods, multi-label classifiers and VLMs under a closed-set protocol, with single-seed runs per reviews.
5PY8CijJHO.claimed_gains: The dataset covers over 2,500 hectares; current methods still struggle with rare small-scale mining structures and fine-grained recovery classes.
5PY8CijJHO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the manually annotated high-resolution dataset fills a real gap for monitoring illegal mining and the benchmarking is extensive.
5PY8CijJHO.main_concern: The experimental protocol is weak: some classes are absent from the test set, geographic splits may leak (two halves of one scene land in different splits), and runs use single seeds without error bars.

n3DF5lNthB.one_liner: Training-free multimodal in-context learning that distills demonstrations into a shared reasoning chain via set-level MCTS and chain-local experiences.
n3DF5lNthB.problem: Few-shot multimodal ICL methods imitate image-question-answer pairs or give demonstration-individual guidance, missing shared task-level reasoning structure and perceptual support for step-wise execution.
n3DF5lNthB.method: ICDs-MCTS collectively expands and evaluates reasoning paths over the whole demonstration set to induce a Normative Reasoning Chain; controlled rollouts along the chain then distill Chain-Local Experiences, including Inter-ICD Pivotal Experiences that capture answer-discriminative visual cues.
n3DF5lNthB.key_idea: Search once over the entire demonstration set with MCTS to get one shared reasoning chain, then attach local perceptual guidance distilled from rollouts at critical nodes.
n3DF5lNthB.evidence: Specialized benchmarks (medical imaging, financial analysis, industrial anomalies and plant pathology per reviews) with ablations, perturbation studies and cross-model transfer of the distilled guidance.
n3DF5lNthB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared task-level chain is an interesting use of the demonstration set and that gains are consistent, with ablations against reasonable alternatives.
n3DF5lNthB.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the method combines existing MCTS, contrastive trajectory analysis and experience summarization, and evaluation covers only specialized benchmarks.

Xzz63gH186.one_liner: Prunes VLA visual tokens by scoring them against action anchors taken from deep FFN value vectors.
Xzz63gH186.problem: Trainable token-pruning criteria for VLA models are action-agnostic, keeping background tokens while discarding fine-grained cues that precise control needs.
Xzz63gH186.method: ActPruner's Action Information Extraction Module extracts compact action anchors from deep FFN value vectors (Deep Prior Extraction), aligns them to shallow pruning layers (Semantic Space Adaptation), and adds a third instruction-related step; reviews say the anchors come from PCA.
Xzz63gH186.key_idea: Deep FFN value vectors define action-relevant residual subspaces whose projection energy approximates local action saliency, which is used to score visual tokens.
Xzz63gH186.evidence: LIBERO, Meta-World and real-robot tasks against baselines including LightVLA and SpecPrune-VLA, with anchor-construction ablations and latency measurements per reviews.
Xzz63gH186.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; reviews report 97.0% LIBERO success at about 4% token retention and a 1.65x per-step speedup, versus 96.5% at 15% retention for LightVLA.
Xzz63gH186.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using action information already encoded inside the VLA is an interesting, task-specific approach with a competitive efficiency-accuracy trade-off and real-robot results.
Xzz63gH186.main_concern: The theory does not identify the PCA subspace with the action subspace, and the independent gain of FFN-PCA over learnable queries or random value vectors is modest (94.6% versus 93.4% and 93.6%).

ikCmxFDkbM.one_liner: Agents shorten Lean proof collections under a kernel proof-term size metric, then mine reusable lemmas, released as a benchmark.
ikCmxFDkbM.problem: Language models can prove hard mathematical statements, but their proofs still need organizing for understanding and reuse.
ikCmxFDkbM.method: They formulate proof compression as a verifiable task of shortening Lean proofs while preserving statements, measured by AST size of proof terms, and use agents plus a lemma-discovery pipeline whose helpers are rated non-trivial by a language model.
ikCmxFDkbM.key_idea: Optimize Lean kernel proof-term AST size under fixed target statements, so compression forces extraction of shared lemmas that can be reused.
ikCmxFDkbM.evidence: Compression of the permanent lower bound proof and the compactness-conjecture counterexamples, plus lemma-discovery trends on Fermat's Last Theorem results and LLM-judged lemma non-triviality.
ikCmxFDkbM.claimed_gains: Agents compress the permanent lower bound proof by 94.2% and the compactness-conjecture counterexample proofs by up to 99.2% under the proof-term size metric.
ikCmxFDkbM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating proof compression with kernel-verified proof-term size is a rigorous, well-motivated objective and that reusable lemma discovery is a promising direction.
ikCmxFDkbM.main_concern: The practical value of the AST-size metric is not established, and claims of meaningful lemma discovery rest mostly on LLM judgments with limited human evaluation.

ny2OH3jQ7q.one_liner: Benchmark of 384 GPU kernel tasks scored at kernel level and end to end inside production inference frameworks.
ny2OH3jQ7q.problem: Existing GPU kernel generation benchmarks evaluate kernels in isolation with synthetic inputs and weak baselines, rewarding sandbox speedups that break or vanish in real inference systems.
ny2OH3jQ7q.method: FastKernels provides 384 tasks from 47 architectures across 8 categories, each mirroring a production module interface and scored against production-shipped kernels, in a compositional hierarchy where higher-level modules import lower-level ones. MacroEval ranks candidates by end-to-end speedup inside the source models, counting a model that does not run correctly as zero.
ny2OH3jQ7q.key_idea: Score generated kernels end to end inside production models on the production execution path, with incorrect models counted as zero, instead of in isolated sandbox speedups.
ny2OH3jQ7q.evidence: Five representative agents were run for 6,900 agent-hours on the benchmark, and the tasks' kernels suffice to reimplement 94.6% (472/499) of HuggingFace Transformers architectures with outputs matching the native implementations.
ny2OH3jQ7q.claimed_gains: Kernel-level speedups of 1.6-6.6x shrink to at most 1.25x end to end, only 20% of winning kernel sets run correctly as-is, and KDA scores 2x higher end to end even though Claude Code matches or beats it at every level in isolation.
ny2OH3jQ7q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the importance of checking generated kernels inside real inference systems and the well-designed compositional L1-L4 hierarchy with production-compatible interfaces.
ny2OH3jQ7q.main_concern: Evaluation validity and robustness are questioned: case sampling is capped at five per operator, the 0.9 correctness threshold may be too permissive, and MacroEval averages only over valid tasks, which may distort rankings.

jfPJxu6soa.one_liner: Sinusoidal INR with coordinate-dependent gain and shift modulation and shared channel mixing, spending parameters on assignment rather than reach
jfPJxu6soa.problem: Existing sinusoidal INRs spend parameters on a separate mixing matrix per layer while applying the same scale and offset at every location, so they do little to control which harmonics are produced where.
jfPJxu6soa.method: SPAN-INR makes sinusoidal INRs spatially adaptive with coordinate-dependent controllers that produce gain and shift for the argument entering each sine, while channel mixing is shared across stages, so parameters go to assignment instead of reach.
jfPJxu6soa.key_idea: By the Jacobi-Anger expansion, per-location gain and shift set harmonic order and odd/even balance, so a shared mixing matrix supplies connectivity while controllers assign harmonics by coordinate.
jfPJxu6soa.evidence: Five reconstruction tasks (especially image fitting) with an analysis of reach versus assignment, including frozen-mixing and diagonal-mixing experiments, ablations, and spectral analyses.
jfPJxu6soa.claimed_gains: Motivating analysis in the abstract: a single dense mixing matrix shared by all stages and frozen at random initialization loses only 0.14 dB against a fully learned one, versus 5.81 dB for a diagonal matrix and 3.48 dB for an independent matrix per stage at the same budget; final SPAN-INR gains are cut off in the batch.
jfPJxu6soa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reach versus assignment framing is clear, the frozen random mixing finding is insightful, and the method gives consistent improvements across reconstruction tasks.
jfPJxu6soa.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty over coordinate-dependent modulation methods (Coordinate-Aware Modulation, INCODE) is not established by direct comparison, ablations are not isolated, and wall-clock training cost is unclear.

jEb5mFuMoP.one_liner: Redefines the edge of stability using the directional Hessian and gradient alignment along the optimizer's actual update.
jEb5mFuMoP.problem: Edge-of-stability formulations based on the maximum Hessian eigenvalue and learning rate are violated by many first-order methods, including gradient descent, by an optimizer-dependent systematic factor.
jEb5mFuMoP.method: The paper derives a realized edge of stability from the directional Hessian and the gradient-alignment score with respect to the update the optimizer actually takes, rather than the maximum curvature mode. Reviews describe a control-theoretic (root-locus, optimizer-filter) analysis, and the paper adds diagnostic tools for the optimizer's temporal and spatial budgets.
jEb5mFuMoP.key_idea: Measure stability along the realized update direction using the directional Hessian and gradient alignment instead of the top Hessian eigenvector, which removes optimizer-dependent offsets.
jEb5mFuMoP.evidence: Systematic experiments across first-order optimizer families, with nonlinear experiments confined to a single architecture and dataset per reviews, plus a quadratic-model analysis with temporal gradient filters.
jEb5mFuMoP.claimed_gains: Many first-order methods, including gradient descent, violate the classical stability bound by a factor as large as 21.1.
jEb5mFuMoP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the systematic comparison across optimizer families is useful and that the paper clearly motivates a limitation of worst-case edge-of-stability formulations with a unified control-theoretic treatment.
jEb5mFuMoP.main_concern: The realized metric is largely diagnostic and may reduce to a one-step descent condition (zeta = 1 + dL/(eta g^T u)) without predicting stability beyond one step, and its novelty relative to the original edge-of-stability findings is unclear.

0PwROOcT6V.one_liner: Convergence analysis of bias-corrected Adam via a magnitude-weighted stochastic sign representation, giving dimension-free T^{-1/4} rates.
0PwROOcT6V.problem: Prior Adam convergence analyses carry explicit dimension factors or extra log T terms, and many drop the standard bias correction.
0PwROOcT6V.method: The analysis writes Adam's update as a magnitude-weighted stochastic sign and controls the accumulated wrong-sign loss while retaining the joint randomness of update magnitude, momentum, and gradient noise. It is then instantiated for fan-in-scaled LayerNorm/RMSNorm networks with fixed depth and growing hidden width, where explicit width-horizon conditions keep iterates in a width-uniform parameter region.
0PwROOcT6V.key_idea: Treat Adam's update as a magnitude-weighted stochastic sign and bound the accumulated wrong-sign loss jointly with magnitude, momentum, and noise randomness, avoiding dimension-dependent constants.
0PwROOcT6V.evidence: Theory under L-smoothness with conditional p-affine second moments and under global point-pair (L_0, L_1, q)-smoothness, plus an explicit width-uniform result for a fixed-affine family of normalized networks; no experiments are stated.
0PwROOcT6V.claimed_gains: Expected average l2 gradient norm at most C T^{-1/4}, where C has no explicit dimension factor and the rate has no extra log T; the same exponent holds with high probability under global point-pair smoothness.
0PwROOcT6V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the proofs are correct and clearly presented, and that handling Adam's correlated update magnitudes and momentum errors under weak assumptions is a meaningful theoretical result.
0PwROOcT6V.main_concern: The dimension-free guarantee needs learning rate and momentum tuned to the horizon and hidden width growing with it, and one reviewer argues the analysis effectively covers momentum SGD with a bounded preconditioner rather than adaptive Adam.

W98s9QNzlX.one_liner: Benchmark of 128 mostly unsolved math problems with deterministic automated verifiers, targeting problems hard to discover but easy to verify.
W98s9QNzlX.problem: Whether AI can make progress on unsolved research mathematics is debated, and existing research-level benchmarks rely on expensive formal proof verification or manual review.
W98s9QNzlX.method: HorizonMath has 128 predominantly unsolved problems across eight domains with an open-source framework that automatically verifies candidate answers, exploiting the generator-verifier gap where discovery is hard but verification is computationally straightforward.
W98s9QNzlX.key_idea: Pick problems whose answers are unknown but checkable by a cheap deterministic program, so progress on unsolved math can be scored without proofs or expert grading.
W98s9QNzlX.evidence: Seven frontier model families evaluated on the benchmark, with analysis of reasoning efficiency and behavior and verification of five novel solutions.
W98s9QNzlX.claimed_gains: Most frontier models score under 10%; five novel solutions that resolve open questions or improve on the best-known results were found, two by GPT-5.4 Pro and three by GPT 5.6 Sol.
W98s9QNzlX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the generator-verifier-gap design yields an open, reproducible benchmark resistant to contamination that has already produced verified new results.
W98s9QNzlX.main_concern: The paper does not test the robustness of its automatic verifiers or explain why this approach is preferable to formal methods, and gives little dataset statistics.

KEEiSAU4Cu.one_liner: Rescales each Soft Thinking embedding to the probability-weighted average norm of its candidate token embeddings, with no training.
KEEiSAU4Cu.problem: Soft Thinking averages candidate token embeddings, which shrinks embedding norm at multi-candidate steps below the typical range of discrete embeddings and creates an input-scale mismatch.
KEEiSAU4Cu.method: NormCaST calibrates each soft embedding to the probability-weighted average norm of its candidate token embeddings, preserving direction and adding no forward passes. It plugs into existing Soft Thinking variants without training.
KEEiSAU4Cu.key_idea: Restore the norm that averaging removes (by Jensen's inequality) by rescaling the soft embedding to the weighted mean norm of its candidate token embeddings.
KEEiSAU4Cu.evidence: Four models from 1.7B to 32B parameters on multiple reasoning benchmarks (AIME, math, and coding sets per reviews), compared with non-calibrated Soft Thinking variants and several norm targets.
KEEiSAU4Cu.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before the figures, and reviewers describe headline gains of about 3 points in average accuracy, mostly from AIME.
KEEiSAU4Cu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the norm-shrinkage diagnosis is clear and the one-line, training-free fix is cheap and easy to adopt.
KEEiSAU4Cu.main_concern: Gains are small, concentrated on AIME, and reported without error bars or significance tests, and the causal role of norm shrinkage rests on correlational evidence.

jsPlJXCatM.one_liner: Primal-dual safe RL for flow policies that propagates endpoint cost sensitivity through flow dynamics to adapt the Lagrange multiplier.
jsPlJXCatM.problem: Flow-policy optimizers update surrogate objectives while safety depends on endpoint actions, so raising the Lagrange multiplier changes the policy substantially yet reduces cost only slightly.
jsPlJXCatM.method: Flow-Lag propagates endpoint cost information through the flow dynamics to measure the safety response of the actual policy update, then uses that response to adapt the multiplier and calibrate the policy update.
jsPlJXCatM.key_idea: Measure how an update changes endpoint cost by differentiating cost through the flow dynamics, and use that response to scale the multiplier and the policy step.
jsPlJXCatM.evidence: Safety-Gymnasium navigation and velocity-constrained Safe MuJoCo benchmarks, with theory on multiplier-update contraction and convergence to active KKT points (per reviews).
jsPlJXCatM.claimed_gains: Improved reward-safety performance over representative baselines on the benchmarks; no numbers stated.
jsPlJXCatM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the surrogate-endpoint mismatch is a relevant, underexplored problem and that the sensitivity-based fix is concrete and backed by theory and experiments.
jsPlJXCatM.main_concern: The signals driving Flow-Lag are not shown to be reliable (the extra action-conditioned cost critic is underspecified), and some baselines use per-step cost constraints, which weakens comparison fairness.

INDoPREy1g.one_liner: TIP splits benchmark similarity into task semantics and interaction realization to explain which source trajectories transfer in agent supervised fine-tuning.
INDoPREy1g.problem: Given a target benchmark, it is unclear how to select source benchmark variants whose teacher trajectories help agent post-training.
INDoPREy1g.method: TIP characterizes benchmark relationships along task semantics (goal, domain, capabilities, success conditions) and interaction realization (information access, action execution, feedback, state management). The authors generate and filter teacher trajectories from two groups of source benchmarks, fine-tune Qwen3 models with trajectory SFT, and test on a target benchmark.
INDoPREy1g.key_idea: Select source benchmarks by proximity in interaction realization rather than task-semantic similarity, since the former predicts positive transfer in trajectory SFT.
INDoPREy1g.evidence: Qwen3 models fine-tuned on two source groups and evaluated on one memory-focused target benchmark, with individual-source experiments and a three-seed supervised-token-matched control.
INDoPREy1g.claimed_gains: Sources aligned in interaction realization give larger gains while sources with high task-semantic similarity induce negative transfer; no numbers stated in the abstract.
INDoPREy1g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is practically relevant and that IR-aligned SFT beats TS-aligned SFT consistently across students and memory interfaces.
INDoPREy1g.main_concern: The comparison uses two pooled source groups on a single target with different sizes and compositions, and TS/IR distances are asserted rather than measured, so the cause of the gap is unresolved.

zMXg4wlWVu.one_liner: Applies SAEs, PCA and random directions with probing, steering and auto-interpretability to voice-cloning TTS models such as Qwen3-TTS.
zMXg4wlWVu.problem: It is unclear which acoustic properties voice-cloning TTS models represent and use.
zMXg4wlWVu.method: They analyze features from sparse autoencoders, PCA and random directions via sparse probing, steering and quantitative auto-interpretability in Qwen3-TTS, and extend probing and steering to five additional models.
zMXg4wlWVu.key_idea: Compare SAE, PCA and random-direction features for probing and steering acoustic concepts, and validate discovered SAE features with an audio-LLM auto-interpretability pipeline.
zMXg4wlWVu.evidence: Qwen3-TTS plus five additional models for probing and steering, with auto-interpretability and human-label checks on Qwen3-TTS only.
zMXg4wlWVu.claimed_gains: Auto-interpretability finds 684 automatically validated SAE features in Qwen3-TTS.
zMXg4wlWVu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the breadth across models and concepts and the quantitative auto-interpretability validation, including reporting of steering failures.
zMXg4wlWVu.main_concern: The claimed SAE advantage is not isolated (random directions and untrained SAEs probe similarly in one setting), and auto-interpretability relies on an LLM judge on a single model.

a0I8jYG8ov.one_liner: Proves a one-layer softmax transformer computes an equality-testing function with p bits of precision but not with p-1 bits.
a0I8jYG8ov.problem: Low-precision weights and arithmetic speed up transformers but may reduce expressive power, and the extent of this loss is poorly understood.
a0I8jYG8ov.method: For every p, the paper exhibits a function Γ that tests equalities, gives an explicit p-bit one-layer softmax transformer construction that computes it, and proves with communication-complexity lower bounds that p-1 bits cannot.
a0I8jYG8ov.key_idea: Combine explicit p-bit transformer constructions with communication-complexity lower bounds on an equality-testing function to obtain a tight one-bit precision threshold.
a0I8jYG8ov.evidence: Theoretical proofs (constructions and communication-complexity lower bounds); no experiments are described.
a0I8jYG8ov.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching upper and lower bounds give a clean, precise one-bit precision threshold for one-layer transformers, a new angle on expressiveness.
a0I8jYG8ov.main_concern: Reviewers say the result has limited generality: it covers a single-layer, single-head setting with specially constructed inputs and one equality function, and the lower bound is a standard communication-complexity reduction.

2iPeaSmBGi.one_liner: Contrastive time-series representation learning that filters unreliable DTW relations and injects reliable warping paths through a lightweight adapter.
2iPeaSmBGi.problem: DTW-based methods use DTW relations directly as supervision and rely on scalar similarities, leaving relation reliability and fine-grained warping-path correspondences underexplored.
2iPeaSmBGi.method: DTW4TS assesses reliability via local neighborhood consistency and alignment path deviation, adds a lightweight DTW Adapter that encodes reliable warping paths into intermediate encoder layers, and uses an elastic contrastive objective with cross-sequence positive pairs from reliable correspondences.
2iPeaSmBGi.key_idea: Select DTW relations by neighborhood consistency and path deviation, then use their warping paths for adapter conditioning and cross-sequence elastic positive pairs.
2iPeaSmBGi.evidence: Classification on 125 UCR and 25 UEA datasets, anomaly detection and forecasting benchmarks, with ablations including raw-DTW and shuffled-path variants.
2iPeaSmBGi.claimed_gains: Highest average classification accuracy, improved anomaly detection and competitive forecasting; no numbers stated.
2iPeaSmBGi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is comprehensive (UCR and UEA classification plus anomaly detection and forecasting) and that using warping-path correspondences beyond scalar DTW distance is a coherent idea.
2iPeaSmBGi.main_concern: Reviewers say the path-deviation reliability measure is a heuristic that may penalize legitimate temporal shifts, and that the presentation makes the central contribution hard to isolate.

qNTM1tmIOT.one_liner: CSQuant replaces intermediate permutations with a cross-block Hadamard transform so adaptive rotations merge, and adds attention-aware Hessian compensation.
qNTM1tmIOT.problem: Aggressive low-bit LLM quantization is hurt by activation outliers, and adaptive rotation methods with intermediate permutations cannot merge rotations and add online computation and data movement.
qNTM1tmIOT.method: Cross-Block Smoothing uses a normalized cross-block Hadamard transform to redistribute outliers across blocks while merging two adaptive rotations into one online transformation, enabling CUDA kernel fusion. LiteBoA applies attention-aware second-order compensation to value projections with head-shared Hessians to cut calibration cost.
qNTM1tmIOT.key_idea: Use a separable cross-block Hadamard transform whose factors commute, so two adaptive rotations fuse into a single online transform and fuse with neighboring CUDA kernels.
qNTM1tmIOT.evidence: Experiments on LLaMA-1/2/3 in W4A4KV4 and weight-only settings including 2-bit weights, plus single-Transformer-block efficiency benchmarks on an RTX 3090 per reviews.
qNTM1tmIOT.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a 2.25x figure (cut off before the quantity it refers to) alongside improved accuracy on LLaMA-1/2/3 at W4A4KV4 and weight-only settings, strongest at 2-bit weights.
qNTM1tmIOT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the commuting-transform design reduces online rotation overhead, with fused CUDA kernels documented in the appendix and extensive results on 7B to 70B LLaMA models.
qNTM1tmIOT.main_concern: The contribution over existing Hadamard and cross-block rotation decompositions (QuaRot, DuQuant, RUQuant) is not sharply distinguished, and evaluation is limited to LLaMA with no end-to-end latency profile.

RJjgy3e1fh.one_liner: Multimodal dynamical model fusing spikes, LFPs and behavior, separating behaviorally relevant from residual neural dynamics via structured staged learning.
RJjgy3e1fh.problem: Latent-variable models that jointly model behavior and neural data largely use a single neural modality, not multiple modalities with distinct statistics and temporal resolutions.
RJjgy3e1fh.method: BREM-NET fuses behavioral signals and multiple neural modalities (LFPs and spike counts) during inference. A structured learning framework learns a low-dimensional behaviorally relevant latent subspace sufficient for decoding and separately models residual neural dynamics.
RJjgy3e1fh.key_idea: Prioritized, staged learning functionally separates behaviorally relevant latent dynamics from residual dynamics, while an additive multimodal encoder fuses neural modalities.
RJjgy3e1fh.evidence: Two independent public multimodal neural datasets spanning multiple behaviors and neural modalities, with baseline comparisons, ablations, and synthetic experiments in the appendix.
RJjgy3e1fh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clearly explained, addresses an important neuroscience problem, and is supported by comparisons to relevant baselines and ablations.
RJjgy3e1fh.main_concern: The method is seen as a fairly straightforward combination of existing methods (DPAD's prioritized learning and MSID's multi-scale fusion), and evaluation covers only two datasets.

TmQ9MTIHEG.one_liner: Two-stage training for browser agents: curriculum SFT on recovery data, then GRPO with prefix-conditioned leave-one-out step-level advantages.
TmQ9MTIHEG.problem: Browser agents must assign credit from a sparse terminal outcome to a few critical steps, but group-relative objectives give every step the same advantage and step-level alternatives need environment resets or recurring observations, which live browsing does not provide.
TmQ9MTIHEG.method: RUIC-SFT introduces recovery data as state-conditioned supervision only after the conditioning state becomes separable. DAO-GRPO then derives variance-reduced step-level advantages from prefix-conditioned leave-one-out baselines within each rollout group, with no environment resets or per-step model calls; the result is the Live-Browser-Agent family (4B, 9B, 27B) plus a verified dataset and a bilingual BrowserBench.
TmQ9MTIHEG.key_idea: Compute step-level advantages from leave-one-out baselines among rollouts in the same group that share the same action-sequence prefix, needing no resets or per-step model calls.
TmQ9MTIHEG.evidence: Three online browser benchmarks (reviews name BrowserBench, WebVoyager, Online-Mind2Web), three general agentic benchmarks, and ablations of SFT data mixture and the GRPO variant.
TmQ9MTIHEG.claimed_gains: The 27B model attains the highest average Pass@1 among open-weight models on three online browser benchmarks (82.3%), on par with Kimi-k3 (which leads on BrowserBench at 74.5% vs. 65.2%); the TL;DR claims frontier performance with 90x fewer parameters.
TmQ9MTIHEG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles practical error recovery and sparse feedback in non-resettable live web settings, that DAO-GRPO suits live environments, and that the recovery dataset and bilingual benchmark are useful with promising results.
TmQ9MTIHEG.main_concern: The same Qwen3.7-Plus judge supplies the RL reward and scores BrowserBench, with single-rollout Pass@1 and no independent evaluator or uncertainty estimates, so gains may partly reflect training against the grader.

Kd9QTd2nBx.one_liner: Augments conditional diffusion imputation with learned temporal and frequency memory modules that guide score estimation under extreme sparsity.
Kd9QTd2nBx.problem: Score-based diffusion imputation degrades under extreme sparsity, where few observations give insufficient context, so outputs look locally plausible but fail to preserve broader temporal structure.
Kd9QTd2nBx.method: TFMemDiff adds a Frequency Memory Module that retrieves recurring global spectral patterns and a Temporal Memory Module that captures localized temporal dependencies. Memories distilled from historical training sequences act as an external structural reference guiding conditional score estimation throughout reverse diffusion.
Kd9QTd2nBx.key_idea: Memory prototypes learned from historical training sequences in both temporal and frequency domains are retrieved per incomplete instance to condition the score network throughout reverse diffusion.
Kd9QTd2nBx.evidence: Experiments on multiple real-world datasets (reviews mention a Stock dataset), with component and backbone ablations, an SSSD evaluation, and 20-step DPM-Solver++ sampling.
Kd9QTd2nBx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of using historical time-frequency memories to supplement sparse observations reasonable and well motivated, with broad empirical coverage and useful ablations.
Kd9QTd2nBx.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the benefit of information stored in historical prototypes from the added conditioning capacity (query encoder, projections, fusion networks).

PGSBQI5zJx.one_liner: Trains one language model end-to-end to sample parallel reasoning traces and aggregate them, using set RL plus standard RL.
PGSBQI5zJx.problem: Post-training optimizes language models only for sequential reasoning within one trace, although test-time scaffolds also use parallel sampling and aggregation of traces.
PGSBQI5zJx.method: The model samples a set of independent chain-of-thought traces in parallel, then generates an aggregation trace conditioned on them; everything is optimized end-to-end against the reward of the final aggregated response. Set RL trains the traces to be collectively useful to the aggregator, and standard RL trains the aggregation.
PGSBQI5zJx.key_idea: Optimize parallel traces for collective usefulness to an aggregator via set-level RL advantages, while training the aggregator with standard RL on the final answer reward.
PGSBQI5zJx.evidence: Reasoning-task experiments compared against GRPO; reviews say all results use Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with LoRA rank 32 on math only.
PGSBQI5zJx.claimed_gains: SPIRAL outperforms GRPO by up to 10.6x scaling efficiency and 13.5% higher performance when all three compute primitives are used (abstract text is cut off after "all three compute").
PGSBQI5zJx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is clean and intuitive, optimizing candidate sets for collective utility, with a gradient that splits naturally into a set-RL term and a standard-RL term.
PGSBQI5zJx.main_concern: No ablation separates set-level credit assignment from aggregation training, so the source of the gains is unclear; evidence is also limited to one model and math reasoning.

bw8Ro9xG1y.one_liner: Trains an episodic-memory retriever for world models from future-aware predictive utility, adaptively weighting time, pose, vision and audio cues.
bw8Ro9xG1y.problem: Fixed recall criteria based on recency, pose overlap or visual similarity are unreliable across environments and queries, so it is unclear which memories and retrieval cues to trust for prediction.
bw8Ro9xG1y.method: Future-Aware Recall (FAR) measures predictive utility during training as the conditional log-likelihood of the realized future given recalled context, approximated by negative diffusion prediction loss, and uses it to train a retriever that stays future-blind at inference. The retriever learns cue-specific relevance and decides per query which cues to trust.
bw8Ro9xG1y.key_idea: Supervise a retriever with the negative diffusion prediction loss of the realized future given recalled memories, and learn per-query weights over time, pose, vision and audio cues.
bw8Ro9xG1y.evidence: Three complementary settings (reviews name LoopNav, SoundSpaces and AI2-THOR-dyn) compared with WorldMem and LongLive-RAG, plus component ablations.
bw8Ro9xG1y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that predictive utility is a sound learning signal for retrieval while keeping inference independent of future observations, with ablations supporting the components.
bw8Ro9xG1y.main_concern: The WorldMem comparison is confounded because FAR retrieves from up to 1,000 memory frames while WorldMem is capped at 200 on LoopNav and SoundSpaces.

JO8va8hZB9.one_liner: Introduces Polaris-Bench, recasting 53 visual reasoning tasks in polar coordinates to test whether MLLMs rely on Cartesian grid layouts.
JO8va8hZB9.problem: MLLMs saturate visual reasoning benchmarks, but orthogonal grid layouts let them transcribe images into textual coordinates and reason in text, so high scores may not reflect visual understanding.
JO8va8hZB9.method: Polaris-Bench reformulates 53 visual reasoning tasks in Polar coordinate space with paired Cartesian counterparts that preserve task semantics, and evaluates 14 MLLMs along with thinking modes and prompting interventions.
JO8va8hZB9.key_idea: Pair each Cartesian-grid task with a Polar-layout equivalent that preserves semantics but breaks orthogonal structure, so coordinate transcription no longer works as a shortcut.
JO8va8hZB9.evidence: Evaluation of 14 MLLMs on 53 paired tasks, with thinking-gain analysis, prompting interventions, other non-orthogonal layouts, and a human baseline.
JO8va8hZB9.claimed_gains: Frontier models scoring 69-83% on Cartesian layouts collapse to 31-39% on Polar equivalents, while humans keep 88.8% accuracy on Polar layouts.
JO8va8hZB9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired design and large accuracy drops convincingly show that MLLM visual reasoning is sensitive to layout and that orthogonal-grid benchmarks may overstate it.
JO8va8hZB9.main_concern: The paper does not separate perceptual difficulty or unfamiliarity from reasoning difficulty, so the drop is not shown to be caused by a textual-coordinate shortcut.

H3dansF6Pq.one_liner: Uses coding agents to solve long-horizon dexterous robot tasks, then expands one solution into diverse trajectories for training a VLA.
H3dansF6Pq.problem: It is unclear whether coding-agent solutions to long-horizon dexterous robotics can supervise general robot policies, since the solutions need substantial iterative interaction and are specialized to individual task instances.
H3dansF6Pq.method: Build EmbodiedSWE-Bench, an agent-native simulation benchmark of contact-rich, deformable, and long-horizon tasks, with supporting tools for agents. EmbodiedSWE-Gen expands a single agent solution into large diverse trajectories to train a VLA, and a pipeline generates diverse verifiable simulation environments for reinforcement learning of coding agents.
H3dansF6Pq.key_idea: Treat coding agents as solvers, teachers, and students: their programmatic solutions are expanded into diverse demonstration trajectories that supervise a VLA.
H3dansF6Pq.evidence: A benchmark of 28 tasks across five embodiments evaluated over six model/harness configurations, plus transfer, VLA-learning, and real-world experiments (per reviews).
H3dansF6Pq.claimed_gains: not stated; per reviews, solved-task counts range from 3 to 23 across configurations, and generalization and half the real-world success rates are around 0.2-0.3.
H3dansF6Pq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad, challenging benchmark and the idea of using coding agents as a source of robot training demonstrations.
H3dansF6Pq.main_concern: Evidence is thin: single runs per model-task pair, generalization and real-world success rates of only about 0.2-0.3 against one baseline, an unvalidated reward-hacking audit, and unclear end-to-end workflow details.

YPnOwLdaEi.one_liner: Learns LLM macrostates from hidden-state trajectories with a BYOL/JEPA-style self-supervised objective for interpretation, prediction, and steering.
YPnOwLdaEi.problem: Understanding LLM computation at a level between individual activation features and full model behavior lacks high-level, dynamically meaningful variables.
YPnOwLdaEi.method: Representational Effective Theory (RET) coarse-grains hidden-state activations into learned macrovariables through a BYOL/JEPA-style self-supervised objective that preserves higher-level structure for prediction and interpretation. The macrostates are then used to trace reasoning trajectories, predict behavior early, and steer generation.
YPnOwLdaEi.key_idea: Train a self-supervised predictor on hidden-state trajectories so coarse-grained macrostates keep temporally consistent higher-level structure, then use them as handles for steering.
YPnOwLdaEi.evidence: Per reviews, comparisons with raw-state, PCA, SAE, and temporal-SAE baselines on controlled scene-boundary experiments, plus early prediction of sycophancy and alignment faking and steering tests, mostly in the NuminaMath domain.
YPnOwLdaEi.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative results only).
YPnOwLdaEi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the macrostate framing conceptually compelling and report that RET gives more coherent trajectories than raw-state, PCA, SAE, and temporal-SAE baselines.
YPnOwLdaEi.main_concern: Interpretability and steering claims rest on qualitative narratives and LLM-generated descriptions, one-step prediction may only reflect temporal smoothness, and evaluation is concentrated in one domain.

SARUJ5MCJF.one_liner: Switches stratified arithmetic sampling back to ordinary sampling once the prefix interval lies inside its slice, avoiding precision exhaustion.
SARUJ5MCJF.problem: Independent sampling wastes a multi-answer budget on repeats, and stratified arithmetic sampling runs out of float64 precision after a median of 44-79 tokens, so later tokens are chosen by rounding error.
SARUJ5MCJF.method: Stratified arithmetic sampling decodes each answer from its own slice of the unit interval, and early release switches an answer to ordinary sampling as soon as its prefix interval lies inside its slice. It composes with top-p, top-k, min-p, and p-less sampling.
SARUJ5MCJF.key_idea: Release each answer to ordinary sampling once its prefix interval is contained in its slice, which provably preserves the joint distribution of infinite-precision stratified arithmetic sampling.
SARUJ5MCJF.evidence: Proofs of exact joint-distribution equivalence and a precision bound, plus experiments across models from 360M to 70B, with TriviaQA pass@8, CoverageQA, and NoveltyBench cited in reviews.
SARUJ5MCJF.claimed_gains: Releases after a median of 6-12 tokens and runs 14% faster than always-on arithmetic sampling; reviews cite TriviaQA pass@8 rising by 1.21 points (34.72 to 35.93).
SARUJ5MCJF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the float64-exhaustion diagnosis is real, the method is simple and needs no training, and the theory shows exact preservation of the joint distribution.
SARUJ5MCJF.main_concern: Gains are modest and confined to tasks where answers diverge early (no detectable gain on math, code, or reasoning benchmarks), and comparison with QuasiMoTTo and other quasi-random methods is insufficient.

ALuByLcgi0.one_liner: Encodes multichannel EEG as structured spectrogram images and fine-tunes a general vision-language model for instruction-conditioned multi-task decoding.
ALuByLcgi0.problem: EEG datasets are small and heterogeneous, and it is unclear how to interface neural signals with foundation models for multi-task learning across datasets.
ALuByLcgi0.method: BraVista encodes multichannel EEG as structured images (an STFT grid, per reviews) and continually post-trains a general-domain VLM with instruction conditioning, without an additional large-scale EEG self-supervised pretraining stage.
ALuByLcgi0.key_idea: Map EEG channels into a window-aligned image grid so an off-the-shelf VLM, post-trained with instructions, handles several EEG tasks without EEG-specific pretraining.
ALuByLcgi0.evidence: Four EEG datasets spanning multiple BCI tasks (abnormality detection, emotion recognition, sleep staging, cognitive workload per reviews), with ablations on the EEG-to-image representation, decoder, and prompt labels.
ALuByLcgi0.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; per reviews, it improves over reported NeuroLM results on three datasets and stays competitive on TUAB.
ALuByLcgi0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it practical that one general-domain VLM handles several EEG tasks without EEG-specific pretraining, with joint training helping small datasets.
ALuByLcgi0.main_concern: The value of language conditioning is not isolated (weak linear-head baseline, collapse without candidate labels in the prompt, almost no gain from 2B to 7B), and the contribution is mainly empirical engineering.

39MvtTbrae.one_liner: Generates part-aware 3D shapes by predicting inter-part boundaries in a sparse Seg-Voxel representation instead of part assignments.
39MvtTbrae.problem: Existing part-aware 3D generation relies on external segmentation, predefined layouts, or extra planning, leaving shape generation and part discovery largely decoupled.
39MvtTbrae.method: Seg-Voxel, a sparse voxel representation built on TRELLIS.2's voxel design, jointly encodes geometry and inter-part boundaries, and a native 3D generative pipeline synthesizes it. Predicted boundaries are refined to ensure geometric separation, then reassigned to adjacent components to recover part assets.
39MvtTbrae.key_idea: Recover parts from local binary separation cues at contact interfaces, generated alongside geometry, rather than from explicit global part assignments.
39MvtTbrae.evidence: Comparison with existing part-aware methods on HY3D-Bench, with average scores over 300 test objects (per reviews).
39MvtTbrae.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract and TL;DR say only that it outperforms existing part-aware methods on HY3D-Bench).
39MvtTbrae.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reformulating part structure as local separation boundaries a useful, simple extension of TRELLIS.2 that avoids explicit part identities and counts and improves part-level scores.
39MvtTbrae.main_concern: Boundary reconstruction quality is not directly evaluated and the post-processing can fail (small parts lost in the boundary band, loops wrongly closed), with metrics reported only as averages over test objects.

s4hEejxe9N.one_liner: Uses a single-layer action expert reading all video-model layers via learned KV fusion to cut world action model latency.
s4hEejxe9N.problem: Many world action models use deep, parameter-heavy action modules that incur high inference latency and may overfit to limited robot demonstrations.
s4hEejxe9N.method: Faster-WAM concentrates capacity in the video world model and adds a lightweight single-layer action expert using three choices: Dock of Transformers with Lite KV-Fusion for access to all video layers, world-model-only conditioning of the action expert, and retracted 1D-RoPE aligning video keys with action queries.
s4hEejxe9N.key_idea: A shallow action expert reads representations from every video layer through learned KV fusion, conditioned only on the world model, with aligned 1D-RoPE positions.
s4hEejxe9N.evidence: LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 without additional embodied pretraining, plus LIBERO-Plus out-of-distribution tests, LTX-Video backbone transfer, and four physical tasks (per reviews).
s4hEejxe9N.claimed_gains: Approximately 3.7x and 1.3x inference speedups over Fast-WAM and pi-0.5 with competitive control on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0; per reviews, 78.3% LIBERO-Plus success versus 51.5% for Fast-WAM.
s4hEejxe9N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how much action-specific computation is needed important, and credit the substantial speedup and strong LIBERO-Plus out-of-distribution results.
s4hEejxe9N.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to action-expert depth, since no depth sweep holds fusion, conditioning, and RoPE fixed and learned fusion is not compared with uniform averaging.

g4Z3tzuDI6.one_liner: Recovers secret covariant transformations from FFN weight compositions to reconstruct private LLM inputs, then proposes a low-rank irreversible defense.
g4Z3tzuDI6.problem: Covariant-transformation schemes for private LLM inference must preserve plaintext computation through gated FFNs and residual connections, and the resulting structural constraints may leak the secret transformations.
g4Z3tzuDI6.method: CrossWeight composes transformed FFN weights to derive an invariant that recovers the secret transformations and then the private inputs. As a defense, an irreversible transformation built from trainable low-rank transformations is combined with an attack-aware objective and teacher-student distillation to preserve utility.
g4Z3tzuDI6.key_idea: Composing transformed FFN weights cancels the secret transformations into an invariant, making recovery a matching problem; the defense breaks that cancellation with non-invertible low-rank transformations.
g4Z3tzuDI6.evidence: The attack is tested across multiple covariant transformation schemes and architectures (Qwen3-1.7B, Llama3-8B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B per reviews), and the defense is evaluated against CrossWeight and existing attacks for its privacy-utility trade-off.
g4Z3tzuDI6.claimed_gains: CrossWeight reaches text-token recovery rates approaching 100%, and the low-rank defense substantially reduces attack effectiveness, with no defense numbers stated.
g4Z3tzuDI6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the structural attack mathematically convincing, with consequential end-to-end prompt leakage.
g4Z3tzuDI6.main_concern: The defense is evaluated only against CrossWeight and not against an adaptive attacker, so it shows reduced attack effectiveness rather than general privacy.

4HiVB5eVlZ.one_liner: Routes pretrained tabular outlier detectors to a dataset-specific early-exit layer using a synthetically pretrained plug-in router.
4HiVB5eVlZ.problem: Pretrained tabular foundation models process every dataset at a fixed depth with inference cost growing with dataset size, and the final layer can be suboptimal for outlier detection because outliers contaminate the in-context samples.
4HiVB5eVlZ.method: The paper studies depth-adaptive early exit for pretrained outlier detection, identifies context pollution (outliers among in-context samples) as the mechanism, and pretrains a post-hoc router to pick a dataset-specific exit layer using query outlier labels as privileged information available only during router training. The base model parameters and prediction head stay unchanged.
4HiVB5eVlZ.key_idea: Exit at an intermediate layer chosen by a router trained on synthetic data with outlier labels as privileged information, avoiding accurate-yet-polluted neighbors retrieved at greater depth.
4HiVB5eVlZ.evidence: Three distinct foundation models on diverse real-world benchmarks, an analysis of context pollution, and router experiments on three large real-world benchmarks.
4HiVB5eVlZ.claimed_gains: Exiting at the optimal intermediate layer improves detection by 4.7-7.3% on average, with gains of 13-21% when context pollution matches the natural outlier rate; the router recovers up to 45% of the oracle gain with up to 1.8x speedup.
4HiVB5eVlZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the counter-intuitive finding that early exit can improve detection well supported empirically, and the post-hoc router practically useful without changing the backbones.
4HiVB5eVlZ.main_concern: The router is trained only on synthetic data and does not consistently capture the extra early-exit opportunities under context pollution (it underperforms full-depth TACTIC in five of nine held-out pollution settings).

sRTZRpmWbI.one_liner: Single algorithm for cooperative multi-armed bandits over graphs with near-optimal individual regret in both stochastic and adversarial regimes.
sRTZRpmWbI.problem: Agents on a connected graph know only their local neighborhood and must keep individual regret small in both stochastic and adversarial regimes, without knowing the regime and with little communication.
sRTZRpmWbI.method: One algorithm with neighbor-to-neighbor information exchange attains the stated individual regret in both regimes, supported by matching worst-graph lower bounds up to logarithmic factors and communication bounds. Reviews mention distributed tests that raise alarms to agents.
sRTZRpmWbI.key_idea: A single algorithm with distributed tests that propagate alarms over the communication graph and a sqrt(K) cooperation scale gives best-of-both-worlds individual regret.
sRTZRpmWbI.evidence: Regret upper bounds in both regimes, matching worst-graph lower bounds up to logarithmic factors, communication bounds, and a polynomial gap between adaptive and oblivious adversaries; the work is theoretical.
sRTZRpmWbI.claimed_gains: Individual regret O~(sqrt(K) + min{sum 1/(V*Delta_i), sqrt(KT/V)}) in the stochastic regime, strictly improving the best known results, and O~(sqrt(KT/V) + K^{1/4} sqrt(T)) in the adaptive adversarial regime, with O(log T) communication rounds per agent in the stochastic regime.
sRTZRpmWbI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combined guarantees strong (sqrt(K) stochastic term, matching lower bounds, adaptive-versus-oblivious gap) and the paper well written with sound analysis.
sRTZRpmWbI.main_concern: The model assumes all agents share the same arm set, the roles of the interacting components are hard to see, and no communication-rounds guarantee is given in the adversarial regime.

cT1RKn40jF.one_liner: Relaxes N:M sparsity with the k-support norm, giving closed-form block projections and joint sparsity-budget allocation for LLM pruning.
cT1RKn40jF.problem: Choosing which N of every M weights to keep is combinatorial, and current methods approximate it with saliency rankings, iterative reconstruction, or nonconvex learnable-mask surrogates.
cT1RKn40jF.method: The convex hull of the N-sparse unit-l2 ball per block is shown to be exactly the k-support norm ball at k = N, whose closed-form proximal operator needs one water level per block, found in a single sorted pass. This turns layerwise pruning into a one-shot convex program with a per-block condition for lossless rounding back to N:M, and the same framework allocates the sparsity budget across matrices.
cT1RKn40jF.key_idea: Use the k-support norm at k = N as the tight per-block convex relaxation of N:M sparsity, with a closed-form water-level proximal operator and certified mask hardening.
cT1RKn40jF.evidence: Models from 1B to 70B compared with Wanda, RIA, SparseGPT, ALPS, MaskPro, and ProxSparse, with shared-refit and latency-matched controls and ablations (per reviews), plus theory on tightness and exact recovery under diagonal curvature.
cT1RKn40jF.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; per reviews, on Llama-3.2-3B KSP improves perplexity over ALPS from 18.20 to 17.93 but takes 2200 versus 1570 seconds.
cT1RKn40jF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified convex framework for N:M selection and budget allocation, the complete theory, and the broad model-size coverage at low cost without backpropagation.
cT1RKn40jF.main_concern: The convex selector contributes least (the largest gains come from refit and allocation), ADMM and MaskLLM baselines are missing, and no real acceleration is measured.

GHdqwWT2Rp.one_liner: Pretrains an EEG encoder to jointly predict future teacher states at micro and macro offsets via a shared transition operator.
GHdqwWT2Rp.problem: EEG foundation models mostly use masked content recovery, which can exploit temporal continuity without predicting subsequent activity, and autoregressive ones do not couple subsecond and multi-second forecasts from the same state.
GHdqwWT2Rp.method: MSDE uses a causal encoder and a shared elapsed-time-conditioned transition operator to jointly predict future teacher states at micro (0.5-1 s) and macro (1, 2 and 4 s) offsets.
GHdqwWT2Rp.key_idea: One elapsed-time-conditioned transition operator predicts teacher states at both subsecond and multi-second horizons from the same encoder state.
GHdqwWT2Rp.evidence: A 5.0M-parameter encoder pretrained on 2,115 hours of EEG and evaluated on 20 OmniEEG-Bench tasks against 16 models, with matched controls (content recovery, single-scale variants) and cross-dataset sleep staging.
GHdqwWT2Rp.claimed_gains: MSDE-10% achieves the second-best average fine-tuning rank across 20 OmniEEG-Bench tasks among 16 evaluated models, behind only MSDE-Full, which also has the best average linear-probing rank among 15 pretrained models; joint supervision beats both single-scale variants on 18 tasks.
GHdqwWT2Rp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-timescale future-prediction motivation sound and note that the objective is tested against matched controls.
GHdqwWT2Rp.main_concern: Novelty over existing multi-timescale and predictive EEG pretraining is limited, strong baselines are missing, and headline claims rest on small test sets (one test subject per split in several datasets) and a single pretraining run.

QhI6TIxfIn.one_liner: Improves time series foundation model forecasts by sampling many perturbed inputs in parallel, with a theory of the diversity-fidelity trade-off.
QhI6TIxfIn.problem: Time series foundation models often fail to follow inference-time scaling laws under standard sampling because it explores the solution space insufficiently.
QhI6TIxfIn.method: Apply tailored time series perturbations to inputs to widen the support of the generative distribution, and analyze the diversity-fidelity trade-off to derive a critical sample threshold above which diversified sampling beats standard sampling. The paper also proposes RobustMSE, a metric for TSFM headroom under a fixed budget.
QhI6TIxfIn.key_idea: Perturb the input series before sampling to expand the forecast distribution's support, trading fidelity for diversity, with a critical sample count where diversified sampling wins.
QhI6TIxfIn.evidence: Experiments across various TSFMs and datasets (per reviews, models from 8M to 1.2B, 9 perturbation types, and 2 aggregators), with a failure analysis and latency report.
QhI6TIxfIn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that proper diversified inference scaling yields substantial performance gains without model parameter updates).
QhI6TIxfIn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the comprehensive empirical sweep and practical guidance on inference-time scaling for TSFMs, including honest reporting of harmful perturbations.
QhI6TIxfIn.main_concern: The theory covers oracle best-of-N selection that uses ground truth, so it does not establish practical aggregation, and RobustMSE comparisons are confounded by pretraining-data leakage and pipeline configuration.

JrD283ECTV.one_liner: Learns a quotient map directly from observed outcomes, giving smooth level-set equivalence classes with local geometry for flow-matching generation.
JrD283ECTV.problem: Group-based equivalence learning defines equivalence classes and quotient geometry through a predefined group action, which excludes task-, context-, or realization-dependent and non-geometric equivalences.
JrD283ECTV.method: Learn a quotient map that assigns shared coordinates to equivalent realizations; in continuous domains its level sets form equivalence classes, and its differential and Riemannian metric give tangent spaces and an orthogonal decomposition. The resulting local quotient geometry is combined with flow matching to generate preferred realizations within a fixed class and to define consistent motion across changing classes.
JrD283ECTV.key_idea: Define equivalence by learned smooth level sets of a quotient map, then use its differential and metric to split directions into within-class and across-class components.
JrD283ECTV.evidence: Experiments on image and language domains for learned equivalence, plus articulated-system experiments on generation and dynamics over the learned quotient geometry.
JrD283ECTV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning equivalence directly from outcomes, rather than from predefined transformations, new and mathematically well formulated, with solid theory and a flow-matching implementation.
JrD283ECTV.main_concern: The central claim of equivalence beyond group actions is weakly tested, since experiments are mostly synthetic with known transformations or controlled settings, with few real-world applications or mainstream-benchmark comparisons.

zRDFNEMWDL.one_liner: Adds a post-hoc Signal Temporal Logic safety layer to existing VLA benchmarks, reporting safety rates and a Violation Severity Index.
zRDFNEMWDL.problem: VLA benchmarks report binary task success, which can hide safety violations such as excessive contact, bystander disturbance, destabilized held objects, or self-contact along the trajectory.
zRDFNEMWDL.method: SafeVLA-Bench encodes task-aware safety requirements as STL invariants with quantitative robustness semantics and applies them post hoc to existing simulator VLA benchmarks without changing tasks or success predicates.
