It reports safety rate, the success-but-unsafe rate (SBU), and the new Violation Severity Index (VSI), a bounded worst-violation depth score.
zRDFNEMWDL.key_idea: Monitor rollouts against STL safety invariants with quantitative robustness, and summarize the deepest violation as a bounded severity score alongside native success.
zRDFNEMWDL.evidence: Twenty-seven policy-benchmark entries on LIBERO and RoboCasa-365, plus a post-training case study and additional hardware validation (per reviews).
zRDFNEMWDL.claimed_gains: The fifteen tabletop policies above 90% mean success still have 18-28% unsafe-episode rates, and 38-56% of successful RoboCasa-365 rollouts violate at least one active safety clause.
zRDFNEMWDL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad, practical post-hoc evaluation that preserves comparability with existing benchmarks and shows that high success does not imply safe execution.
zRDFNEMWDL.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (post-hoc monitoring, STL robustness, and severity scoring appear in prior work such as SafeManip), and the added value of VSI and the physical validity of the safety thresholds are not well demonstrated.

EqmfB0mwUM.one_liner: Evolves LLM-written heuristics with complementary-gain population management and an Analyst that writes feature functions for distributional feedback.
EqmfB0mwUM.problem: LLM-generated heuristics degrade in less-studied combinatorial optimization domains such as airline crew pairing, where scalar-fitness selection and feedback are uninformative in a joint constructive-plus-refinement search space.
EqmfB0mwUM.method: GEAR retains candidates that excel on different instances through complementary-gain population management, and an executable Analyst writes feature functions over evaluated solutions to produce structured, distributional feedback. Constructive and refinement heuristics are evolved jointly.
EqmfB0mwUM.key_idea: Select population members by complementary per-instance gain and replace scalar-fitness feedback with Analyst-written executable feature functions summarizing solution distributions.
EqmfB0mwUM.evidence: Four less-studied and four classic combinatorial optimization domains, with all baselines adapted to the same joint space, three-run variation, and component ablations (per reviews).
EqmfB0mwUM.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest mean test fitness in all eight domains and consistent gains on scale-up generalization in the classic domains, with no numbers stated.
EqmfB0mwUM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GEAR reaches the highest mean test fitness across all eight domains and that the executable Analyst feedback and component ablations show meaningful gains.
EqmfB0mwUM.main_concern: Substantial overlap with EoH-S's complementary population management without a direct comparison, no equal time or token budget comparison, and no direct test of the link to weaker domain priors.

YflE98S0mI.one_liner: Controls per-step KL in flow-matching GRPO via KL-scaled clipping and learning-rate feedback holding mean KL near a target.
YflE98S0mI.problem: In GRPO-based reinforcement learning for flow-matching models, ratio clipping does not directly control the KL divergence of policy updates.
YflE98S0mI.method: An exact Gaussian decomposition of the per-step log-ratio shows the per-step KL sets both its mean and variance. Three layers follow: F-Clip clips the centered log-ratio in KL-scaled coordinates, Z-Clip adapts the clipping range to the batch spread for a target clipping fraction, and K-Hold uses learning-rate feedback to keep floor-corrected mean KL over selected denoising steps near a target.
YflE98S0mI.key_idea: Hold the floor-corrected mean per-step KL near a target through learning-rate feedback, since standardized clipping calibrates clipping frequency but not policy displacement.
YflE98S0mI.evidence: OCR-based text rendering with SD3.5-M and FLUX.2-klein, with four held-out reward models, matched-OCR comparisons, fixed-learning-rate controls, and a second sampler (per reviews).
YflE98S0mI.claimed_gains: K-Hold improves held-out reward-model scores over the baselines while preserving the gain under matched OCR performance, with no numbers stated.
YflE98S0mI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the exact Gaussian log-ratio decomposition a useful explanation of why clipping fails to control displacement, supported by experiments on two backbones with several held-out reward models.
YflE98S0mI.main_concern: The analyzed and implemented KL corrections differ (batch-mean versus per-state), and validation is limited to a single OCR text-rendering task.

8P0tdYX1Fj.one_liner: Scales the query budget with each step's change to estimate quantities along slowly varying sequences, including dynamic traces.
8P0tdYX1Fj.problem: Prior implicit trace estimation fixes the query budget by the worst-case step size, which is inefficient for stable sequences with rare bursts.
8P0tdYX1Fj.method: A framework generalizes reuse of past queries to linear and nonlinear functions on normed vector spaces (matrix powers, spectral densities, Monte Carlo integration, certain boundary value PDEs). An algorithm (AdaDeltaShift per reviews) locally scales the estimation budget with the step size alpha_i, with an extension to unknown step sizes.
8P0tdYX1Fj.key_idea: Allocate each step's query budget in proportion to its local change alpha_i instead of the worst-case maximum, reusing queries from earlier sequence elements.
8P0tdYX1Fj.evidence: Theoretical bounds, with experiments (largely in the appendix per reviews) including Hessian trace estimation and a comparison with DeltaShift.
8P0tdYX1Fj.claimed_gains: Cost O((1/eps^2) * sum_{i=1}^m alpha_i) for a sequence of length m at accuracy eps, improving the earlier (m/eps^2) * max_i alpha_i dependence.
8P0tdYX1Fj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the path-length bound a clear theoretical improvement over worst-case step-size budgets, obtained by a simple modification, with a framework that applies to several estimation problems.
8P0tdYX1Fj.main_concern: Experiments are limited and do not clarify the end-to-end cost of the unknown-step algorithm (whether step sizes are estimated and counted) or isolate which adaptive component drives the gains.

34VlQmtqkM.one_liner: Predicts compressed-LLM accuracy by composing per-block answer-margin statistics into a Gaussian score model, without evaluating each configuration.
34VlQmtqkM.problem: Choosing among compression configurations normally requires constructing and evaluating every candidate, which is expensive.
34VlQmtqkM.method: For each block and compression option, the change in answer margins (score differences between competing answers) is summarized by a scaling coefficient and a residual variance, estimated by compressing one block at a time. These statistics are combined across configurations to parameterize a Gaussian score model, and per-example correct-answer probabilities from the uncompressed model's scores are averaged to predict task accuracy.
34VlQmtqkM.key_idea: Statistics of answer-margin shifts measured one block at a time compose across configurations into a Gaussian model of the compressed model's scores.
34VlQmtqkM.evidence: Exhaustively evaluated MMLU quantization and pruning allocation spaces, K2-Horizon-7B quantization spaces, and GPTQ across five checkpoints from 7B to 65B, with comparisons to additive, multiplicative, covariance-based, and empirical-residual predictors.
34VlQmtqkM.claimed_gains: Prediction MAE of 0.61 to 3.83 pp on exhaustively evaluated MMLU spaces, 1.10 pp mean per-space MAE on five K2-Horizon-7B spaces versus 1.55 and 1.42 pp for additive and multiplicative composition, and GPTQ MAE within 0.67-1.19 pp across five checkpoints from 7B to 65B.
34VlQmtqkM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the margin-based method simple and interpretable, and its evaluation more exhaustive and better separated into fit, selection, and test than typical proxy-correlation studies.
34VlQmtqkM.main_concern: Predictions are compressed and optimistically biased with no confidence intervals, cross-block interactions are not validated, and it is unclear that the method beats a simple additive proxy or that low average error yields good allocation choices.

7jkkiv0av9.one_liner: Compares showing, directing, and enforcing task state for LLM agents on paired long-horizon episodes with exact scoring.
7jkkiv0av9.problem: Agent systems keep task state as prompt text or in an enforcing module and are evaluated as wholes, so it is unknown how much reliability comes from the state being shown, told, or enforced.
7jkkiv0av9.method: Fix task rules, model, and paired episodes and vary how strongly state reaches the agent: a raw transcript, an exact checklist, per-turn directives from a state machine compiled from the brief and advanced only by receipts, or an enforcement gate on that machine that refuses state-violating actions. Scoring uses exact payload matching against dynamic ground truth.
7jkkiv0av9.key_idea: Vary state-coupling strength along a ladder from shown to directed to enforced, so reliability gains can be attributed to each rung.
7jkkiv0av9.evidence: Three models, two reasoning regimes, and two domains with paired episodes, plus the same gate applied to a compile of tau^2-bench's airline policy.
7jkkiv0av9.claimed_gains: not stated (the findings are qualitative: shown state is unreliable, directives help in proportion to obedience, and enforcement is bounded by state correctness and request matching).
7jkkiv0av9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question clear and practical and the controlled four-tier comparison, with verifiable receipts, paired episodes, and negative results, a solid empirical design.
7jkkiv0av9.main_concern: The tiers confound state accuracy and request matching with coupling strength, the main experiments use synthetic projects and the authors' own configurations, and the closest related methods are not compared directly.

mt6TZjyRHa.one_liner: Post-trains multi-agent systems with on-policy distillation using role-advantage signals and privileged conflict attribution given only to the teacher.
mt6TZjyRHa.problem: RL post-training of multi-agent systems gets a team-level reward that does not say which agent's step caused the outcome, local rewards need per-task redesign, and on-policy distillation is underexplored for interdependent agents.
mt6TZjyRHa.method: MAS-OPD combines Role-Advantage Specialization, which defines role advantage as the difference between teacher signals under target and non-target role conditions, with Privileged Attribution for Coordination, which attributes an interaction conflict to its source and supplies it to the teacher alone as privileged information.
mt6TZjyRHa.key_idea: Distill token-level teacher signals on student-sampled trajectories, with role advantage from contrasting role conditions and conflict attribution visible only to the teacher.
mt6TZjyRHa.evidence: Code and mathematics benchmarks (six benchmarks with five independent training runs for the main results per reviews), compared with prompt-only and RL baselines, with component ablations.
mt6TZjyRHa.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract and TL;DR say only that it consistently outperforms prompt-only and RL baselines).
mt6TZjyRHa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework a straightforward, targeted way to give dense teacher supervision for role specialization and coordination, with consistent improvements and component ablations over six benchmarks.
mt6TZjyRHa.main_concern: Missing ordinary role-conditioned multi-agent OPD and single-agent OPD baselines leave the contribution unquantified, generalization beyond two agent roles is unclear, and role advantage may reflect prompt sensitivity.

5O06exJifK.one_liner: Zero-shot causal discovery model pretrained on synthetic SCM datasets, with invariance losses, test-time optimization, and feature-semantics post-processing.
5O06exJifK.problem: Classical causal discovery relies on restrictive assumptions and large datasets, and classical and existing zero-shot approaches do not exploit feature semantics.
5O06exJifK.method: ALICE is a foundation model trained entirely on synthetic datasets from diverse structural causal models that maps observational data to a full directed graph in one forward pass. Augmentations and consistency losses enforce realization, permutation, and scale invariances, which enable test-time optimization, and feature semantics are added as post-processing.
5O06exJifK.key_idea: Amortize causal graph estimation in a network trained on diverse synthetic SCMs, enforcing graph invariances that also enable test-time optimization over transformed views.
5O06exJifK.evidence: Synthetic data, physical systems, and real-world datasets (best reported AUROC on four real-world datasets in Table 1 per reviews), with analyses of consistency, identifiability, graph width, and inference cost.
5O06exJifK.claimed_gains: Test-time optimization improves F1 by up to 14%, and feature semantics as post-processing yield up to 15% improvement over ALICE on real-world causal estimation tasks.
5O06exJifK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find amortized zero-shot causal discovery from synthetic training a practically relevant direction, with diverse evaluation and competitive real-world results.
5O06exJifK.main_concern: Generalization from simulated to real data is not argued rigorously, the case for enforcing invariances on imperfect predictions and the causal justification of subgraph voting are unclear, and some terms are left undefined.

6LK4new7Pi.one_liner: Benchmark, streaming model, and memory harness for proactive video agents that infer implicit and evolving user intents.
6LK4new7Pi.problem: Proactive video models rely on explicit requests, miss implicit user intents, and fail to update state as user requests change.
6LK4new7Pi.method: StreamMind-Bench provides 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K task-oriented training examples across explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. StreamMind-VL infers implicit intents from continuous observations and tailors interactions as they evolve, and StreamMind-Harness keeps intents as persistent states with flexible lifecycles via hierarchical memory.
6LK4new7Pi.key_idea: Maintain user intents as persistent states in hierarchical memory while a streaming VLM, trained with adaptive weighting and localized trajectory RL (per reviews), decides when and how to respond.
6LK4new7Pi.evidence: Experiments on StreamMind-Bench across physical and digital environments with pointwise and trajectory-level evaluation, against baselines such as Gemini-3.1-Pro (per reviews), plus general video understanding.
6LK4new7Pi.claimed_gains: StreamMind-VL preserves strong general video understanding while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over other baselines.
6LK4new7Pi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of implicit and evolving intents well motivated and the benchmark comprehensive, covering diverse intent types and environments.
6LK4new7Pi.main_concern: Reported results look inconsistent (Explicit and Implicit values swapped or mismatched between Tables 2 and 3), training-strategy ablations and a real-user study are missing, and the dataset's implicit requests can be fairly explicit.

CUaY4R3h7C.one_liner: Shows spot-check debate fails against a debater who claims only true values unless the honest side claims a discriminating value.
CUaY4R3h7C.problem: Spot-check debate assumes a false answer must rest on a checkable false claim, but a dishonest debater claiming only values shared by the true and false computations passes every check.
CUaY4R3h7C.method: Build a testbed of 600-step arithmetic programs that an oracle verifies step by step but the judge cannot execute, with one LLM in all roles, recording for each debate whether the honest side held, claimed, and had checked a discriminating value (a covered debate).
CUaY4R3h7C.key_idea: Use an attacker claiming only shared true values as a measuring instrument: no check contradicts it, so checks help only when the honest debater claims a discriminating value.
CUaY4R3h7C.evidence: A testbed of 600-step arithmetic programs with one LLM in all roles and open-weight honest debaters, under full-trace and thinned-trace conditions.
CUaY4R3h7C.claimed_gains: With the full true trace one check suffices (accuracy 0.98), while with a thinned trace open-weight honest debaters claim a discriminating value in only a third to half of the debates in which they hold one.
CUaY4R3h7C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the point that a judge cannot catch a true-claims-only liar without a checked discriminating value clear, with careful, rigorous experiments and clearly stated limitations (one review has no text).
CUaY4R3h7C.main_concern: The setting is narrow (one synthetic arithmetic task family, one main model, an author-constructed attacker) and the paper is dense and relies on an unpublished domain paper.

rlreaX2A0a.one_liner: Benchmark of 56 simulated company workdays testing whether agents can carry out organizational work with business systems and colleagues unsupervised.
rlreaX2A0a.problem: Existing agent benchmarks give limited evidence that agents can reliably fulfill organizational responsibilities that combine inferring obligations, reprioritizing work, and coordinating with colleagues under time constraints.
rlreaX2A0a.method: ORGWorld has 56 simulated company environments, each a full workday built around nine business systems, a company handbook, and 15 simulated colleagues, with routine duties plus a cross-department project whose subtasks only colleagues can complete. Programmatic verification checks business outcomes, prohibited actions, and temporal constraints, and a workday is solved only if all responsibilities are completed with no prohibited action.
rlreaX2A0a.key_idea: Score whole simulated workdays as pass/fail using programmatic checks of outcomes, ordering, deadlines, and prohibited actions, with coordination required through scripted colleagues.
rlreaX2A0a.evidence: 12 frontier models on 56 environments reviewed by experts for solvability, plus isolated versus concurrent track ablations for two models (per reviews).
rlreaX2A0a.claimed_gains: Benchmark result rather than a method gain: the strongest of 12 frontier models solves just 48.2% of workdays, while no other model exceeds 20%.
rlreaX2A0a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark realistic and well quality-controlled, combining long-horizon multi-system work, changing priorities, colleague coordination, and programmatic checks of outcomes and prohibited actions.
rlreaX2A0a.main_concern: Representativeness and validation are unclear (how task types and policies were chosen, scripted coworker responses), and the comparison with existing benchmarks is not rigorous enough to support the novelty claims.

8e5bsuFZfb.one_liner: Designs one enzyme sequence for multiple catalytic states by alternating motif-conditioned structure prediction with shared sequence updates.
8e5bsuFZfb.problem: Enzyme catalysis is multistate, but most computational design methods optimize proteins around a single catalytic geometry.
8e5bsuFZfb.method: Multistate Gibbs Sampling (MuGS) alternates motif-conditioned structure prediction for each state with a shared sequence update (tied LigandMPNN averaging per-state amino acid probabilities, per reviews). It extends single-state Gibbs sampling to multiple states and introduces MAME, a curated benchmark of experimentally characterized enzymes.
8e5bsuFZfb.key_idea: Gibbs-style alternation between per-state structure prediction conditioned on catalytic motifs and one sequence update shared across all states.
8e5bsuFZfb.evidence: The single-state AME benchmark compared with RFD2, the MAME benchmark of five motif sets, and a five-state serine hydrolase catalytic cycle, evaluated mainly by motif RMSD (per reviews).
8e5bsuFZfb.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says MuGS refines and rescues existing designs and can generate multistate compatible sequences unseeded; per reviews, single-state sampling saves over 1000 failed RFD2 designs).
8e5bsuFZfb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explicitly multistate Gibbs sampling framework intuitive and aimed at a real limitation, with consistent gains over RFdiffusion2 on AME and MAME.
8e5bsuFZfb.main_concern: Utility is weakly shown: evaluation relies on motif RMSD rather than catalytic activity, the benchmark is small (five motif sets, one serine hydrolase system), and averaging per-state probabilities does not enforce agreement across states.

xakjdUSQA4.one_liner: Decodes text lines in parallel on a 2D lattice, committing confident tokens and deferring unready ones until dependencies are computed.
xakjdUSQA4.problem: Line-parallel models such as LCLM use a fixed commitment schedule that cannot hold back a line whose prerequisites are uncomputed, causing premature commitments and cascading reasoning errors.
xakjdUSQA4.method: LatLM places text on a 2D lattice where eligible frontier tokens are scored each round and a policy commits confident candidates while deferring unready ones. One forward pass supervises entire sampled trajectories via 2D causal masking, and an append-only cache retains exact states.
xakjdUSQA4.key_idea: Make the commitment schedule an adaptive decoding-time choice: score frontier tokens each round, commit confident ones, and defer the rest, with one set of weights supporting several schedules.
xakjdUSQA4.evidence: A 482M-parameter model compared with a data- and capacity-matched autoregressive model and with LCLM on held-out text, independent-line tasks, and mixed dependency chains.
xakjdUSQA4.claimed_gains: Near-autoregressive accuracy on independent-line tasks using 25-43% as many decoding rounds, and 96.5% accuracy versus LCLM's 78.5% on mixed dependency chains.
xakjdUSQA4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the deferred-commitment idea well motivated and the lattice architecture coherent, with careful ablations that share one set of weights.
xakjdUSQA4.main_concern: Practical benefit is not established: results come from synthetic, templated tasks with task-specific fine-tuning at a single 482M scale, and timing is measured separately from accuracy, so end-to-end speedup at matched quality is unshown.

r3ikMLV1ZD.one_liner: Adapts an audio language model into a Music Reasoner and learns shared music-text embeddings for full-song retrieval.
r3ikMLV1ZD.problem: Existing music retrieval methods align short clips well but struggle to preserve full-song detail, understand complex queries, and obtain high-quality supervision.
r3ikMLV1ZD.method: MUUNE combines music-text data construction (audio language models and MIR tools produce multi-view retrieval text and atomic counterfactual evaluation), music knowledge adaptation of a pretrained audio language model into a Music Reasoner, and unified representation learning for inputs up to 300 seconds. The MUUNE-EH variant uses an independent embedding head with Music-Meta-of-Thought (MMOT).
r3ikMLV1ZD.key_idea: Adapt an MLLM with music knowledge first, then learn shared song-text embeddings through an independent embedding head over the whole song in one language-model sequence.
r3ikMLV1ZD.evidence: Seven primary retrieval tasks plus atomic counterfactual evaluation against baselines including CLaMP3 and MuQ-MuLan adapted with the same contrastive data, with controlled ablations; training uses about 2.3 million songs (per reviews).
r3ikMLV1ZD.claimed_gains: MUUNE-EH with MMOT exceeds all compared baselines on all seven primary retrieval tasks, reaching 44.48% mean R@10 and 93.93% mean counterfactual accuracy, exceeding CLaMP3 by 23.30 and 15.37 percentage points and MuQ-MuLan adapted with the same contrastive data by 16.09 and 7.70.
r3ikMLV1ZD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the data construction pipeline with multi-view queries and atomic counterfactuals, the music knowledge adaptation, and the detailed experiments.
r3ikMLV1ZD.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed: MMOT adds little (about 0.14% on the embedding head), gains from 120 s to 300 s inputs are small, and training data scale and source differ from the public baselines.

hETa2TB1RH.one_liner: Proves GRPO is biased for pairwise CRPS rewards, shrinking forecast dispersion, and corrects it with a two-line fix.
hETa2TB1RH.problem: RL post-training and test-time-compute recipes from language models assume single-answer verifiers, but probabilistic forecasting is graded by a proper scoring rule over a whole distribution.
hETa2TB1RH.method: Decompose excess CRPS into Monte-Carlo, optimisation, and information gaps, derive the per-sample pairwise reward under which policy gradient is unbiased for CRPS, and analyze GRPO under it: the group-mean baseline lowers the effective dispersion coefficient from 1/2 to (G-2)/(2(G-1)), and per-group standard-deviation scaling adds more shrinkage. A two-line correction removes the bias.
hETa2TB1RH.key_idea: GRPO's group-relative baseline and standard-deviation scaling bias pairwise CRPS rewards toward under-dispersion, so correcting the advantage estimator restores calibration.
hETa2TB1RH.evidence: Two model families and three model sizes (Chronos-T5-small cited), a GIFT-Eval comparison with an SFT control trained on the same data, synthetic examples with known conditional laws, and self-backtest verifiers for test-time compute.
hETa2TB1RH.claimed_gains: Uncorrected runs are under-dispersed (coverage 0.63 to 0.55 for Chronos-T5-small), a two-line correction removes this, and corrected RL then matches an SFT control with no significant short-term GIFT-Eval gain for either.
hETa2TB1RH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question clear, the GRPO bias diagnosis well supported by controlled experiments across model sizes and families, and the strict SFT comparison valuable.
hETa2TB1RH.main_concern: Test-time-compute conclusions are broader than the study supports (only weak self-backtest verifiers), the theoretical step resembles known leave-one-out baseline ideas, and the practical value of corrected RL over SFT is not shown.

TPSGXw1H8A.one_liner: GPU kernels for attention JVPs and backward-over-backward that cut matmuls from eighteen to fifteen and use Hopper and Blackwell-specific schedules.
TPSGXw1H8A.problem: FlashAttention optimizes attention evaluation and first-order reverse-mode differentiation, while attention JVPs and second-order derivatives, needed for consistency models and learning through gradient updates, lack equally optimized kernels.
TPSGXw1H8A.method: Building on FlashAttention-3/-4, FlashBoB-2 reformulates the backward-over-backward (BoB) computation to cut exact BoB matrix multiplies from eighteen to fifteen without storing N x N intermediates, with on-chip memory independent of sequence length. On Hopper, separate warpgroups build intermediates and accumulate outputs; on Blackwell, it reuses Tensor Memory after the last read and keeps intermediates in shared memory.
TPSGXw1H8A.key_idea: Rewrite the BoB computation so a row statistic comes from an already computed output, removing redundant matmuls, and schedule warpgroups or Tensor Memory per GPU generation.
TPSGXw1H8A.evidence: Causal BF16 benchmarks with head dimension 128 on H100 and B200 against FlashBoB, and non-causal JVP benchmarks from 1K to 128K sequence length against two baselines.
TPSGXw1H8A.claimed_gains: BoB speedups of 2.7-3.0x on H100 and 3.6-4.2x on B200 over FlashBoB, and non-causal JVP speedups of 1.78-5.44x on H100 and 3.16-7.34x on B200.
TPSGXw1H8A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the computation rewrite and hardware-specific schedules a concrete, carefully engineered contribution with solid speedups.
TPSGXw1H8A.main_concern: Most of the speedup comes from engineering (Triton versus CuTe DSL) rather than the reformulation, which gives only 1.11-1.17x on H100 and 1.04-1.07x on B200 in Triton, and numerical error in sharp-attention cases is unvalidated.

RGI3iyJOsE.one_liner: Compares RL and SFT domain teachers for on-policy distillation merging, finding RL teachers give stronger students with smaller parameter displacement.
RGI3iyJOsE.problem: Research on OPD-based model merging focuses on the merging process, while the algorithms used to train the domain experts have received little systematic comparison.
RGI3iyJOsE.method: Controlled single-teacher comparisons of SFT and RL teachers across agentic, reasoning, and perception domains, with teachers and students sharing one Qwen3.5-9B initialization and teachers matched at similar task performance, then extended to multi-teacher OPD (MOPD). Analysis covers parameter displacement and teacher-student Top-K overlap.
RGI3iyJOsE.key_idea: At matched task performance, RL teachers move less in parameter space from the shared initialization than SFT teachers, and this coincides with better transfer to the student under OPD.
RGI3iyJOsE.evidence: Controlled single-teacher comparisons across agentic, reasoning, and perception domains and a multi-teacher OPD experiment, all from a shared Qwen3.5-9B initialization.
RGI3iyJOsE.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative only: RL teachers yield stronger students and higher teacher-gain recovery in all three domains, and a higher three-domain mean in MOPD).
RGI3iyJOsE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question practically relevant and the design well controlled, with shared initialization, matched teachers, and fixed OPD settings.
RGI3iyJOsE.main_concern: The SFT-versus-RL comparison is confounded (external off-policy targets versus on-policy samples, different learning rates and KL penalties), so the effect may not come from RL itself, and single-teacher results may not carry over to multi-teacher merging.

fPHxboFEwZ.one_liner: DNLM fuses retrieval sources without labels by combining Plackett-Luce reliability with pairwise association estimates from anchor-relative score deviations.
fPHxboFEwZ.problem: Agreement among retrieval sources may reflect shared errors rather than stronger evidence, and equal-weight fusion cannot tell the two apart.
fPHxboFEwZ.method: The Deliberative Noisy Label Model (DNLM) learns source reliability with a Plackett-Luce model and estimates pairwise source associations from score deviations relative to pair-excluded anchors. Fusion weights are determined from both.
fPHxboFEwZ.key_idea: Estimate source-pair association from score deviations against anchors that exclude the pair, and combine it with Plackett-Luce reliability to downweight correlated errors.
fPHxboFEwZ.evidence: Four scientific and biomedical benchmarks (five settings) against fixed-rule and correlation-weighted fusion, individual sources, and weak-supervision baselines, plus controlled analyses of shared irrelevant agreement.
fPHxboFEwZ.claimed_gains: Raising agreement on irrelevant candidates drops equal-weight fusion NDCG@10 from 0.39 to 0.17, while DNLM has the highest NDCG@10 in four of five settings and the highest MRR in four of five.
fPHxboFEwZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that correlated errors undermining fusion is an important, intuitively motivated problem, and credit the multiple benchmarks, controlled experiments and component ablations.
fPHxboFEwZ.main_concern: There is no theoretical analysis of whether the pair-excluded anchor biases the estimated correlations, and support rests on four benchmarks without a complexity discussion.

TUwwyMGCu6.one_liner: A unified video DiT for monocular portrait reshooting and animation, using FLAME renderings as camera representation and gradient-reversal expression latents.
TUwwyMGCu6.problem: Portrait animation is usually restricted to a fixed viewpoint, while reshooting relies on limited multi-view data with little identity diversity, and the two are treated as separate problems.
TUwwyMGCu6.method: One video DiT uses FLAME-based renderings as a unified camera representation for multi-view generation, adds point-cloud renderings for reshooting consistency, and uses a high-capacity expression latent for animation. The generated multi-view videos can be reconstructed into a 4DGS representation for real-time free-viewpoint rendering.
TUwwyMGCu6.key_idea: Condition one video DiT on FLAME renderings as a shared camera signal, and train the expression latent adversarially with gradient reversal to reduce driver-identity predictability.
TUwwyMGCu6.evidence: Experiments on cross-identity animation and multi-view reshooting; datasets and baselines are not named in the abstract, and reviewers cite supplementary demos and a Table 3(b) ablation.
TUwwyMGCu6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified framework is simple and well motivated, with point-cloud plus FLAME conditioning and gradient-reversal expression encoding judged effective and the demos stable.
TUwwyMGCu6.main_concern: Several baselines are missing (e.g., 4DAnyone, LivePortrait, DeX-Portrait), and the unified training is under-specified and not validated in the animation-to-reshooting direction.

8YlT0AchRV.one_liner: Q-REACT distills sparse reranker rewards into query-dependent low-rank residuals on frozen embeddings for test-time visual document retrieval.
8YlT0AchRV.problem: Improving retrieval over a fixed visual-document index normally needs training or encoder access, and reranker gains stay local to reordering a small candidate set.
8YlT0AchRV.method: A test-time optimization method combines query-dependent low-rank residual adaptation with document-context scoring while encoders and page index stay fixed. It distills local reranker preferences with cross-entropy against a student distribution normalized over the full task-specific index, so unscored pages compete via cached embeddings without extra reward calls.
8YlT0AchRV.key_idea: Distill reranker preferences into a low-rank query residual using a softmax over the entire cached index, so unscored pages act as competitors without extra reward calls.
8YlT0AchRV.evidence: Eight ViDoRe V3 tasks and five open-weight and proprietary backbones, compared with direct reranking and TTT-Embed at sparse and full-coverage feedback budgets.
8YlT0AchRV.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports higher average retrieval quality than direct reranking and TTT-Embed, without numbers).
8YlT0AchRV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical for frozen or proprietary encoders without index rebuilds, and that results across tasks and backbones with detailed ablations are strong.
8YlT0AchRV.main_concern: The novelty is incremental: it combines existing ideas (low-rank residual adaptation, document-context scoring, reranker distillation) and is close to prior query-conditioned transformation work such as QuARI and CAST.

GsYOcSVD9b.one_liner: SuperMem is a two-level hypergraph memory for LLM agents, with hyperedges binding each unit's text and native media embeddings.
GsYOcSVD9b.problem: Hypergraph agent memories index only text while all-modal memories stay flat or pairwise, causing modality collapse in storage, a modality gap in recall, and repetition and revision problems in update.
GsYOcSVD9b.method: Each unit's text and native media are bound in one first-level hyperedge, and units are nested into second-level episode hyperedges, with no extra LLM call. Recall credits each modality only above its own per-query median and returns whole units with raw media, and consolidation merges repeats and supersedes revisions without deleting any unit.
GsYOcSVD9b.key_idea: Nest units in two hyperedge levels (unit, episode) and score cross-modal recall by crediting each modality only above its own per-query median.
GsYOcSVD9b.evidence: Nine text, multimodal and omni-modal benchmarks against 13 memory baselines on three frozen backbones, with ablation, efficiency and robustness analyses noted by reviewers.
GsYOcSVD9b.claimed_gains: Best average against 13 memory baselines on each of three frozen backbones, with a mean margin of 9.5 points over the strongest.
GsYOcSVD9b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hypergraph structure suits grouped multimodal data and that the method performs strongly across benchmarks and backbones without extra LLM calls.
GsYOcSVD9b.main_concern: The super-hypergraph is not justified against a conventional hierarchical graph memory, and the second-level hyperedges are not evaluated independently.

5okwaPNsME.one_liner: AdaRoll allocates GRPO rollouts per prompt using a predictor of degeneracy built from pilot-rollout entropy and reward.
5okwaPNsME.problem: GRPO gives every prompt the same number of rollouts, wasting compute on degenerated prompts whose sampled responses all receive identical rewards and so give no policy gradient.
5okwaPNsME.method: In the first epoch, one pilot rollout per prompt, with its entropy and reward, predicts prompt degeneracy and the distribution of future correct and incorrect rollouts. Extra rollouts are then allocated over multiple rounds by a cost-benefit tradeoff between predicted learning value and generation cost, and the predictor adapts in later epochs without pilot rollouts.
5okwaPNsME.key_idea: Predict prompt degeneracy from one rollout's entropy and reward with a Beta-Binomial model, then add rollouts progressively where predicted value exceeds generation cost.
5okwaPNsME.evidence: Mathematical reasoning tasks across model scales; reviewers describe two Qwen2.5-Math sizes and six math benchmarks, compared with baselines such as GRESO and VIGOR.
5okwaPNsME.claimed_gains: 26% less rollouts to obtain predictions 22% more accurate than the baselines, with a 1.5x to 2.0x average speed up against baselines.
5okwaPNsME.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identical-reward rollout groups are a concrete inefficiency and that adaptive allocation reduces rollouts while maintaining or improving accuracy on math benchmarks.
5okwaPNsME.main_concern: Efficiency is measured by rollout count only, with no wall-clock or token-cost evidence, no accounting for pilot-rollout overhead, and unclear gains over the strongest baseline VIGOR.

Cg5E8RiA3Q.one_liner: Goedel-Architect proves Lean 4 theorems via a global blueprint of lemmas, proved in parallel and refined from failed lemmas.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.problem: Mainstream formal theorem-proving approaches use recursive lemma decomposition, which can loop inefficiently on dead-end strategies.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.method: An agentic pipeline generates a blueprint, a dependency graph of formally stated definitions and lemmas, optionally guided by a natural-language proof. A tool-equipped Lean prover closes each open lemma node in parallel, and failed lemmas drive refinement of the global blueprint.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.key_idea: Replace recursive decomposition with a global dependency-graph blueprint whose failed lemma nodes trigger statement repair, lemma splitting and dependency changes.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.evidence: Lean 4 benchmarks MiniF2F-test, PutnamBench, IMO 2025, Putnam 2025 and USAMO 2026 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B-A13B) as backbone, plus same-backbone comparisons that reviewers cite.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.claimed_gains: 99.2% pass@1 on MiniF2F-test and 75.6% on PutnamBench; with natural-language proof seeding, 100% on MiniF2F-test and 88.8% (597/672) on PutnamBench, 95.5% (642/672) with Gemini 3.1 Pro proofs, and 4/6 IMO 2025, 11/12 Putnam 2025, 3/6 USAMO 2026.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives strong open-weight results at low cost and that failure-driven blueprint refinement is effective, supported by same-backbone comparisons and ablations.
Cg5E8RiA3Q.main_concern: Novelty over related decomposition and blueprint work (ProofFlow, Delta Prover, LEAP) is unclear, and the claim that global blueprints beat recursive decomposition lacks controlled, systematic ablation.

Prv7ZI5DpZ.one_liner: Studies which frozen VLM layers a VLA action head should read, and proposes action-conditioned InfoNCE as a cheap layer-selection proxy.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.problem: It is unclear which backbone layers the latent interface between a pretrained vision-language backbone and the action head should expose in VLA policies.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.method: The paper compares single-layer selection with multi-layer fusion (three fusion mechanisms, three layer-subset strategies) on frozen backbones. It derives a reweighting equivalence between information-bottleneck objectives for action-conditioned InfoNCE and action prediction, and uses the InfoNCE score to pick the layer.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.key_idea: Rank backbone layers by an action-conditioned InfoNCE score, motivated by a proven reweighting equivalence between the InfoNCE and action-prediction information-bottleneck objectives.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.evidence: Three pretrained backbones on LIBERO and CALVIN with three policy-training seeds per configuration, comparing four proxies for layer quality against exhaustive policy sweeps.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.claimed_gains: 47 of 54 fusion configurations underperform the best single layer; InfoNCE selection needs 9–33 times less GPU compute than exhaustive sweeps and cuts mean selection regret from 17.89 percentage points (deepest-layer selection) to 3.71 points across six settings.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a systematic multi-seed, multi-backbone study with a clear finding on fusion and a practical InfoNCE-based layer selector.
Prv7ZI5DpZ.main_concern: The theory does not show why a higher InfoNCE score predicts policy success (fitted-critic tightness check, gap between IB and task losses), and the frozen-VLM setting omits fine-tuned VLMs such as pi0.

Fj1JACpMeM.one_liner: KnowledgeClaw builds and maintains an omnimodal typed hypergraph from personal files with a lifecycle agent, evaluated on the new OmniKE-Bench.
Fj1JACpMeM.problem: A live knowledge base needs omnimodality, a closed-loop lifecycle and multi-granular application at once, yet existing systems meet at most two and no benchmark measures all three.
Fj1JACpMeM.method: The paper formalizes Omnimodal Knowledge Engineering and releases OmniKE-Bench (six tasks, 1,829 model-free items over 3,960 real files in five modalities). KnowledgeClaw builds an omnimodal typed hypergraph from all of a person's files, keeps it current with a closed-loop lifecycle agent, and routes each query to the granularity it needs.
Fj1JACpMeM.key_idea: Build one typed hypergraph over files in five modalities, update it with a closed-loop lifecycle agent, and route each query to the granularity it needs.
Fj1JACpMeM.evidence: OmniKE-Bench against 30 baselines (10 method families per reviewers), with ablations that remove one component at a time.
Fj1JACpMeM.claimed_gains: Ranks first on all six tasks against 30 baselines with an overall OKE of 55.9, +14.6 points over the strongest baseline.
Fj1JACpMeM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is high quality with model-free gold answers, the evaluation against 30 baselines is extensive, and the system coherently integrates construction, maintenance and retrieval.
Fj1JACpMeM.main_concern: The method appears tailored to the benchmark's schema and setting, so gains may reflect setting match and system integration rather than methodological novelty.

FR6hIon4lL.one_liner: AMVL trains continuous latent reasoning in MLLMs with a forward-KL prior and reverse-KL posterior regularizer to curb answer leakage.
FR6hIon4lL.problem: In continuous latent reasoning, an answer-conditioned training posterior can exploit shortcuts, and standard variational training forces the inference-time prior to mimic a posterior that sees information unavailable at test time.
FR6hIon4lL.method: Asymmetric Mutual Variational Learning (AMVL) uses a bidirectional calibration objective: a forward KL trains the target-agnostic prior to match the posterior, and a reverse KL regularizes the posterior so it does not collapse into inference-incompatible regions. It is instantiated in a latent-integrated MLLM, with theory formalizing the leakage as prior contamination.
FR6hIon4lL.key_idea: Add a reverse-KL term that regularizes the answer-conditioned posterior alongside forward-KL prior alignment, using stop-gradients to keep their roles distinct and reduce prior contamination.
FR6hIon4lL.evidence: Theoretical analysis proving the dual-KL objective reduces contamination, and comparisons against discrete and latent-reasoning baselines on visual-reasoning datasets (the abstract is cut off before naming them).
FR6hIon4lL.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says AMVL consistently outperforms strong discrete and latent-reasoning baselines, without numbers).
FR6hIon4lL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the train-inference mismatch is a real, well-formalized problem and that the dual-KL fix is cheap and theoretically supported.
FR6hIon4lL.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute to the reverse-KL term: baselines differ in data and supervision, no experiment isolates leakage reduction as the cause, and the objective resembles DreamerV2 KL balancing.

FFEqOyIFtc.one_liner: A-DEFEAT-GT scales accumulated compression error by an adaptive discount coefficient and adds gradient tracking for compressed decentralized learning.
FFEqOyIFtc.problem: Correcting compression error and mitigating network-topology effects in decentralized non-convex learning under communication constraints remains open, particularly in sparse networks.
FFEqOyIFtc.method: Error feedback is combined with an adaptively tuned discount coefficient that controls the influence of accumulated compression errors, plus gradient tracking for heterogeneous data, without momentum propagation or consensus model updates. Reviewers also mention a companion algorithm, A-DEFEAT, without gradient tracking.
FFEqOyIFtc.key_idea: Discount the accumulated compression error in error feedback with an adaptively tuned coefficient, and use gradient tracking to handle heterogeneous data.
FFEqOyIFtc.evidence: Convergence guarantees for both algorithms (improved dependence on the network spectral gap per reviewers) and experiments comparing test accuracy under the same communication budget.
FFEqOyIFtc.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says higher test accuracy than existing decentralized methods under the same communication budget, especially on sparse networks, without numbers).
FFEqOyIFtc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the adaptive discounting idea is simple and well motivated, with rigorous convergence guarantees that improve dependence on the network spectral gap.
FFEqOyIFtc.main_concern: The motivation for focusing on discounted error feedback and the presentation (Assumption 1, Figure 1) are unclear, and hyperparameters appear to be selected on the test set.

Y6qHdsEvAu.one_liner: RL post-training on five-question quizzes under one shared token budget makes reasoning LLMs produce shorter responses without length penalties.
Y6qHdsEvAu.problem: Long chain-of-thought traces dominate inference cost, and prior fixes such as length penalties, early exit or distilled shorter traces rely on explicit length mechanisms.
Y6qHdsEvAu.method: Multiple questions are grouped into one prompt under a shared response budget that is not enforced per question, and a model is post-trained with RL (PPO on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct) on GSM8K-Quiz and Math-Quiz built from five-question groups. The reward counts only correct answers, with no length penalty or difficulty labels.
Y6qHdsEvAu.key_idea: Pack five questions under a shared response budget so the policy learns to allocate tokens across questions implicitly, with no explicit length objective.
Y6qHdsEvAu.evidence: PPO training on GSM8K-Quiz and Math-Quiz, with quiz evaluation (the abstract is cut off before single-question results) and, per reviewers, additional base models DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.
Y6qHdsEvAu.claimed_gains: Quiz-trained PPO policies use about 50% fewer tokens than the base instruct model on GSM8K-Quiz and 35% fewer on Math-Quiz, with comparable accuracy.
Y6qHdsEvAu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, needs no change to architecture or optimizer, and yields clear token savings while matching or exceeding baseline accuracy.
Y6qHdsEvAu.main_concern: Gains may come from tighter per-question token limits rather than learned cross-question allocation, since no control imposes comparable per-question budgets in single-question training.

8BSs4LpdRk.one_liner: Formalizes multi-agent attribution as a cooperative game over coalition distribution, intervention protocol and target metric, and compares attribution methods.
8BSs4LpdRk.problem: Existing approaches to credit assignment among agents in multi-agent systems lack a unified formulation.
8BSs4LpdRk.method: Agent attribution is framed as a cooperative game parameterized by coalition distribution, intervention protocol and target metric. The paper compares agent ablation with introspective LLM judges, Leave-One-Out (LOO) with combinatorial methods, prompt-conditioned attribution for prompt optimization, and audits a medical multi-agent system.
8BSs4LpdRk.key_idea: Treat coalition distribution, intervention protocol and target metric as parameters of a cooperative game, so that different intervention protocols are shown to induce distinct attribution games.
8BSs4LpdRk.evidence: Experiments varying one design choice at a time on multi-agent systems of four to six agents (per reviewers, including WorkBench) and a medical multi-agent system audit.
8BSs4LpdRk.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says LOO identifies bottleneck agents as effectively as combinatorial methods at much lower cost, and ethics alignment rises while diagnostic accuracy is maintained, without numbers).
8BSs4LpdRk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multi-agent attribution is an important problem and the framework is extensive, with the top-rated review crediting it for separating design choices that prior work fixed together.
8BSs4LpdRk.main_concern: The LOO and attribution-guided optimization claims are weakly supported (tested only on four- to six-agent systems, and attribution is computed after already optimizing all agents), and technical novelty is unclear.

RX2UGTRAKz.one_liner: Brain-referenced transfer evaluation shows fMRI encoding predictions transfer worse than measured responses; Population Subspace Supervision upweights leading-subspace errors.
RX2UGTRAKz.problem: It is unclear whether model-predicted fMRI responses preserve the cross-subject transfer capability of measured brain responses.
RX2UGTRAKz.method: The paper compares transfer from measured source-subject responses with transfer from model predictions under matched target adaptation, and diagnoses the gap through principal-component analysis. Population Subspace Supervision (PSS) upweights training errors in the leading source-population subspace, which reviewers describe as a PCA-subspace-weighted MSE.
RX2UGTRAKz.key_idea: Upweight prediction errors along the leading principal-component subspace of measured source responses, because predicted responses concentrate variance in fewer PCs and transfer less.
RX2UGTRAKz.evidence: NSD with 4 backbones x 3 predictors (12 configurations) and 12 BOLD5000 configurations, with controlled diagnostics such as random PC subsets, spectrum replacement and shuffled coordinate maps.
RX2UGTRAKz.claimed_gains: PSS closes 39.5% of the brain–model transfer gap, improves mean transfer across all 12 NSD configurations, and improves mean correlation in 11 of 12 BOLD5000 configurations.
RX2UGTRAKz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is meaningful and the diagnostic chain is carefully controlled, with broad validation across backbones, configurations and an external dataset.
RX2UGTRAKz.main_concern: PSS is a simple PCA-subspace reweighting of MSE, and the transfer gap is not separated from ordinary source-prediction error, with only four participants limiting generalization.

74m9TJzUIf.one_liner: A lightweight predictor on frozen audio-encoder representations detects unreliable speech inputs to Audio LLMs before generation.
74m9TJzUIf.problem: When an input recording is too degraded, an Audio LLM may answer from an incorrect transcription, and the model is a poor judge of its own transcription reliability.
74m9TJzUIf.method: A lightweight reliability predictor (a pooling module plus MLP per reviewers) takes representations from the frozen audio encoder and predicts a reliability class before generation. A predicted unreliable query can trigger a clarification request without modifying the Audio LLM.
74m9TJzUIf.key_idea: Read transcription reliability from the frozen audio encoder's representations with a small classifier, instead of self-assessment prompts, speech quality predictors or generation uncertainty.
74m9TJzUIf.evidence: Comparison with self-assessment prompting, speech quality predictors, generation uncertainty and transcript-conditioned WER estimation, on in-domain and cross-domain sets across three model families, with cross-model label transfer.
74m9TJzUIf.claimed_gains: 77.56% in-domain (the metric and cross-domain figure are cut off in the abstract); a reviewer cites macro-F1 gains of 10.33 and 11.93 points over the strongest baseline for Qwen2-Audio.
74m9TJzUIf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting transcription failure before decoding is a useful goal and that the lightweight predictor, which leaves the Audio LLM unmodified, beats the evaluated baselines.
74m9TJzUIf.main_concern: The claim that reliability is encoded in the Audio LLM's own encoder is untested against other frozen encoders (HuBERT, WavLM, Whisper) with the same head, and labels come from controlled synthetic corruption.

MW0CIgxt0T.one_liner: PMF-CL casts continual learning as Pareto-optimal balancing of conflicting tasks, using static O(d^2) memory regardless of task count.
MW0CIgxt0T.problem: Continual learning lacks a grounded account of what past-task information must be stored, and because tasks rarely share a common global minimizer, some forgetting is inevitable.
MW0CIgxt0T.method: Continual learning is reframed as balancing conflicting tasks in hindsight from a multi-task perspective, seeking Pareto-optimal solutions that minimally forget earlier tasks. PMF-CL is derived for linear and basis-function regression and extends to losses with quadratic upper bounds around their minimizers, with a static memory footprint of O(d^2) for d model parameters.
MW0CIgxt0T.key_idea: Preserve each task's quadratic loss information in a fixed-size memory so preference-selected Pareto-optimal solutions are recovered sequentially, exactly for quadratic losses.
MW0CIgxt0T.evidence: Theory with exact recovery for quadratic losses and bounded-forgetting guarantees for quadratically upper-bounded losses, plus Appendix G experiments on synthetic linear regression and a linear classifier on Sequential MNIST.
MW0CIgxt0T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Pareto view is a theoretically motivated, realistic setting that allows different task minimizers and specifies what history to retain, with memory that does not grow with the number of tasks.
MW0CIgxt0T.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the linear-regression case reduces to recursive least squares, and experiments are confined to synthetic linear regression and linear classification on Sequential MNIST against older baselines.

W14LMlMpXd.one_liner: IG-VLA learns latent future-scene reasoning, then internalizes it into a Scene Gist Token so inference skips explicit imagination.
W14LMlMpXd.problem: VLA reasoning mostly covers observed states rather than anticipating future scene evolution, and explicit future rollouts at every inference step add substantial computational overhead.
W14LMlMpXd.method: Latent Spatiotemporal Reasoning learns to imagine task-relevant future scene evolution in visual representation space to guide action prediction, without pixel-level video generation. Scene Gist Memory internalizes the reasoning-derived scene-behavior associations into a compact Scene Gist Token, so inference bypasses explicit future imagination.
W14LMlMpXd.key_idea: Train with latent future-scene prediction, then distill the scene-behavior associations into one Scene Gist Token so deployment needs no explicit future imagination.
W14LMlMpXd.evidence: Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and VLABench (plus a real-robot test per reviewers), with latency measured on a single NVIDIA A6000 GPU.
W14LMlMpXd.claimed_gains: On the LIBERO-Plus Language suite both the reasoning and gist policies outperform the strongest baseline by nearly 6% in success rate, and the gist policy gives up to 6.38x speedup, cutting latency from 1,081 ms to 169.5 ms per action chunk.
W14LMlMpXd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training with future imagination and deploying without it is a practical way to cut VLA inference cost while largely preserving success rates, with broad benchmark coverage.
W14LMlMpXd.main_concern: Gains over the ACoT-VLA backbone are small and lack controls to attribute them to future reasoning, and novelty over existing world action models is unclear.

VFePP8Kmzn.one_liner: EviBoltz conditions Boltz-2 on cryo-EM density in both the Pairformer representations and diffusion coordinate generation.
VFePP8Kmzn.problem: Biomolecular structure predictors produce plausible conformations that may not match the state observed in a particular sample, and using cryo-EM density to guide both global relationships and local atomic placement remains hard.
VFePP8Kmzn.method: Global density interactions update the single and pair representations of the Boltz-2 Pairformer, and atom-centered, multiscale density queries continually guide diffusion-based coordinate generation.
VFePP8Kmzn.key_idea: Inject cryo-EM density at two levels: global density interactions update Pairformer single and pair representations, and atom-centered multiscale density queries steer diffusion-based coordinate generation.
VFePP8Kmzn.evidence: An independent benchmark (120 systems per reviewers) with ablation of the two conditioning pathways, long-loop analysis, and a controlled supervised experiment on two states of the same URAT1 sequence.
VFePP8Kmzn.claimed_gains: Relative to Boltz-2, acceptable protein–protein interface success rises from 27.8% to 70.4% and joint ligand-pocket success from 7.0% to 34.9%, with protein–peptide rising from 0.0% to 75.0% and antibody–antigen from 0.0% to 66.7%.
VFePP8Kmzn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning both the trunk and the diffusion head on density is a reasonable design, with ablations showing value for both pathways on a sizable benchmark.
VFePP8Kmzn.main_concern: Gains over density-free Boltz-2 do not isolate the architecture's contribution, since density adds information, and density-aware baselines are hard to interpret while map-to-structure and geometry-validation metrics are missing.

iSpFXrUGA7.one_liner: UA-NWM scores UAV trajectories by the part of the prediction-goal discrepancy that an uncertainty subspace cannot explain.
iSpFXrUGA7.problem: World-model navigation methods rank candidate trajectories with one or a few point predictions of the future, which is inadequate in large outdoor environments with substantial future-state uncertainty.
iSpFXrUGA7.method: A latent world model represents plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace and decomposes the prediction–goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explainable and unexplainable components, framing trajectory scoring as conditional out-of-distribution detection. Only the unexplainable residual is used for scoring, without multiple future samples.
iSpFXrUGA7.key_idea: Score each trajectory only by the residual of the prediction-goal discrepancy outside a learned uncertainty subspace, in a single forward pass.
iSpFXrUGA7.evidence: Aerial navigation benchmarks (a new dataset per reviewers), real-world UAV experiments, and 2D navigation tasks in the appendix, with a latency comparison against NWM and One-Step WM.
iSpFXrUGA7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says UA-NWM consistently outperforms existing navigation world models at low inference latency, without numbers).
iSpFXrUGA7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring from point predictions is a real weakness and that the single-pass fix is low-cost and validated across benchmarks and real-world tests.
iSpFXrUGA7.main_concern: The uncertainty and out-of-distribution framing is weakly supported, since much of the gain appears already in the deterministic baseline and the conditional-compatibility AUROC differs by only about 0.01.

sgJwkKC1rv.one_liner: Protects private attributes from closed-source VLM inference by sequentially editing out attribute-related visual cues ranked by importance.
sgJwkKC1rv.problem: Images submitted to closed-source VLMs passively reveal attributes such as age, gender and occupation, and perturbation-based defenses fail because the service controls its own preprocessing and can strip pixel-level perturbations.
sgJwkKC1rv.method: The paper formalizes Service-Time Private Attribute Inference (ST-PAI) and defends with semantic image editing that removes attribute-related visual cues in order of importance, giving a discrete privacy-utility frontier. It also builds SynthPAI-Visual, a synthetic multi-attribute benchmark with automatically generated annotations, and repurposes VQA tasks to measure utility cost.
sgJwkKC1rv.key_idea: Edit out attribute-revealing visual cues in order of importance at the semantic level, so protection survives upstream purification that strips pixel-level perturbations.
sgJwkKC1rv.evidence: Two geolocation benchmarks and SynthPAI-Visual, with multiple attackers and downstream VQA tasks, comparing semantic editing against perturbation-based protection.
sgJwkKC1rv.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says semantic editing remains robust to upstream purification while perturbation-based protection collapses, without numbers).
sgJwkKC1rv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the method is well designed, with extensive evaluation across attackers and downstream domains and a useful privacy-utility tradeoff.
sgJwkKC1rv.main_concern: The threat model is narrow, novelty over other editing-based defenses is unclear, and the benchmark's ground truth comes from the same Qwen3-VL-8B model used by the main pipeline.

I0jCvRExZY.one_liner: Basketball-QA is a benchmark of over 8K questions that separates perception from reasoning failures in multi-player basketball video understanding.
I0jCvRExZY.problem: Existing evaluations rarely combine multiple interacting players, dense event sequences and fine-grained spatial and temporal relations in a single video understanding task.
I0jCvRExZY.method: The benchmark has over 8K questions covering player matching, spatial grounding, action recognition, temporal grounding, event relations, counting, hallucination and tactical analysis. Targeted experiments then localize failures with atomic perception probes and by giving correct perceptual facts as text to a small language model.
I0jCvRExZY.key_idea: Locate failures by comparing end-to-end video QA, atomic perception probes, and a text-only language model given correct facts, to separate perception errors from reasoning errors.
I0jCvRExZY.evidence: End-to-end evaluation of video-input MLLMs (open- and closed-source per reviewers), atomic perception tests, and a small language model given correct facts in text without task-specific fine-tuning.
I0jCvRExZY.claimed_gains: The best video-input MLLM reaches 76.0% multiple-choice accuracy and 2.87/5 on open-ended questions, while a small language model given correct perceptual facts in text reaches 78.5% multiple-choice accuracy.
I0jCvRExZY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that multi-player basketball understanding is a meaningful gap, the evaluation covers many recent MLLMs, and the perception-versus-reasoning diagnostic is useful.
I0jCvRExZY.main_concern: The multiple-choice items may contain answer-position and surface-form shortcuts (negation-style hallucination options almost always in option D), and error analysis linking perception errors to wrong answers is limited.

ovSzy71h0x.one_liner: MGME represents unknown objects with multiple prototypes generated by orthogonal geodesic traversal around known-class embeddings instead of a single mean.
ovSzy71h0x.problem: Open-world object detectors represent unknowns by the arithmetic mean of known class embeddings or one generic prompt, which compresses diverse semantic directions into one proxy that can land in ambiguous regions (mean collapse).
ovSzy71h0x.method: MGME extracts an orthogonal residual subspace as an exploration space and generates unknown prototypes by geodesic traversal along known-class boundaries. A dual-constraint selection combines cross-class boundary pruning with LLM-driven semantic steering, and Discriminative Prototype Orthogonalization pushes known text prototypes apart during training.
ovSzy71h0x.key_idea: Generate multiple unknown prototypes by geodesic steps in the orthogonal residual subspace of known-class embeddings, filtered by boundary pruning and LLM semantic steering.
ovSzy71h0x.evidence: A shared OWL-ViT implementation with ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14, compared with FOMO, UMB and PASS retrained under the same splits, backbones and evaluation code per reviewers.
ovSzy71h0x.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (reviewers cite overall unknown mAP rising from 6.8 to 11.8 on ViT-B/16 and from 15.9 to 19.2 on ViT-L/14).
ovSzy71h0x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a single mean prototype is too restrictive for heterogeneous unknowns, that multi-prototype generation is a reasonable alternative, and that the aggregate gains are substantial.
ovSzy71h0x.main_concern: The geometric claim is not established, since a normalized Euclidean addition with a matched step size equals the geodesic step, so the Table 2 gap may come from unmatched step sizes or missing normalization.

FVwIiNbeUM.one_liner: A benchmark built from MPRA diplotype data tests whether genomic sequence models compose non-additive variant effects across four tasks.
FVwIiNbeUM.problem: Genomic sequence models are benchmarked almost exclusively on single variants against a reference background, yet real haplotypes carry many variants and regulatory grammar is non-additive.
FVwIiNbeUM.method: The benchmark uses MPRA diplotype experiments that assay all four haplotypes (REF, A, B, AB) of thousands of variant pairs, plus about 1.15M single-variant (variant x cell-type) measurements across three studies. Five models are evaluated on single-variant regression (T1), interaction regression (T2), non-additive pair detection (T3) and full-versus-additive prediction across 421 phased personal genomes (T4), under zero-shot and frozen-encoder linear-probe readouts.
FVwIiNbeUM.key_idea: Score models directly on measured interaction effects across all four haplotypes of variant pairs, under both zero-shot and linear-probe readouts, to test whether they compose variant effects.
FVwIiNbeUM.evidence: Five models spanning supervised sequence-to-function predictors and genome language models, evaluated on MPRA data from three studies (including Siraj et al. 2026) and 421 phased personal genomes.
FVwIiNbeUM.claimed_gains: On Siraj et al. (2026), single-variant ranking reaches zero-shot Spearman rho up to 0.42 and linear probe up to 0.73, while interaction signal is captured far less (rho <= 0.32; AUROC <= 0.68, against 0.62 for inter-variant distance alone).
FVwIiNbeUM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a timely gap by testing non-additive regulatory effects and shows a clear performance drop from single-variant to interaction prediction.
FVwIiNbeUM.main_concern: MPRA-derived interactions may reflect global nonlinearities rather than true epistasis, and the high-confidence interaction datasets are small, so the poor model results are hard to interpret.

plmHDI1b7d.one_liner: Compares competitive and cooperative social rewards as the upstream environment shaping what self-evolving LLM agents store in memory.
plmHDI1b7d.problem: Work on self-evolving LLM agents refines downstream memory updaters, while the upstream social environment that generates and filters interaction trajectories is largely unexamined.
plmHDI1b7d.method: With the memory updater held fixed, the paper studies two social regimes: competition driven by relative individual credit and cooperation driven by shared team outcomes. Rewards act as process rewards during interaction and as social credit after it, and results are measured by immediate discovery and by transfer to fresh solvers with frozen memory.
plmHDI1b7d.key_idea: Vary only the social reward structure, individual versus shared credit during and after interaction, to change which experiences are retained in persistent memory.
plmHDI1b7d.evidence: Experiments with reward audits, communication ablations and frozen-memory transfer on tasks such as AIME and HotpotQA across backbones, as described by reviewers.
plmHDI1b7d.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports that competition accelerates discovery and cooperation favors structured routines, without numbers).
plmHDI1b7d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating social structure as a design variable upstream of memory updates is meaningful, with a simple design and a clear split between immediate discovery and frozen-memory transfer.
plmHDI1b7d.main_concern: Reported numbers are inconsistent across tables (reward-audit AIME and HotpotQA values in Tables 2 and 5 disagree), and the communication ablation confounds agent roles and the number of solutions.

bYpvxDEkUD.one_liner: TeleQuant feeds each step's discarded activation-rounding residual into the next evaluation to cancel accumulated quantization drift in diffusion transformers.
bYpvxDEkUD.problem: In post-training-quantized diffusion transformers, correlated rounding errors from chained denoiser evaluations accumulate into structured trajectory drift that persists in the returned sample and degrades fidelity.
bYpvxDEkUD.method: A training-free temporal noise-shaping framework feeds a discarded activation-rounding residual into the next evaluation, with a gain matched to adjacent solver responses and activation scales. An INT8 residual state and a fused activation operator add the compensation on the host's path, with selective layer placement and damped feedback motivated by a first-order telescoping identity.
bYpvxDEkUD.key_idea: Re-inject the previous step's activation-rounding residual into the next denoiser evaluation with damped, scale-matched gain, so accumulated error telescopes into a terminal residual.
bYpvxDEkUD.evidence: DiT-XL/2, PixArt-Sigma, SDXL and Open-Sora 1.2 on frozen ViDiT-Q and SVDQuant hosts, with matched rounding ablations.
bYpvxDEkUD.claimed_gains: Improved image fidelity and video consistency over frozen ViDiT-Q and SVDQuant hosts, retaining most of the host speedup at 1.03×–1.05× latency; no fidelity numbers are stated in the abstract.
bYpvxDEkUD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coordinating rounding errors across denoising steps is a sound idea, supported by the telescoping analysis and gains on two quantization hosts and four backbones with minimal overhead.
bYpvxDEkUD.main_concern: The main ablation changes damping, solver weighting and scale matching together, so the contribution of the matching rule is unclear, and the TCEC comparison may be incomplete.

rDMS8TZJKo.one_liner: Dual-anchoring combined with stochastic resolvent approximation and batch-size scheduling reaches near-optimal oracle complexity for stochastic monotone root-finding.
rDMS8TZJKo.problem: Existing stochastic dual-anchoring guarantees require cocoercivity in expectation and attain only O(eps^-3) oracle complexity, leaving a gap to the near-optimal O~(eps^-2) of other methods.
rDMS8TZJKo.method: The algorithm combines dual-anchoring with stochastic resolvent approximation and optimized variance control (a batch-size schedule per reviewers). It targets unbiased stochastic oracles with variance bounded by sigma^2, where sample operators are monotone and uniformly L-Lipschitz.
rDMS8TZJKo.key_idea: Combine dual-anchor acceleration with stochastic resolvent approximation and a batch-size schedule that controls variance, extending dual anchoring beyond cocoercive operators.
rDMS8TZJKo.evidence: Theoretical complexity analysis under samplewise monotone and L-Lipschitz assumptions, plus numerical experiments including a monotone experiment compared with RAIN per reviewers.
rDMS8TZJKo.claimed_gains: Finds x_eps with E||F(x_eps)|| <= eps at oracle complexity O((LD/eps)l + (sigma^2/eps^2)l^2), l = log(1+LD/eps), cutting the poly-logarithmic factor from cubic (the new factor is cut off in the abstract; a reviewer says quadratic).
rDMS8TZJKo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the batch-size scheduling is simple and effective, improving complexity to near-optimal and extending dual anchoring from cocoercive to monotone problems.
rDMS8TZJKo.main_concern: Technical novelty and improvement over existing near-optimal methods such as RAIN are limited to a logarithmic factor, and the best experimental results come from a practical variant without the stated guarantee.

kgFMhJvQ2l.one_liner: PuriShield trains a generator that produces structured, density-guided protective perturbations robust to diffusion-based purification against unauthorized diffusion customization.
kgFMhJvQ2l.problem: Unstructured protective perturbations against unauthorized diffusion customization are fragile under diffusion-based purification.
kgFMhJvQ2l.method: A Robust Protective Perturbation Generator (RPPG) is trained with three designs: pattern density-guided generation for structured perturbations, a latent distribution contrastive loss to refine perturbations, and embedded dual-head modulation for high-quality perturbation synthesis.
kgFMhJvQ2l.key_idea: Generate structured, pattern-density-guided perturbations with a learned generator refined by a latent distribution contrastive loss, so protection survives diffusion-based purification.
kgFMhJvQ2l.evidence: Defense against 5 customization methods and 13 purification methods including UDAP, plus cross-task and cross-domain tests; reviewers add ten baselines, an adaptive Fourier-domain attack and a browser extension.
kgFMhJvQ2l.claimed_gains: Defends against 5 customization methods before purification, attains optimal robustness across 13 purification methods and surpasses baselines against UDAP, and trains the RPPG in 31.6 minutes with 5.8 ms inference (the unit text is cut off in the abstract).
kgFMhJvQ2l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real fragility of protective perturbations under purification, with broad empirical coverage and fast single-pass deployment.
kgFMhJvQ2l.main_concern: Novelty over close precedents (BlurGuard, PatchOut, Anti-Reference) is unclear, and reported numbers are inconsistent across tables.

kErdmYc01b.one_liner: READ refines feed-forward 3D Gaussian renderings by reprojecting rendered depth to retrieve source evidence and predicting a bounded residual.
kErdmYc01b.problem: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting loses fine appearance details when source observations are encoded into Gaussian attributes, and learned correspondence estimation or costly refinement adds substantial overhead.
kErdmYc01b.method: Rendered depth establishes candidate correspondences into the source views, and geometric reliability with target-conditioned source weights guides fusion of source colors and shallow features. A shared convolutional network with 21K trainable parameters predicts a bounded residual to refine the target rendering.
kErdmYc01b.key_idea: Use rendered depth to directly retrieve reprojected source evidence, fuse it by geometric reliability and target-conditioned weights, and apply a bounded CNN residual to the rendering.
kErdmYc01b.evidence: DL3DV, RealEstate10K and Replica, with reviewers noting transfer across TokenGS, DepthSplat and ReSplat and two to eight source views.
kErdmYc01b.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says rendering quality improves on DL3DV, RealEstate10K and Replica with 21K trainable parameters, without numbers).
kErdmYc01b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the module is lightweight and carefully gated by depth consistency, and that it transfers across reconstruction models and datasets with clear improvements.
kErdmYc01b.main_concern: Gains concentrate near source views and fade far from them, and the evaluation lacks comparisons with other refinement methods and broader reconstruction models.

fQ8BgQXIQU.one_liner: CreditFilter weights RLVR tokens by an exponential window over within-response entropy rank, calibrated to measured fork probability.
fQ8BgQXIQU.problem: Critic-free RLVR gives every token a uniform advantage, and token-reweighting heuristics such as the 80/20 mask favor high-entropy tokens without measuring a token's actual impact on the outcome.
fQ8BgQXIQU.method: The paper defines the forking value (variance of success probability over next-token choices) and factorizes it into fork consequence and fork probability, which decays exponentially with within-response entropy rank on Qwen3-8B-Base. CreditFilter weights tokens by an exponential window over that rank with no extra forward passes, stabilized by difficulty damping and an entropy-gated fallback.
fQ8BgQXIQU.key_idea: Weight each token by an exponential window over its within-response entropy rank, calibrated to the measured decay of fork probability under an approximately flat fork consequence.
fQ8BgQXIQU.evidence: Qwen3-8B-Base on MATH500 and AIME sets against GRPO, DAPO, the 80/20 mask and STARE, with ablations of window shape, rank coordinate and stabilizers, plus a variance-decomposition argument.
fQ8BgQXIQU.claimed_gains: Outperforms GRPO and DAPO by 4--5 points on MATH500 and 8--10 on the AIME sets.
fQ8BgQXIQU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, needs no extra forward passes, and that response-local ranking ablations show where the gains come from.
fQ8BgQXIQU.main_concern: The theory-to-algorithm link is loose, since the variance decomposition holds in expectation rather than per response and the abstract overstates weighting by measured impact when only the fork-probability envelope is used.

44TyROTlFy.one_liner: CovenantBench is a benchmark and RL environment for agentic reasoning over real corporate debt contracts, with litigation-anchored verifiable rewards.
44TyROTlFy.problem: Existing legal benchmarks such as CUAD and LegalBench use short snippets (per reviewers), so reasoning over full corporate debt instruments with outcomes anchored to real covenant litigation is untested.
44TyROTlFy.method: The benchmark has three layers: agentic document-navigation tasks over real indentures and credit agreements (4,042 tasks, deterministic checkers), outcome prediction on 101 held-out issue prompts from 89 real covenant disputes, and an adversarial debate protocol judged against true outcomes. A 9B model is trained with QLoRA and GRPO under $150 of compute through supervised fine-tuning, navigation RL, judge anchoring and two rounds of debate self-play.
44TyROTlFy.key_idea: Anchor RL rewards in deterministic checkers for document navigation and in real court outcomes for a judge that scores advocate policies in debate self-play.
44TyROTlFy.evidence: A 4,042-task audited evaluation suite, 825 held-out instances from the training task families, and 101 outcome-prediction prompts, with closed-book, constant-answer and tool-budget controls.
