2FaHRono5T.main_concern: Attention and saliency comparisons lack enough validation to distinguish differences in human-like processing from measurement limitations.

oeP0Cw5dOl.one_liner: Models fine-grained video state changes for temporal grounding by differencing aligned patch embeddings across consecutive frames.
oeP0Cw5dOl.problem: Video-MLLMs rely on static RGB frame features that fail to capture fine-grained visual state transitions needed to localize event boundaries accurately.
oeP0Cw5dOl.method: DynaSense aligns visual features at each timestamp with their nearest neighbor references from the preceding timestamp in a position-free embedding space using a shared visual backbone. It then adds 2D spatial positional encodings and computes feature differences to capture both appearance changes and spatial displacements, trained with a new automated Video State Change Recognition (VideoSCR) dataset.
oeP0Cw5dOl.key_idea: Matches patch features across adjacent timestamps in position-free space and differences them after adding 2D spatial encodings to represent appearance and motion transitions.
oeP0Cw5dOl.evidence: Evaluated on video temporal grounding benchmarks by fine-tuning Qwen3-VL at 2B and 8B parameter scales along with VideoSCR dataset pretraining.
oeP0Cw5dOl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that DynaSense extracts dynamic temporal-change representations directly from a shared vision backbone without requiring a separate motion encoder and improves over Qwen3-VL baselines.
oeP0Cw5dOl.main_concern: Ablations show that alternative matching and differencing orders yield identical mIoU, the synthetic VideoSCR dataset lacks human validation or train-test overlap checks, and comparisons pit two-stage fine-tuned models against unadapted baselines.

dFxJh93AKz.one_liner: Clusters latent actions by motion category via supervised contrastive learning while separately conditioning the action decoder on embodiment or scene.
dFxJh93AKz.problem: Latent-action representations typically entangle motion semantics with embodiment-specific dynamics, preventing skills learned on one robot body from driving another.
dFxJh93AKz.method: Clustered Latent Actions Separated from Body and Scene (CLASS) uses supervised contrastive learning with a continuity regularizer to pull latent actions from different bodies into a single cluster per motion category. An action decoder conditioned separately on a body domain embedding or scene object position allows the fixed centroid of each motion cluster to act as a shared control signal across bodies.
dFxJh93AKz.key_idea: Separates motion semantics from physical dynamics by pulling cross-body latent actions into per-category contrastive clusters and conditioning the decoder on explicit body or scene vectors.
dFxJh93AKz.evidence: Evaluated on four DeepMind Control and Loco-MuJoCo locomotion bodies and simulated object manipulation tasks (including LIBERO) using centroid driving, mid-rollout switching, and cross-body transfer tests.
dFxJh93AKz.claimed_gains: Adapting about 32 parameters adds a new body; cross-body cumulative reward drops about 80% without body conditioning and 88% without contrastive learning, while cosine interpolation between centroids lowers mid-rollout switch fall rates from about 98% to 13–19%.
dFxJh93AKz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value that the paper tests cluster centroids directly as closed-loop control inputs for cross-body locomotion and mid-rollout skill switching rather than relying only on latent visualizations.
dFxJh93AKz.main_concern: Probing shows that body identity (80.4% accuracy) and object position (R^2=0.62) remain partially encoded in the latent variable, transfer to LIBERO grasping is weak, and driving with fixed category centroids closely resembles standard category-conditioned control.

hq6BOHmaBA.one_liner: Precomputes subspace query-centroid-to-key score tables during reusable-prefix prefill to enable fast top-L sparse attention during decoding.
hq6BOHmaBA.problem: In long-context LLM serving with reusable prefixes, dense KV-cache attention bottlenecks decoding, while online sparse-attention retrieval either loses accuracy from query-key distribution mismatch or incurs high per-step search overhead.
hq6BOHmaBA.method: CSAttention shifts sparse-attention indexing offline to the prefix-build stage by clustering prefill queries in subspaces, precomputing centroid-to-key partial scores, and storing bounded top-L lookup tables per query centroid. During decoding, each new query routes to its nearest query centroids, aggregates their precomputed key shortlists, and computes exact attention over the selected KV entries.
hq6BOHmaBA.key_idea: Clusters prefill queries in subspaces to precompute top-L centroid-to-key lookup tables offline, routing online decode queries to nearest centroids for fast KV shortlist retrieval.
hq6BOHmaBA.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM backbones on LongBench, LongBench-v2, and long-generation stress tests.
hq6BOHmaBA.claimed_gains: Preserves near-full-attention accuracy at 95% sparsity (5% active prefix KV cache) on LongBench and LongBench-v2.
hq6BOHmaBA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that precomputing query-centroid score lookup tables for reusable prefixes is a well-motivated, training-free mechanism that retains accuracy at 95% KV sparsity while accelerating decoding.
hq6BOHmaBA.main_concern: Prefill-derived query centroids can drift during very long generations or short-input long-output reasoning tasks, and the paper insufficiently details how head-varying token selections are batched for efficient GEMM execution.

PwQRrZHqbk.one_liner: Benchmarks research-ideation agents across 100 resource-constrained tasks using a 12-dimension LLM judge aligned against conference peer reviews.
PwQRrZHqbk.problem: Existing evaluations of automated research-ideation agents ignore explicit compute and budget feasibility constraints and rarely validate their LLM judges against human peer review.
PwQRrZHqbk.method: AlphaIdeaBench provides 100 ideation tasks (50 workshop calls for papers and 50 survey open problems), each paired with an explicit resource budget and standardized proposal schema. An LLM judge evaluates proposals across 12 validity, novelty, and feasibility dimensions, validated by comparing its novelty scores on 600 ICLR, NeurIPS, and ICML papers against scores extracted from reviewer comments.
PwQRrZHqbk.key_idea: Pairs 100 research-ideation tasks with explicit resource budgets and evaluates proposals using a 12-dimension LLM rubric checked against conference peer-review novelty scores.
PwQRrZHqbk.evidence: Validates the Gemini 3.7 Flash judge on 600 papers from ICLR 2026, NeurIPS 2025, and ICML 2025, and benchmarks 8 ideation harnesses and 8 backbone LLMs across 100 tasks.
PwQRrZHqbk.claimed_gains: For problem and method novelty, Gemini 3.7 Flash is within one point of the reviewer-derived score on 94–97% of papers.
PwQRrZHqbk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers welcome the explicit incorporation of compute, time, and budget feasibility constraints into research-idea evaluation along with the multi-axis rubric comparing harnesses and backbones.
PwQRrZHqbk.main_concern: The judge validation is circular because the same Gemini 3.7 Flash model both extracts the reference novelty scores from human reviewer comments and acts as the evaluated judge without independent human verification.

wmBiZKsp47.one_liner: Formulates LLM confidence estimation as distributional regression over continuous correctness scores using Beta and piecewise-uniform distributions.
wmBiZKsp47.problem: Standard LLM confidence estimation binarizes continuous output quality metrics with an arbitrary threshold, discarding partial-correctness information and predictive uncertainty.
wmBiZKsp47.method: The authors model LLM confidence as a full probability distribution over continuous correctness scores in [0,1] using Beta regression (including Hurdle-Beta) and piecewise-uniform regression. This enables querying exceedance probabilities at arbitrary quality thresholds without retraining and provides predictive variance and credible intervals.
wmBiZKsp47.key_idea: Predicts parametric probability distributions over continuous response correctness scores via Beta and piecewise-uniform regression instead of binary correctness probabilities.
wmBiZKsp47.evidence: Supported by sample-efficiency theoretical analysis for Beta regression and empirical evaluations across multiple NLP tasks and datasets including XSum, CNN/DM, and Biographies.
wmBiZKsp47.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reframing LLM confidence estimation as distributional regression over continuous correctness scores well-motivated for querying arbitrary quality thresholds without retraining.
wmBiZKsp47.main_concern: A mathematical error in Lemma 2 invalidates the claimed O(k^-4) histogram approximation rate, and fixing the Beta precision parameter phi makes predictive variance a deterministic function of the mean, undermining the claimed uncertainty-quantification benefit.

8UgphlLDok.one_liner: Periodically forks long-horizon autoresearch agents into parallel branches with inherited workspaces but reset chat contexts to escape local optima.
8UgphlLDok.problem: Long-horizon autoresearch agents frequently become trapped in localized regions of the solution space ('idea basins'), plateauing at suboptimal scores despite additional compute.
8UgphlLDok.method: The authors embed candidate artifacts by functional similarity to diagnose idea basins and introduce branch-reset, a periodic test-time intervention. Branch-reset forks an agent into parallel trajectories that each inherit the accumulated workspace files but start with a fresh chat context, runs each branch for a fixed horizon, and continues from the highest-scoring trajectory.
8UgphlLDok.key_idea: Periodically forks parallel agent trajectories that retain the accumulated workspace but clear the conversation history, selecting the highest-scoring branch after a fixed horizon.
8UgphlLDok.evidence: Evaluated across 13 long-horizon research and engineering tasks with individual agent runs lasting up to 107 hours against single-run and best-of-N baselines.
8UgphlLDok.claimed_gains: Across 13 long-horizon research and engineering tasks, branch-reset outperformed single-run and best-of-N baselines by a relative improvement of 66.0% and 44.4%, respectively, on the min-max normalized average score under an equal compute budget.
8UgphlLDok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the empirical diagnosis and visualization of idea basins in multi-day autoresearch runs and find the workspace-preserving context reset mechanism simple and practical.
8UgphlLDok.main_concern: Matching compute by total LLM token credits systematically favors context-reset branches because shorter contexts consume fewer input tokens per step, allowing more actions and submissions than unreset baselines.

pnBfN0xQvi.one_liner: Derives within-client and unseen-client generalization bounds for client-level differentially private federated learning via hierarchical distributional stability.
pnBfN0xQvi.problem: Generalization in client-level differentially private federated learning is poorly understood across the distinct levels of local within-client samples and unseen clients.
pnBfN0xQvi.method: The authors develop a hierarchical distributional-stability framework decomposing generalization error into sample-replacement (within-client) and client-replacement (unseen-client) stability using total variation (TV) distance and KL divergence. They combine these bounds with optimization error analysis to characterize population excess risk under client heterogeneity, learning-rate decay, and privacy noise.
pnBfN0xQvi.key_idea: Decomposes DP-FL generalization into sample- and client-replacement distributional stability using TV distance and KL divergence to isolate local dataset size and client heterogeneity.
pnBfN0xQvi.evidence: Supported by theoretical TV and KL stability bounds, excess-risk derivations, and empirical validation across multiple federated learning datasets.
pnBfN0xQvi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the decomposition of DP-FL generalization into within-client and unseen-client bounds and the KL-based insight showing horizon independence when squared learning rates sum to a finite value.
pnBfN0xQvi.main_concern: The theoretical bounds rely on a globally bounded loss assumption that is violated by the cross-entropy loss used in the experiments, and decaying learning rates for horizon-independent generalization conflict with the optimization cost term.

vbeAwar80N.one_liner: Splits a fixed action-token budget into sparse long-horizon reference tokens and dense near-term execution tokens denoised jointly.
vbeAwar80N.problem: Action-chunking robot policies predict a long sequence of future controls but execute only a short prefix before replanning, wasting token capacity on unexecuted dense predictions.
vbeAwar80N.method: LeapBot-JAC reorganizes a fixed action-token budget within a single shared action expert into two parallel chains: sparse future-control reference tokens and dense near-term execution targets. Both chains are supervised by demonstrated controls and jointly denoised at aligned physical-time positions using directed attention that lets execution tokens read reference tokens without extra parameters or tokens.
vbeAwar80N.key_idea: Reallocates a fixed action-chunk budget into jointly denoised sparse future reference tokens and dense near-term execution tokens linked by directed reference-to-execution attention.
vbeAwar80N.evidence: Evaluated by integrating JAC into FastWAM and LeapBot-WA across LIBERO, zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin, and two real-world manipulation tasks.
vbeAwar80N.claimed_gains: On LIBERO, JAC reaches 98.3% success with FastWAM and LeapBot-WA, up from 97.0% and 97.3%; on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, success rates improve from 53.5% to 70.4% and from 73.1% to 77.3%, respectively.
vbeAwar80N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the parameter-free, zero-overhead reallocation of the fixed action-token budget into sparse references and dense execution targets, noting strong gains on LIBERO-Plus.
vbeAwar80N.main_concern: Ablations modify target allocation, temporal horizon, positional encoding, directed attention, and loss weighting simultaneously under a single training seed, making it difficult to isolate the effect of the sparse reference chain, and gains on RoboTwin are minimal.

znVa5R4aSI.one_liner: Proves test-risk improvement guarantees for inserting a new residual block into a trained post-normalized residual network.
znVa5R4aSI.problem: The theoretical mechanism explaining why increasing model depth improves test risk in normalized residual networks remains incomplete.
znVa5R4aSI.method: The authors analyze depth expansion by inserting a new residual block at an intermediate layer of a trained post-normalized residual network and decomposing the effect into representational gain, optimization gain, and generalization transfer. Under a first-order descent condition near zero initialization and post-normalization norm control, they derive an auxiliary jumpboard model with lower population risk and establish norm-based Rademacher complexity bounds yielding two test-risk guarantees.
znVa5R4aSI.key_idea: Combines a first-order descent condition at zero-output block insertion with norm-based Rademacher complexity bounds to prove test-risk reduction under residual depth expansion.
znVa5R4aSI.evidence: Supported by theoretical population-risk and train/test-level risk bounds along with experiments on CIFAR and a 32-layer LLaMA-style model on C4.
znVa5R4aSI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition of depth scaling into representational, optimization, and generalization components clearly structured and addressing an important theoretical question.
znVa5R4aSI.main_concern: The theory assumes a first-order descent condition and analyzes inserting a block into a frozen network without specifying a concrete training algorithm, creating a gap with end-to-end training and offering limited insight into why such descent directions exist.

HDvKU3cLbA.one_liner: Benchmarks longitudinal self-evolution of LLM agents across 120 sequential financial workflow cases with paired state-reset controls.
HDvKU3cLbA.problem: Benchmarks composed of independent tasks cannot evaluate whether an LLM agent accumulates procedural experience across recurring professional workflows over time.
HDvKU3cLbA.method: FinEvo-Bench organizes 120 open-ended financial tasks across 20 business scenes in six financial domains, where each scene has six distinct cases sharing a professional workflow and an expert-authored quality and compliance rubric. It evaluates self-evolving agent scaffolds on interleaved task streams using a Claude Opus 4.6 rubric judge and compares evolving runs against paired state-reset controls.
HDvKU3cLbA.key_idea: Evaluates self-evolving agent scaffolds on interleaved streams of six-case financial workflow scenes against paired state-reset controls using expert quality and compliance rubrics.
HDvKU3cLbA.evidence: Evaluated four self-evolving agent scaffolds with Qwen3.7-Max across 120 tasks in 20 financial scenes over three shuffled streams scored by a Claude Code rubric judge backed by Claude Opus 4.6.
HDvKU3cLbA.claimed_gains: Evolving runs score 9.33–19.37 points higher and trigger 0.12–0.44 fewer compliance issues per task than their paired state-reset controls.
HDvKU3cLbA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the longitudinal multi-case workflow design with paired state-reset controls and expert financial rubrics provides a realistic and well-curated test of experience reuse.
HDvKU3cLbA.main_concern: All experiments rely on a single backbone model (Qwen3.7-Max) across 120 finance tasks, and the shared scene-level rubric and external judge feedback may reward procedural comprehensiveness rather than case-specific judgment.

lwhVTweouW.one_liner: Routes agent decisions between compressed memory and raw-evidence recovery using a learned sufficiency scorer and unit-level conformal risk control.
lwhVTweouW.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents that always trust compressed memory risk acting on insufficient evidence, whereas always recovering raw history wastes tokens and treating correlated steps as independent invalidates risk calibration.
lwhVTweouW.method: ReCoverMem trains a memory-sufficiency scorer to rank agent decisions and applies unit-level conformal risk control calibrated over independent episode or source units rather than correlated individual steps. Given a target false-safe risk budget alpha, it selectively routes high-sufficiency decisions to Trust compressed memory and falls back to Recover raw evidence otherwise.
lwhVTweouW.key_idea: Calibrates a learned memory-sufficiency threshold at the episode/source unit level via conformal risk control to bound false-safe memory reliance.
lwhVTweouW.evidence: Evaluated across three long-horizon agent workloads (including NarrativeXL, ALFWorld, and Retail) and four downstream LLM backbones.
lwhVTweouW.claimed_gains: Across three workloads and four backbones, always trusting memory yields 45–72% false-safe risk, whereas at alpha=0.10 ReCoverMem routes 10–22% of decisions to Trust with lower false-safe risk in all 12 configurations and saves 8.5–13.6% of executed-branch tokens on NarrativeXL (3.9% at alpha=0.05).
lwhVTweouW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous statistical treatment of episode-level dependence in conformal calibration and the careful experimental controls including negative results.
lwhVTweouW.main_concern: The learned sufficiency scorer shows statistically significant coverage gains over random scoring with conformal risk control in only 3 of 12 configurations (and none on NarrativeXL), while the controlled proxy risk label does not reliably translate to final task completion.

Ixqm6k0cVW.one_liner: Quantizes World Action Models to 4 bits while protecting action-sensitive channel subspaces identified via an Action Observability Gramian.
Ixqm6k0cVW.problem: Standard post-training quantization methods degrade the continuous action precision of iterative diffusion-based World Action Models.
Ixqm6k0cVW.method: Q-WAM introduces the Action Observability Gramian (AOG) to measure how rounding errors in each weighted combination of a layer's input channels propagate through all denoising steps to perturb the final robot action. Using Action-Subspace Protection (ASP), it retains the most action-sensitive channel combinations in a low-rank 16-bit branch within the most action-critical experts while quantizing the remaining weights and activations to 4 bits.
Ixqm6k0cVW.key_idea: Computes the Action Observability Gramian across all diffusion denoising steps to isolate and protect top action-sensitive input subspaces in a 16-bit branch during 4-bit quantization.
Ixqm6k0cVW.evidence: Evaluated on three World Action Models (including Fast-WAM) in simulation on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark and on real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
Ixqm6k0cVW.claimed_gains: On the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, Q-WAM reaches 89.6–93.0% average success rate, within 1.1 percentage points of full precision.
Ixqm6k0cVW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that measuring quantization sensitivity with respect to final action perturbation across the denoising trajectory is well-motivated for robot control and validated on multiple WAMs and real hardware.
Ixqm6k0cVW.main_concern: Ablations introduce the 16-bit ASP branch without matching the high-precision bit budget against simpler subspace selection baselines, and end-to-end system latency and the heavy 130,000-step backpropagation calibration cost are not fully reported.

Aw9cUzSLWU.one_liner: Constructs and mechanistically analyzes a one-layer Transformer that detects invalid graph path transitions and emits an abort token.
Aw9cUzSLWU.problem: How Transformers internally detect invalid reasoning transitions during planning and how error recognition interacts with model width and attention circuits remain poorly understood.
Aw9cUzSLWU.method: Following a graph path-finding abstraction of planning on a directed acyclic graph with node set V, the authors train a Transformer to output a special abort token after any invalid edge transition. They prove that a one-layer ReLU Transformer of feed-forward width O(|V|) is sufficient and near-optimal in the worst case, while exact single-head QK thresholding requires linear head dimension, and analyze how abort supervision shapes attention and FFN logits in trained models.
Aw9cUzSLWU.key_idea: Trains a path-finding Transformer to emit an abort token upon non-edge transitions and characterizes the O(|V|) FFN width bounds and previous-node QK-to-FFN detection circuit.
Aw9cUzSLWU.evidence: Supported by constructive upper and lower expressivity bounds on DAGs, mechanistic circuit analysis across 5 seeds, and rejection-sampling experiments including a 0.6B model on Blocksworld.
Aw9cUzSLWU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical expressivity bounds and controlled mechanistic isolation of local transition checking versus next-node planning rigorous and clearly presented.
Aw9cUzSLWU.main_concern: The model memorizes a fixed graph's edge table without testing generalization to unseen edges or non-edges, and the bilinear QK attention circuit may already compute non-adjacency while the FFN merely thresholds attended previous-node content.

1yd42Deiyw.one_liner: Selects reasoning-critical context chunks via submodular information gain while condensing remaining chunks into query-guided latent vectors.
1yd42Deiyw.problem: Query-centric context compression retains only chunks with high surface semantic similarity to the question, discarding intermediate logical bridging evidence needed for multi-step reasoning.
1yd42Deiyw.method: CCoR (Context Compression for Reasoning) formulates chunk selection as a submodular maximization problem capturing reasoning sufficiency and necessity rather than direct query similarity. It retains full token representations for high-importance chunks while pooling redundant chunks into query-guided latent summary vectors, trained jointly with supervised alignment and reasoning-preservation reinforcement learning.
1yd42Deiyw.key_idea: Maximizes a submodular reasoning-information objective to select critical chunks kept at full resolution while compressing remaining chunks into query-pooled latent vectors.
1yd42Deiyw.evidence: Evaluated on multi-hop and single-hop QA benchmarks (NaturalQuestions, 2WikiMQA, and HotpotQA) across LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B at multiple compression ratios.
1yd42Deiyw.claimed_gains: At 8x compression, average F1 exceeds RAM by 9.23 points on LLaMA-3.1-8B and 6.13 points on Qwen3-8B.
1yd42Deiyw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing multi-step reasoning utility from surface query similarity is well-motivated for multi-hop QA and yields clear F1 improvements over baselines.
1yd42Deiyw.main_concern: The hybrid architecture keeping full hidden states for selected chunks and query-pooled vectors for others is identical to RAM's operator and drives most of the ablation gain, while evaluated context lengths average only 1K–3K tokens.

bDTyJPXGhI.one_liner: Defends against multi-turn LLM jailbreaks by maintaining an evolving user intent profile and asking targeted verification probes when requests are ambiguous.
bDTyJPXGhI.problem: Passive multi-turn safety filters classify only what the user reveals, forcing a trade-off between over-refusing benign requests and assisting multi-turn jailbreaks that disguise malicious intent across turns.
bDTyJPXGhI.method: Active Intention Verification (AIV) tracks an evolving user intent profile across dialogue turns and triggers targeted clarification, credential, or trap probes whenever a sensitive request is ambiguous under benign versus malicious hypotheses. By forcing the user to commit to a verifiable benign frame before deciding to assist or refuse, AIV constrains subsequent adversarial escalation.
bDTyJPXGhI.key_idea: Interactively issues targeted verification probes when multi-turn intent is ambiguous to separate benign users from attackers before granting assistance.
bDTyJPXGhI.evidence: Evaluated across four multi-turn jailbreak attacks (including Intention Deception and adaptive protocol-aware attackers) and six open- and closed-source LLMs, plus benign over-refusal benchmarks.
bDTyJPXGhI.claimed_gains: Across four multi-turn attacks and six models, AIV achieves defense success rates of 0.83–0.98 with 2–5% over-refusal, defending 83–90% of intention deception attempts on open-source models (where passive baselines defend <22%) and 0.78–0.94 against protocol-aware attackers.
bDTyJPXGhI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting multi-turn jailbreak defense from passive classification to active probing is well-motivated and achieves high defense success with low over-refusal across multiple models.
bDTyJPXGhI.main_concern: The paper lacks fine-grained ablations and qualitative analyses of the three individual probe types (clarification, credential, trap), omits modern reasoning models and ActorAttack, and does not fully separate genuine intent verification from response narrowing.

aqyvExE4ST.one_liner: Co-evolves agent harnesses and mutated infeasible execution environments so tool-using LLM agents learn when to abstain.
aqyvExE4ST.problem: Tool-using LLM agents struggle to recognize when a task is infeasible, and optimizing prompts or harnesses on a fixed task set fails to generalize to unseen failure modes.
aqyvExE4ST.method: HERA automatically constructs verifiable pairs of feasible and infeasible tasks by applying controlled environment mutations that render solvable tasks unsolvable. It then runs a co-evolution loop where agent failures on previous tasks drive both harness adaptation and the generation of new mutated environments targeting discovered weaknesses.
aqyvExE4ST.key_idea: Mutates executable environments to create verified feasible/infeasible task pairs and co-evolves the agent harness against adversarially generated environment failure modes.
aqyvExE4ST.evidence: Evaluated on HERA-Bench (60 held-out task pairs) using GPT-5.6-Luna for co-evolution and testing zero-shot transfer of the evolved harness across 19 LLMs.
aqyvExE4ST.claimed_gains: On held-out evaluation tasks, an evolved harness from HERA improves abstention accuracy from 61.7% to 83.3% while maintaining feasible task performance, and transfers across 19 other LLMs with a 15.3 percentage point average gain in abstention accuracy.
aqyvExE4ST.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the paired feasible/infeasible environment-mutation design and the practical problem of teaching tool-using agents to abstain without over-abstaining.
aqyvExE4ST.main_concern: HERA-Bench is small (60 pairs) and evaluated with a single rollout without confidence intervals, training and test tasks come from the same mutation pipeline, and HERA lags a failure-driven task-generation baseline on the primary Pair metric (70.0% vs 73.3%).

dxmuNmCiVN.one_liner: Mitigates OOD reasoning-strategy collapse in RLVR by co-training non-bijective equation-solving tasks with bijective inversion tasks.
dxmuNmCiVN.problem: Models trained with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can master structured step-by-step derivation in-distribution yet collapse to brute-force enumeration under out-of-distribution shifts.
dxmuNmCiVN.method: The authors design a controllable string-equation inversion testbed f(x)=y with executable verifiers to track whether an LLM uses structured derivation or brute-force enumeration across easy-to-hard OOD shifts. They show that co-training non-bijective inversion tasks with bijective (unique-solution) inversion tasks stabilizes step-by-step derivation and prevents OOD strategy collapse.
dxmuNmCiVN.key_idea: Co-trains RLVR models on bijective unique-solution inversion tasks alongside non-bijective tasks to preserve step-by-step derivation under OOD complexity shifts.
dxmuNmCiVN.evidence: Evaluated on a controllable string-equation inversion benchmark across three training seeds, multiple OOD shifts (including Length Change), and diversity controls.
dxmuNmCiVN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean, executable string-inversion testbed that makes reasoning strategy shifts observable and reliably demonstrates across multiple seeds that bijective co-training prevents OOD collapse.
dxmuNmCiVN.main_concern: The evaluation rubric folds repetition loops (LOOP) into brute-force enumeration (ENUM), potentially conflating execution failure with strategy switching, while the theoretical policy-gradient analysis does not rigorously prove why singleton solution sets increase token-level information gain.

ySQajKziJR.one_liner: Scales diffusion-generated synthetic data for knowledge distillation and drops all synthetic samples midway through student training.
ySQajKziJR.problem: Standard knowledge distillation is limited by the finite size of the real training dataset, preventing small student classifiers from matching large cross-architecture teachers.
ySQajKziJR.method: The authors augment knowledge distillation with up to 1M synthetic images generated by a fine-tuned SDXL diffusion model and train the student to mimic the teacher on the combined pool. Midway through training, they drop all synthetic data and continue distillation on real data alone (SynDrop), cutting training cost roughly in half while improving final accuracy.
ySQajKziJR.key_idea: Augments knowledge distillation with a large fine-tuned diffusion synthetic image pool and drops all synthetic samples midway through training to finish on real data.
ySQajKziJR.evidence: Evaluated on five fine-grained visual classification benchmarks (including Aircraft, Cars, and Flowers102) and one semantic segmentation setting using a ViT-L teacher (307M) and ResNet-18 student (11M).
ySQajKziJR.claimed_gains: A ResNet-18 (11M parameters) trained on 1M SDXL-generated images matches or exceeds a ViT-L teacher (307M parameters), while dropping synthetic data midway roughly halves student training cost and improves performance.
ySQajKziJR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the pipeline clear and practical, noting impressive results where a ResNet-18 student matches or surpasses a ViT-L teacher while benefiting from dropping synthetic data midway.
ySQajKziJR.main_concern: Scaling the synthetic dataset size under fixed epochs drastically increases the total number of gradient updates (from ~1k–2.6k to ~780k), confounding synthetic data scale with training duration in the absence of update-matched real-data augmentation baselines.

CYxmQV30gg.one_liner: A latent Universal Horizon Model jointly shapes behavior-model representations and supplies model-based updates for high-discount zero-shot reinforcement learning.
CYxmQV30gg.problem: Behavior foundation models struggle with long-horizon tasks, while separate horizon-model planning adds inference cost and training complexity.
CYxmQV30gg.method: A latent-predictive Universal Horizon Model is trained jointly with a latent-predictive behavior foundation model as an auxiliary representation objective. Its latent predictions also support model-based updates to stabilize training at high discount factors.
CYxmQV30gg.key_idea: Jointly learn latent horizon predictions and behavior representations, then use predicted future latents in model-based training updates.
CYxmQV30gg.evidence: Compatibility analysis relates the auxiliary objective to TD-JEPA, and AntMaze experiments use matched baselines and multi-seed high-discount training comparisons.
CYxmQV30gg.claimed_gains: Model-based updates enable stable latent-predictive behavior-model training at discounts as high as gamma=0.999.
CYxmQV30gg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value joint horizon-model training and the substantial stability improvement relative to matched high-discount baselines.
CYxmQV30gg.main_concern: Theoretical guarantees do not directly validate replacing true future-state samples with approximate latent point predictions inside nonlinear model-based updates.

hyTorr2WXN.one_liner: FidKV weights token attention inversely by retained query coverage to balance KV-cache eviction across queries.
hyTorr2WXN.problem: Selecting cached tokens by aggregate attention can preserve high total attention while leaving individual queries poorly covered.
hyTorr2WXN.method: The framework relates attention conditioning after token retention to KL divergence and derives an objective maximizing geometric-mean query coverage. FidKV estimates retained mass online and prioritizes attention from queries with lower coverage without training or calibration.
hyTorr2WXN.key_idea: Maximize geometric-mean retained attention mass, giving larger marginal token scores to poorly covered queries.
hyTorr2WXN.evidence: Theoretical ranking bounds and experiments on LongBench and RULER across three language-model families examine coverage imbalance and matched weighting controls.
hyTorr2WXN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the coverage objective and derived weighting rule principled, interpretable, and well motivated.
hyTorr2WXN.main_concern: Matched ablations do not establish that the central fidelity-weighting term causes the reported task-performance gains.

LRD2eaJN3r.one_liner: Recency Forcing biases attention by temporal distance and denoising step to reduce dependence on evicted video context.
LRD2eaJN3r.problem: Long autoregressive video generation faces poorly understood temporal dependencies and mismatches between training context and inference-time KV eviction.
LRD2eaJN3r.method: A perturbation-based positional response measures context-frame influence across temporal distance and denoising steps. Recency Forcing applies a timestep-dependent temporal attention bias, with Biased Attention Reparameterization implementing the bias through a FlashAttention-compatible reformulation.
LRD2eaJN3r.key_idea: Attenuate attention to distant frames with denoising-step-dependent biases based on measured temporal sensitivity.
LRD2eaJN3r.evidence: Reviews describe positional-response measurements, comparisons with context truncation and alternative bias families, frame-wise evaluations, and a human preference study.
LRD2eaJN3r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the temporal-dependency diagnostic and simple attention intervention for long video generation.
LRD2eaJN3r.main_concern: The evaluation does not sufficiently isolate the benefit of response-guided timestep dependence from generic recency bias and retraining.

gD9g3rE93K.one_liner: Clean-latent video features support anatomically constrained hand tracking and separate contact-force estimation.
gD9g3rE93K.problem: Frame-based hand trackers lack motion and interaction priors and usually omit physical cues needed for robot learning.
gD9g3rE93K.method: RLHND turns Cosmos 3 into a deterministic clip-level feature extractor, predicting anatomical hand poses with optional shared shape conditioning. A separate tactile stream learns contact and force with the pose stream frozen, using LBS-based feature spreading for vertex features.
gD9g3rE93K.key_idea: Reuse clean-latent video diffusion features for constrained pose estimation and a separate tactile stream predicting surface contact and force.
gD9g3rE93K.evidence: Monocular egocentric-video evaluations and demonstrations examine hand pose, contact, and force estimation, including a cached-shape configuration.
gD9g3rE93K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of recovering both hand pose and tactile information from human videos for robot learning.
gD9g3rE93K.main_concern: The evaluations do not sufficiently separate gains from Cosmos 3 pretraining and the proposed tracking and tactile components.

0PO2ZkgbFL.one_liner: Calibrated cosine compression and wavelet routing reduce KV storage and selectively access compressed attention states.
0PO2ZkgbFL.problem: Growing KV caches strain memory, while token eviction and model fine-tuning limit joint reductions in storage and attention computation.
0PO2ZkgbFL.method: WaveKV uses query-independent attention calibration to guide adaptive DCT compression by position and layer. Attention-guided DWT hierarchical routing selectively accesses the compressed cache without directly evicting tokens.
0PO2ZkgbFL.key_idea: Compress KV states with calibrated DCT budgets and use wavelet-based hierarchical routing to select compressed regions during attention.
0PO2ZkgbFL.evidence: Experiments across LLaMA-3.1-8B, Phi3-medium-128k, and Qwen3-8B include LongBench, RULER, compression-routing ablations, and system-level memory and throughput measurements.
0PO2ZkgbFL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate jointly addressing cache storage and attention access, with practical system measurements and component ablations.
0PO2ZkgbFL.main_concern: Modified or weak baseline implementations undermine the reported quality advantages over existing compression methods.

IQS8ezcGsX.one_liner: Evidence-aware semantic matching evaluates complete, temporally grounded annotations of egocentric workflows.
IQS8ezcGsX.problem: Existing benchmarks do not adequately test complete workflow recovery together with limits on unsupported annotation claims.
IQS8ezcGsX.method: EgoEasy defines a query-free workflow schema and separates content recovery from evidential reliability. Prediction-side canonicalization, evidence-aware adjudication, and capacity-constrained matching support workflow, proposition, and reliability assessments.
IQS8ezcGsX.key_idea: Canonicalize predicted workflow claims, adjudicate their evidence, and match them under capacity constraints to assess coverage and reliability.
IQS8ezcGsX.evidence: Seven video-language baselines undergo evaluation on 472 videos totaling 38.15 hours and 2,891 episodes across 10 environmental and 13 workflow families.
IQS8ezcGsX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating complete workflow annotations and their evidential reliability beyond selected questions or segments.
IQS8ezcGsX.main_concern: Different input budgets and annotation procedures confound comparisons of the baseline models' capabilities.

fb5u1aer8v.one_liner: Latent trajectory optimization projects generated video plans onto action-conditioned world-model dynamics.
fb5u1aer8v.problem: Video-generated plans can violate temporal and physical constraints, preventing their execution as actions.
fb5u1aer8v.method: GVP-WM generates a video from initial and goal observations, then jointly optimizes latent states and actions under a pretrained world model. Video-guided latent collocation preserves semantic alignment while enforcing dynamical feasibility.
fb5u1aer8v.key_idea: Jointly optimize latent states and actions under world-model dynamics while aligning the trajectory with generated video guidance.
fb5u1aer8v.evidence: Experiments examine out-of-distribution long-horizon planning and 3D robotic manipulation, including Push-T and same-planner video-guidance ablations.
fb5u1aer8v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the formulation of grounding video plans through dynamics-constrained world-model optimization useful.
fb5u1aer8v.main_concern: Zero-shot video guidance can hurt the same planner, so experiments do not establish that it causes the reported planning gains.

T1w8LuehrA.one_liner: Training-time attention concentration counteracts diffuse global attention in hybrid models before sparsification.
T1w8LuehrA.problem: Diffuse global attention in hybrid models leaves little attention mass recoverable under a fixed sparse budget.
T1w8LuehrA.method: The paper studies attention entropy and retained mass in hybrid models, then applies an architecture-aware concentration prior during pretraining. It examines prior strength, learned QK gains, and trained sparse indexers.
T1w8LuehrA.key_idea: Scale attention concentration during pretraining to reduce entropy and preserve more mass when global attention is sparsified.
T1w8LuehrA.evidence: Controlled Full, SWA-hybrid, and GDN-hybrid pretraining comparisons include entropy, retained-mass, retrieval, and 16K/64K RULER measurements.
T1w8LuehrA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the hybrid-specific sparsification analysis and controlled pretraining evidence connecting entropy with retained attention mass.
T1w8LuehrA.main_concern: Limited architectural and compute controls leave the attribution of the entropy gap specifically to hybridization uncertain.

vb8eZeehZv.one_liner: Progressively enabling multimodal memory stages tests when visual information fills evidence gaps in agent decisions.
vb8eZeehZv.problem: Adding richer multimodal memory does not necessarily help agents, and the useful stages of integration remain unclear.
vb8eZeehZv.method: The study defines four cumulative memory configurations that add multimodal capabilities to construction, storage and retrieval, and utilization. Comparisons examine whether added information resolves evidence gaps or introduces distraction.
vb8eZeehZv.key_idea: Enable multimodal capabilities progressively across memory stages and compare performance to identify where added evidence changes decisions.
vb8eZeehZv.evidence: Long-horizon experiments span four memory-intensive domains, ten benchmarks, and four MLLM backbones, with repeated runs and alternative implementations.
vb8eZeehZv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the structured comparisons across memory stages and evidence that richer multimodal integration is not uniformly preferable.
vb8eZeehZv.main_concern: The cumulative hierarchy measures conditional transitions rather than isolating independent stage effects and their interactions.

e2gOeIaYLo.one_liner: Offline self-generated probes diagnose memory failures and guide learned graph repairs with reversible decay.
e2gOeIaYLo.problem: Reactive memory maintenance discovers retrieval weaknesses only after they have already harmed a user interaction.
e2gOeIaYLo.method: MemDream uses Dreamer, Analyst, and Consolidator agents to probe, diagnose, and repair memory during offline cycles. GRPO trains repair choices for lasting retrieval gains, while soft decay supports reversible forgetting.
e2gOeIaYLo.key_idea: Generate memory-grounded probes before user queries, diagnose retrieval failures, and apply learned graph repairs plus reversible retrieval-weight decay.
e2gOeIaYLo.evidence: LoCoMo and MemoryAgentBench experiments include GPT-4.1 and Llama-3.1-8B readers, component ablations, and repeated-maintenance analyses.
e2gOeIaYLo.claimed_gains: MemDream improves answer F1 by 4.5 points on LoCoMo and achieves a 9.1-point higher overall score on MAB over the strongest reactive-evolution baselines.
e2gOeIaYLo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value proactive memory testing and the clearly separated probing, diagnosis, and repair roles.
e2gOeIaYLo.main_concern: The comparisons and ablations do not isolate the added value of the dream cycle and three-agent design over simpler maintenance systems.

ZExlJYlSn6.one_liner: Top-1-relative logit gaps restrict watermark bias to plausible near-tie tokens for model fingerprint distillation.
ZExlJYlSn6.problem: Strong watermark teachers can degrade generation quality, while simply weakening their signals reduces fingerprint detectability.
ZExlJYlSn6.method: The paper re-evaluates watermark-teacher quality and exploits fingerprint verification's ability to aggregate signals across queries. Near-tie restriction places sparse watermark bias only on tokens close to the base model's top prediction.
ZExlJYlSn6.key_idea: Apply sparse watermark bias only to tokens whose logit gaps from the top prediction fall within a near-tie threshold.
ZExlJYlSn6.evidence: Experiments across Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3 models examine detection-quality trade-offs, matched-strength signal placement, and deployment changes including fine-tuning.
ZExlJYlSn6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the detectability-quality trade-off important and view near-tie teachers as a simple way to reduce generation distortion.
ZExlJYlSn6.main_concern: Tuning and detector choices complicate attribution of the reported detection-quality gains to near-tie signal placement.

W2QBENehgb.one_liner: Dense semantic correspondences condition a diffusion policy for few-shot robotic manipulation across objects.
W2QBENehgb.problem: In-context imitation policies struggle to transfer demonstrations to unseen objects and scenarios.
W2QBENehgb.method: MatchingPolicy separates demonstration-to-scene matching from action prediction and conditions a diffusion policy on dense semantic correspondences. Vision foundation models and a two-stage matching algorithm establish those correspondences.
W2QBENehgb.key_idea: Extract demonstration-to-scene semantic correspondences separately and feed them directly into the action-generating diffusion policy.
W2QBENehgb.evidence: Evaluations on RLBench and real-world manipulation tasks test transfer to unseen object instances and semantic categories.
W2QBENehgb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find explicit correspondence conditioning well motivated and the simulation and real-world results promising.
W2QBENehgb.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate correspondence conditioning from differences in architecture, supervision, and synthetic training data.

aod4gjWGp7.one_liner: Natural context-dependent tokens calibrate attention heads for single-pass selection of long-context pretraining documents.
aod4gjWGp7.problem: Prediction-based long-context data selectors are costly, while attention-based selectors can miss heads that track useful distant evidence.
aod4gjWGp7.method: SNAS uses prediction contrasts on a calibration corpus to locate context-dependent tokens and their distant evidence, then selects attention heads enriched over those intervals. It scores corpus documents in one forward pass using distant attention and retrieved-content signals.
aod4gjWGp7.key_idea: Calibrate attention heads against naturally occurring distant evidence, then reuse those heads for single-pass document scoring.
aod4gjWGp7.evidence: Experiments cover two scoring models and three data domains, with head-selection and scoring ablations and matched training budgets.
aod4gjWGp7.claimed_gains: With the Llama-3.1-8B scorer, SNAS reports 1.8× LongFilter's corpus-scoring throughput and 44% fewer GPU-hours, excluding calibration.
aod4gjWGp7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value calibrating on natural dependencies and reusing selected heads to reduce corpus-scoring cost while retaining downstream performance.
aod4gjWGp7.main_concern: The cost comparison excludes head calibration and does not establish total selection cost or the corpus size needed to recover calibration overhead.

keF1Doc7eY.one_liner: Uniform Fréchet aggregation replaces attention in an SPD-valued architecture for small-data brain decoding.
keF1Doc7eY.problem: The contribution of learned token weighting to SPD manifold models for noisy, limited-label brain recordings remains unclear.
keF1Doc7eY.method: SPD-MetaFormer uses uniformly weighted log-Euclidean Fréchet aggregation, geodesic residual updates, and spectral feedforward transformations to refine a summary token. It retains memory tokens for a learned weighted readout.
keF1Doc7eY.key_idea: Mix SPD tokens with a uniform log-Euclidean Fréchet mean and refine the summary through geodesic residual and spectral transformations.
keF1Doc7eY.evidence: Uniform-weight interventions on MAtt and GBWAtt, ten-seed attention diagnostics, EEG comparisons, and ABIDE evaluation support the analysis.
keF1Doc7eY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value investigating whether adaptive attention weights actually explain the performance of existing SPD models.
keF1Doc7eY.main_concern: Published rather than matched EEG baselines and multiple architectural changes make the marginal performance gains difficult to attribute.

QfT6pSuefe.one_liner: Hypergraph memory preserves re-openable multimodal evidence across context compaction while segment-level reinforcement learning trains the agent.
QfT6pSuefe.problem: Native multimodal agents exhaust context windows, lose evidence during compaction, and struggle with credit assignment across compacted segments.
QfT6pSuefe.method: OmniPlex-RL compacts context into segments and stores observations with calls that reopen their raw media in a hypergraph memory. Single-rollout RL treats each segment as a training sample with a per-modality moving batch baseline.
QfT6pSuefe.key_idea: Store observations with raw-media retrieval calls across context folds and assign reinforcement-learning updates separately to each segment.
QfT6pSuefe.evidence: Evaluation spans twelve text, multimodal, and omni-modal benchmarks, five held out of training, with memory and compaction ablations.
QfT6pSuefe.claimed_gains: OmniPlex-RL leads on all twelve benchmarks with 27.0 average F1, exceeding the strongest of eight baselines by 4.5 F1 points.
QfT6pSuefe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize context saturation and evidence loss as practical problems for native multimodal agents.
QfT6pSuefe.main_concern: Controlled baselines are insufficient to isolate the contributions of hypergraph memory, context compaction, and single-rollout RL.

bbgYeL02GH.one_liner: Flow reversal supplies supervision for condition-dependent Gaussian sources in temporal flow matching.
bbgYeL02GH.problem: Standard conditional flow matching conditions the vector field while retaining a fixed Gaussian source distribution.
bbgYeL02GH.method: CNP-Flow reverses observed targets through a pretrained flow model to supervise a conditional noise predictor that produces an isotropic Gaussian source. Its three-stage pipeline pretrains the flow model, trains the predictor, and fine-tunes the original backbone with learned sources.
bbgYeL02GH.key_idea: Reverse targets through a pretrained flow to supervise a condition-dependent source distribution, then fine-tune generation from that source.
bbgYeL02GH.evidence: Experiments evaluate video prediction, video interpolation, and 7-DoF Franka robot motion planning, including performance with fewer function evaluations.
bbgYeL02GH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find flow-reversal supervision a useful approach that integrates into existing flow-matching backbones without architectural changes.
bbgYeL02GH.main_concern: The theory does not explain why reversed sources improve generation when an ideal conditional flow should recover the original Gaussian source.

rGmv0X20Oj.one_liner: Fixed request-local reduction traces permit adaptive GPU tiling and shared KV loads during batch-invariant LLM inference.
rGmv0X20Oj.problem: Existing batch-invariant inference ties numerical reproducibility to fixed physical schedules that restrict concurrency and prefix-sharing optimizations.
rGmv0X20Oj.method: FlexBI separates request-local numerical contracts from physical scheduling. FlexTile changes GEMM output tiling without changing reduction traces, while FlexLoad shares identical physical KV page loads without changing each query's logical reduction.
rGmv0X20Oj.key_idea: Keep each request's arithmetic reduction trace fixed while adapting GEMM output tiles and sharing physical KV page loads.
rGmv0X20Oj.evidence: Online serving experiments use two models and two datasets in vLLM and SGLang, alongside operator ablations and bitwise checks.
rGmv0X20Oj.claimed_gains: FlexBI reports 25--33% higher output throughput and 16--32% lower P99 time to first token than same-engine batch-invariant inference in vLLM and SGLang.
rGmv0X20Oj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge promising online serving gains from restoring scheduling flexibility under batch-invariance constraints.
rGmv0X20Oj.main_concern: The end-to-end comparisons do not clearly attribute throughput and latency gains to FlexTile and FlexLoad rather than other system changes.

yI89gN70gL.one_liner: Unrolled fixed-point updates estimate absolute-value equation signs before conventional solvers compute high-accuracy solutions.
yI89gN70gL.problem: Absolute value equations are difficult to solve because their absolute-value operator induces nonsmooth, nonconvex, NP-hard structure.
yI89gN70gL.method: MFPI-Net unrolls modified fixed-point iteration using a learnable smooth absolute-value approximation and paired modules regularized for mutual-inverse consistency. A two-stage solver uses the network to estimate signs, then applies conventional solvers after eliminating the absolute-value operator.
yI89gN70gL.key_idea: Learn sign estimates through unrolled modified fixed-point updates, then remove the absolute-value operator and solve the resulting system conventionally.
yI89gN70gL.evidence: Approximation-error bounds, layerwise stability analysis, a continuous-time interpretation, and experiments on synthetic AVE instances support the approach.
yI89gN70gL.claimed_gains: The abstract reports approximately 3× faster high-accuracy AVE solving than MFPI.
yI89gN70gL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and appreciate its theoretical and empirical treatment of a meaningful numerical problem.
yI89gN70gL.main_concern: Narrow synthetic evaluation and incomplete comparisons with related neural methods and established solvers limit the performance claims.

gGEBCALh0h.one_liner: Diffusion reconstruction and auxiliary visual prediction train compact visual representations and their use by language models.
gGEBCALh0h.problem: Vision-language alignment can lose visual information and leave language models unable to use retained content, contributing to hallucinations.
gGEBCALh0h.method: VLSA first combines compressed high-resolution encoding with reconstruction through a pretrained text-to-image latent diffusion model. It then trains the language model with auxiliary codebook-index and pixel-value prediction objectives.
gGEBCALh0h.key_idea: Supervise compressed visual embeddings through diffusion reconstruction, then supervise language-model visual processing through codebook-index and pixel-value prediction.
gGEBCALh0h.evidence: Experiments span over 30 MLLM benchmarks and 9 architectures, with component ablations, computational-overhead analyses, and fixed-representation controls.
gGEBCALh0h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize practical benefits in retaining and using visual information, supported by extensive evaluation and component analyses.
gGEBCALh0h.main_concern: Component comparisons do not sufficiently specify matched conditions or isolate the contributions of the individual alignment objectives.

PonZdGNTzX.one_liner: Necessity and sufficiency interventions score representation segments for cross-domain feature selection and classifier retraining.
PonZdGNTzX.problem: Features stable across source domains need not drive reliable classification under distribution shift.
PonZdGNTzX.method: The method intervenes on representation segments to measure their necessity and sufficiency for prediction, converting these measurements into causal effectiveness scores. It selects high-scoring segments and retrains a classifier on their representation subspace.
PonZdGNTzX.key_idea: Pair necessity and sufficiency interventions on feature segments, rank their causal effectiveness scores, and train on the selected subspace.
PonZdGNTzX.evidence: The paper provides theoretical derivations and evaluations across multiple datasets and pretrained backbones, with PACS ablations.
PonZdGNTzX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find necessity-and-sufficiency evaluation an interesting way to distinguish predictive feature selection from observational cross-domain stability.
PonZdGNTzX.main_concern: The comparisons lack strong feature-selection baselines with matched selection budgets and may disadvantage methods designed for end-to-end training.

UCys6Fc21w.one_liner: Kalman-inspired measurement updates add scalable cross-variable interactions to a selective state space forecaster.
UCys6Fc21w.problem: Channel-independent forecasters ignore cross-variable dependencies, while channel-dependent models face overfitting and computational overhead.
UCys6Fc21w.method: Chameleon adapts GatedDeltaNet for temporal modeling and adds a Kalman-filter-inspired measurement update for data-dependent cross-variable interactions with linear variable scaling. It also introduces stochastic perturbations of reversible instance normalization to aid generalization.
UCys6Fc21w.key_idea: Separate temporal recurrence from a structured measurement-update module that calibrates states using data-dependent cross-variable information.
UCys6Fc21w.evidence: Experiments cover strongly dependent ODE and PEMS datasets and 28 standard benchmark settings, with a channel-independent ablation.
UCys6Fc21w.claimed_gains: The CI ablation and prior CD methods incur 61-178% higher MSE on average on ODE and PEMS, while Chameleon beats each baseline in MSE and MAE in at least 27 and 22 of 28 standard settings.
UCys6Fc21w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating temporal dynamics from scalable cross-variable updates through the connection between selective SSMs and Kalman filtering.
UCys6Fc21w.main_concern: Removing the entire measurement-update module does not isolate cross-variable interactions from generic low-rank or channel-wise correction.

sb9GorRAvU.one_liner: Family-aware genotype reconstruction measures genomic model leakage, while family-level differential privacy protects correlated relatives jointly.
sb9GorRAvU.problem: Familial correlations spread an individual's genomic information across relatives' records, creating risks beyond record-level privacy protection.
sb9GorRAvU.method: GenoFA exploits Mendelian inheritance for family-aware genotype reconstruction and subtracts ordinary imputation effects through imputation-corrected reconstruction risk. The paper treats each family as a client for differential privacy.
sb9GorRAvU.key_idea: Use relatives' inherited genotypes to reconstruct target variants, discount non-training imputation, and protect each family as one privacy unit.
sb9GorRAvU.evidence: Genomic language model experiments examine family-aware reconstruction and compare client-level with group-level differential privacy.
sb9GorRAvU.claimed_gains: At a privacy budget of 6.0, client-DP reportedly improves model utility by 22.9%, reducing RMSE from 0.35 for group-DP to 0.27.
sb9GorRAvU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that familial correlations create a relevant and practically motivated privacy question for genomic language models.
sb9GorRAvU.main_concern: Unmatched attack information and family-level privacy guarantees weaken the empirical comparisons supporting the claimed advantages.

KDCxPcu5Qt.one_liner: Off-policy LLM RL algorithm optimizing sequence-level optimal-advantage regression anchored to a lagged inference policy without importance sampling
KDCxPcu5Qt.problem: Distributed LLM reinforcement learning introduces severe policy lag and inference-training discrepancies that destabilize on-policy algorithms like PPO and GRPO or require brittle importance sampling.
KDCxPcu5Qt.method: Optimal Advantage-based Policy Optimization with Lagged Inference policy (OAPL) drops on-policy ratio clipping and importance sampling, instead optimizing a sequence-level optimal-advantage objective directly referenced to the lagged inference policy. This formulation trains on asynchronous rollouts without modifying the inference engine.
KDCxPcu5Qt.key_idea: Eliminate importance-sampling ratios by regressing sequence-level log-probability ratios relative to the lagged inference policy against optimal KL-regularized advantages on stale rollouts.
KDCxPcu5Qt.evidence: Evaluated on math reasoning benchmarks (using Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B against GRPO with importance sampling) and LiveCodeBench coding tasks (compared against DeepCoder) under policy lags exceeding 400 gradient steps.
KDCxPcu5Qt.claimed_gains: Matches DeepCoder on LiveCodeBench while using 3x fewer generations during training and remains effective with lags of more than 400 gradient steps.
KDCxPcu5Qt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling asynchronous policy lag without importance sampling is practically valuable and that OAPL trains stably under large rollout lags.
KDCxPcu5Qt.main_concern: OAPL closely inherits A*PO's objective without a controlled A*PO baseline to isolate off-policy gains, decouples KL parameters in practice against its own theory, and tests on narrow model setups.

4X9XyclRB2.one_liner: Hyperparameter-free LLM decoding that samples uniformly from the top-k token prefix minimizing KL divergence to the model distribution
4X9XyclRB2.problem: Applying temperature scaling before support truncation admits low-probability tail tokens that derail LLM generation at high temperatures and require per-model hyperparameter tuning.
4X9XyclRB2.method: Global KL* truncates the token distribution first and samples uniformly at infinite temperature over the top-k candidate set whose uniform distribution minimizes forward KL divergence from the model's original probabilities. Equivalently replacing the arithmetic mean in top-p with the geometric mean of kept probabilities, it executes via one sort and one scan with zero tuning parameters.
4X9XyclRB2.key_idea: Select the top-k token subset whose uniform distribution minimizes KL divergence to the raw next-token distribution, then draw uniformly from that subset without temperature tuning.
4X9XyclRB2.evidence: Evaluated in full-precision vLLM on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME-level reasoning, and creative writing across ten 2026 LLM checkpoints with up to 16 samples per prompt against developer-recommended and truncation baselines.
4X9XyclRB2.claimed_gains: Produces 10 significant gains and 0 significant losses in 60 comparisons against developer-recommended settings (up to 5.8 points on the smallest checkpoint), stays within 0.7 points of greedy decoding on eight checkpoints, and keeps 58.5% on AIME-level problems where temperature-first top-p scores 1% at temperature 3 and 0.2% at temperature 1.6.
4X9XyclRB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean, tuning-free mathematical rule proving the optimal uniform support is a top-k set and the careful, pre-specified evaluation across ten checkpoints.
4X9XyclRB2.main_concern: Empirical results mainly show statistical non-inferiority under wide multiple-testing intervals rather than consistent gains, with tuned baselines outperforming KL* on pass@8 and P-less winning on several models.

zJMIAeQ4kT.one_liner: Lightweight camouflaged object detector combining cross-layer foreground-background prototype competition with evidence-guided hierarchical feature reconstruction
zJMIAeQ4kT.problem: Dimension compression and simplified feature interactions in lightweight camouflaged object detection networks weaken the subtle semantic and structural cues needed to separate camouflaged foregrounds from similar backgrounds.
zJMIAeQ4kT.method: DMRNet introduces Discriminative Evidence Mining (DEM), which extracts cross-layer feature discrepancies using foreground-background prototype competition and background interference gating. A Discriminative Evidence Reconstruction (DER) stage then uses this mined evidence to modulate deep semantic representations and shallow structural details.
zJMIAeQ4kT.key_idea: Mine cross-layer foreground-background prototype discrepancies while gating background distractions, then inject that evidence to reconstruct both deep semantic and shallow structural features.
zJMIAeQ4kT.evidence: Evaluated on four camouflaged object detection benchmark datasets against lightweight and standard COD baselines alongside module ablations and parameter and compute comparisons.
zJMIAeQ4kT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, targets a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off in lightweight camouflaged object detection, and shows competitive benchmark and qualitative results.
zJMIAeQ4kT.main_concern: The foreground-background prototype competition and distraction-suppression modules closely resemble prior mechanisms in PANet, PFNet, and standard spatial attention, and ablations do not cleanly isolate their specific contribution.

d6HH2Irwch.one_liner: Proves exact and fixed-tolerance training of a scalar-projection single attention head on two-token sequences is NP-hard
d6HH2Irwch.problem: The worst-case computational complexity of fitting weights for the minimal nontrivial self-attention head on two-token sequences lacked a formal Blum-Rivest-style characterization.
d6HH2Irwch.method: The authors construct polynomial-time reductions from 1-in-3 SAT to the weight-existence problem for a single attention head with one-dimensional query, key, and value projections over n-dimensional two-token inputs. They analyze both softmax and hardmax attention under exact fit as well as fixed positive coordinatewise and mean-squared-error tolerances.
d6HH2Irwch.key_idea: Reduce 1-in-3 SAT to fitting scalar query, key, and value projections on two-token sequences to establish NP-hardness for softmax attention and NP-completeness for hardmax attention.
d6HH2Irwch.evidence: Supported by formal complexity-theoretic proofs and polynomial-time reductions from 1-in-3 SAT for exact and tolerance-bounded fitting.
d6HH2Irwch.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and agree that the hardness proofs for minimal two-token attention heads are mathematically sound.
d6HH2Irwch.main_concern: The paper overlooks closely related recent ICLR NP-hardness results for single-head softmax attention, and worst-case hardness on scalar two-token heads is viewed as unsurprising with limited practical relevance.

2mJcO7qMO2.one_liner: Detects stalled multi-agent LLM interaction tails and truncates GAE optimization to a shared prefix boundary to preserve credit
2mJcO7qMO2.problem: Unproductive late rounds in multi-agent LLM collaboration generate negative temporal-difference residuals that propagate backward and invert credit for earlier useful coordination.
2mJcO7qMO2.method: Phantom-Control monitors observable collaborative progress across shared-memory rounds to detect persistent stagnation and places a common system-level optimization boundary across agents. Policy gradient updates and Generalized Advantage Estimation are restricted to the retained prefix before the boundary, preventing stalled tails from corrupting prefix advantages.
2mJcO7qMO2.key_idea: Detect persistent low progress in multi-round shared-memory interactions and truncate trajectory-level advantage estimation at a shared prefix boundary before unproductive tails invert early-action credit.
2mJcO7qMO2.evidence: Supported by theoretical GAE prefix-tail decomposition and false-trigger bounds, plus experiments with random-matched truncation controls across five multi-agent active-reasoning tasks.
2mJcO7qMO2.claimed_gains: Achieves late-stage reward gains reaching 35–50% and reduces mean total generated response length by 20–35% in representative regimes across five multi-agent active-reasoning tasks.
2mJcO7qMO2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value connecting unproductive multi-agent chatter to GAE advantage inversion and including random-matched controls that verify targeted boundary placement.
2mJcO7qMO2.main_concern: The theoretical propositions and tail-truncation detector closely mirror the prior single-agent T3 framework without sufficient differentiation, and guarantees at the ideal boundary do not cover the practical detector.

uFh1lX7xJk.one_liner: One-step consistency distillation for joint video-action models using separate noise-scaling parameterizations for action and video streams
uFh1lX7xJk.problem: Applying uniform consistency step-distillation to joint video-action diffusion models collapses manipulation success because standard consistency parameterizations yield vanishing learning signal at low noise where precise actions are refined.
uFh1lX7xJk.method: Flash-WAM distills multi-step world-action diffusion models into single-step generators using modality-specific consistency functions. It retains the standard consistency parameterization for high-dimensional video latents while assigning the action stream a parameterization whose learning signal scales linearly with the noise level.
uFh1lX7xJk.key_idea: Decouple consistency distillation across modalities by pairing standard video consistency with a linearly noise-scaled action consistency function that preserves gradient signal near zero noise.
uFh1lX7xJk.evidence: Evaluated on two world-action model architectures (LingBot-VA and Motus) across two manipulation simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks against multi-step teachers and distillation baselines.
uFh1lX7xJk.claimed_gains: Reduces inference to a single denoising step per modality and cuts per-chunk latency on LingBot-VA from 8.1 s to 347 ms on an NVIDIA L40S GPU.
uFh1lX7xJk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Flash-WAM addresses a real latency bottleneck in world-action models with a simple modification that achieves large speedups across two architectures.
uFh1lX7xJk.main_concern: The action consistency function closely resembles standard flow-matching clean-sample prediction, direct gradient measurements and loss-reweighting controls are missing, and real-robot evaluation is small-scale.

bSMYqzbdST.one_liner: Dual-space music-to-dance generator combining contact-aware 3D joint-coordinate diffusion with music-conditioned invertible inverse kinematics for SMPL rotations
bSMYqzbdST.problem: Directly predicting joint rotations in audio-driven 3D dance generation accumulates errors along the kinematic chain, causing foot skating, ground penetration, and unstable support.
bSMYqzbdST.method: PhysIKDance first uses a coordinate-space diffusion model to generate root translation, 3D joint positions, axial twist, and foot-interaction states under losses that penalize planted-foot drift and ground penetration while allowing intentional sliding. A music-conditioned two-stage invertible inverse-kinematics module then recovers joint swing angles and fuses them with predicted twist under cross-space consistency losses to output SMPL rotations.
bSMYqzbdST.key_idea: Generate physically constrained 3D joint positions, axial twist, and foot-contact states via diffusion first, then recover SMPL joint rotations through a music-conditioned invertible inverse-kinematics network.
bSMYqzbdST.evidence: Evaluated on the AIST++ and FineDance 3D music-to-dance benchmarks with motion-quality, foot-ground contact metrics, and component ablations.
bSMYqzbdST.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating 3D joint-coordinate generation from inverse-kinematics rotation recovery is an intuitive way to reduce distal foot-skating errors on AIST++ and FineDance.
bSMYqzbdST.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the dual-space design against direct rotation generation with forward-kinematics contact losses, key IK components adapt NIKI and EDGE, and demos show upper-arm twist artifacts.

IaDWNAgIx1.one_liner: Parameter-free pre-ViT visual token pruner that drops pixel-redundant image patches via 2D predictive coding before vision encoding
IaDWNAgIx1.problem: High-resolution document and GUI inputs generate tens of thousands of visual patches—many of which are pixel-level duplicates—causing heavy latency inside the Vision Transformer encoder before post-ViT token pruners can act.
IaDWNAgIx1.method: PixelPrune applies parameter-free 2D predictive coding directly in pixel space to prune exact or near-duplicate merge-block patches prior to the ViT while retaining original spatial coordinates. It operates training-free on document and GUI QA tasks and uses lightweight self-distillation from full-token model outputs when coordinate-sensitive GUI grounding requires adaptation.
IaDWNAgIx1.key_idea: Measure 2D predictive-coding residuals in raw pixel space to discard redundant patch blocks before the ViT encoder while preserving original positional coordinates.
IaDWNAgIx1.evidence: Evaluated across three VLM architectures and three model scales on seven document understanding benchmarks, GUI question answering, and GUI grounding under training-free, self-distilled, and from-scratch training setups.
IaDWNAgIx1.claimed_gains: Stays within 0.9 points of full-token accuracy on average across document benchmarks without training while pruning redundant patches across benchmarks where 29–78% of patches are pixel-level duplicates.
IaDWNAgIx1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pruning redundant patches before the ViT yields genuine end-to-end speedups across the vision encoder and LLM and is thoroughly evaluated across scales and tasks.
IaDWNAgIx1.main_concern: Dropping pixel-similar neighbor patches closely resembles prior methods like ShowUI and RLT, while comparisons omit both simple resolution downscaling and the pre-ViT baseline IndexPrune.

U02wywhh1J.one_liner: ASTRO uses local-neighbor support tubes to gate robust model learning and adaptive offline rollouts.
U02wywhh1J.problem: Offline model-based RL applies scalar trust and fixed rollout horizons despite direction-dependent data support and off-support dynamics drift.
U02wywhh1J.method: ASTRO builds anisotropic support tubes from local k-nearest-neighbor covariance and density, using them for robust value-aware model loss and learned state-dependent rollout horizons.
U02wywhh1J.key_idea: Local covariance and density define direction-specific support tubes shared by pessimistic model training and rollout control.
U02wywhh1J.evidence: Experiments cover 24 D4RL Adroit and MuJoCo datasets with five seeds, seven baselines, and ablations of covariance and value-aware loss.
U02wywhh1J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one local geometry for model learning and rollout control is coherent and supported by broad multi-seed benchmarks.
U02wywhh1J.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that theory assumes the Gaussian support it aims to justify and does not establish a link from local covariance to model error.

lBeUhj7uRJ.one_liner: Low-shot performance prediction guides target-specific sampling-circuit search for scalable sample-based quantum diagonalization.
lBeUhj7uRJ.problem: The scalability of sample-based quantum diagonalization depends on sampling circuits, but evaluating them under limited measurement budgets is difficult.
lBeUhj7uRJ.method: Qas²QD formulates ground-state estimation as family-level learning across related Hamiltonians and couples circuit search with low-shot subspace-quality feedback. It supports direct SQD evaluation and learned evaluation that reuses circuit-performance knowledge while guiding target-specific searches.
lBeUhj7uRJ.key_idea: A multimodal predictor reuses circuit-performance knowledge across related Hamiltonians to guide target-specific circuit search from low-shot subspace-quality feedback.
lBeUhj7uRJ.evidence: Evaluations on TFIM and XXZ benchmarks and quantum systems with up to 40 qubits test circuit ranking, measurement efficiency, and SQD scaling.
lBeUhj7uRJ.claimed_gains: The multimodal predictor preserves strong circuit-performance rankings using only 1% of the reference shots per circuit, and Qas²QD reduces mean SQD energy error by up to 90.6% over vanilla SQD.
lBeUhj7uRJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the family-level formulation and low-shot surrogate prediction address an important SQD circuit-design bottleneck with promising experimental support.
lBeUhj7uRJ.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the substantial offline training and labeling costs are adequately accounted for and amortized in the efficiency claims.

vFlneB9BVy.one_liner: Replacing textual pixel coordinates with drawn markers causally changes what spatial RLVR learns while holding other training variables fixed.
vFlneB9BVy.problem: Textual pixel coordinates can leak ground-plane depth information, allowing spatial models to learn distribution shortcuts instead of visual geometry.
vFlneB9BVy.method: The study holds the model, algorithm, reward, data volume, step count, and geometric sample distribution fixed while varying only whether questions reference pixels through coordinates or drawn markers. Paired training arms and decomposition controls test the resulting learned abilities and their transfer limits.
vFlneB9BVy.key_idea: Changing only the pixel-reference format from text coordinates to drawn markers intervenes on the depth shortcut available during spatial training.
vFlneB9BVy.evidence: Three paired seeds per arm, adversarial off-ground points, indoor transfer tests, and RLVR and supervised fine-tuning comparisons evaluate metric and ordinal spatial reasoning.
vFlneB9BVy.claimed_gains: The marker formulation more than doubles metric accuracy and lifts every depth bucket off zero, while the coordinate formulation leaves the hardest bucket at exactly zero under both RLVR and supervised fine-tuning.
vFlneB9BVy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the single-variable intervention, blind baselines, and adversarial controls provide a systematic investigation of coordinate-based spatial shortcuts.
vFlneB9BVy.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the training and evaluation reporting unclear, particularly the RLVR-versus-SFT labeling and differences between test-time input formats.

ZcTWawQepH.one_liner: Object-referenced operations and evolving stock states jointly guide machining-plan and toolpath generation from B-rep models.
ZcTWawQepH.problem: Correct machining-operation sequences do not guarantee correct material removal because every toolpath acts on stock changed by preceding cuts.
